3.4.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
śrutaṃ sumahadākhyānaṃ bhavatā parikīrttitam /
prajānāṃ manubhiḥ sārddhaṃ devānāmṛṣibhiḥ saha //
3.4.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
श्रुतं सुमहदाख्यानं भवता परिकीर्त्तितम् ।
प्रजानां मनुभिः सार्द्धं देवानामृषिभिः सह ॥
3.4.m: The sages said: / The very great narrative told by you has been heard, / concerning the subjects together with the Manus, and the gods along with the sages,

3.4.s:
pitṛgandharvabhūtānāṃ piśācoragarakṣasām /
daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca yakṣāṇāmeva pakṣiṇām //
3.4.d:
पितृगन्धर्वभूतानां पिशाचोरगरक्षसाम् ।
दैत्यानां दानवानां च यक्षाणामेव पक्षिणाम् ॥
3.4.m: of the ancestors, Gandharvas, spirits, Piśācas, serpents, and Rākṣasas, / of the Daityas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, and birds,

3.4.s:
atyadbhutāni karmāṇi vividhā dharmaniścayāḥ /
vicitrāśca kathāyogā janma cāgryamanuttamam //
3.4.d:
अत्यद्भुतानि कर्माणि विविधा धर्मनिश्चयाः ।
विचित्राश्च कथायोगा जन्म चाग्र्यमनुत्तमम् ॥
3.4.m: their exceedingly wondrous deeds, the various determinations of dharma, / their diverse narrative sequences, and their foremost, unsurpassed birth.

3.4.s:
tatkathyamānamasmākaṃ bhavatā ślakṣṇayā girā /
manaḥ karṇasukhaṃ saute prīṇātyamṛtasannibham //
3.4.d:
तत्कथ्यमानमस्माकं भवता श्लक्ष्णया गिरा ।
मनः कर्णसुखं सौते प्रीणात्यमृतसन्निभम् ॥
3.4.m: Being recounted to us by you in smooth speech, / pleasing to the mind and ears, O bard, it delights like nectar.

3.4.s:
evamārādhya te sūtaṃ satkṛtya ca maharṣayaḥ /
papracchuḥ sattriṇaḥ sarve punaḥ sargapravarttanam //
3.4.d:
एवमाराध्य ते सूतं सत्कृत्य च महर्षयः ।
पप्रच्छुः सत्त्रिणः सर्वे पुनः सर्गप्रवर्त्तनम् ॥
3.4.m: Having thus honored the bard and paid him respect, / all the sacrificers asked about the setting in motion of creation once again:

3.4.s:
kathaṃ suta mahāprājña punaḥ sargaḥ prapatsyate /
bandheṣu saṃpralīneṣu guṇasāmye tamomaye //
3.4.d:
कथं सुत महाप्राज्ञ पुनः सर्गः प्रपत्स्यते ।
बन्धेषु संप्रलीनेषु गुणसाम्ये तमोमये ॥
3.4.m: How, O bard of great wisdom, will creation take place again / when the bonds are completely dissolved in the equilibrium of the guṇas consisting of tamas,

3.4.s:
vikāreṣvavisṛṣṭeṣu hyavyakte cātmani sthite /
apravṛtte brahmaṇā tu sahasā yojyagaistadā //
3.4.d:
विकारेष्वविसृष्टेषु ह्यव्यक्ते चात्मनि स्थिते ।
अप्रवृत्ते ब्रह्मणा तु सहसा योज्यगैस्तदा ॥
3.4.m: when the evolutes are not yet emitted, abiding in the unmanifest Self, / and when, without commencement, [all things] are suddenly brought together by Brahman?

3.4.s:
kathaṃ prapatsyate sargastannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām /
evamuktastataḥ sūtastadāsau lomaharṣaṇaḥ //
3.4.d:
कथं प्रपत्स्यते सर्गस्तन्नः प्रब्रूहि पृच्छताम् ।
एवमुक्तस्ततः सूतस्तदासौ लोमहर्षणः ॥
3.4.m: How will creation proceed? Tell us that as we ask. / Being addressed thus, then, the bard Lomaharṣaṇa

3.4.s:
vyākhyātumupacakrāma punaḥ sargapravarttanam /
atra vo varttayiṣyāmi yathā sargaḥ prapatsyate //
3.4.d:
व्याख्यातुमुपचक्राम पुनः सर्गप्रवर्त्तनम् ।
अत्र वो वर्त्तयिष्यामि यथा सर्गः प्रपत्स्यते ॥
3.4.m: began to explain the setting in motion of creation once again: / Here I shall describe to you how creation proceeds.

3.4.s:
pūrvavatsa tu vijñeyaḥ samāsāttannibodhata /
dṛṣṭenaivānumeyaṃ ca tarkaṃ vakṣyāmi yuktitaḥ //
3.4.d:
पूर्ववत्स तु विज्ञेयः समासात्तन्निबोधत ।
दृष्टेनैवानुमेयं च तर्कं वक्ष्यामि युक्तितः ॥
3.4.m: It is to be understood as being just as before; comprehend it in brief. / And I shall state by reasoning the inference based strictly on what is observed.

3.4.s:
yasmādvāco nivarttante tvaprāpya manasā saha /
avyakta vatparokṣatvādgahanaṃ taddurāsadam //
3.4.d:
यस्माद्वाचो निवर्त्तन्ते त्वप्राप्य मनसा सह ।
अव्यक्त वत्परोक्षत्वाद्गहनं तद्दुरासदम् ॥
3.4.m: Since words turn back together with the mind without reaching it, / it is deep and difficult to approach, because like the unmanifest it is beyond perception.

3.4.s:
vikāraiḥ pratisaṃsṛṣṭo guṇaḥ sāmyena varttate /
pradhānaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ ca sādharmyeṇaiva tiṣṭhati //
3.4.d:
विकारैः प्रतिसंसृष्टो गुणः साम्येन वर्त्तते ।
प्रधानं पुरुषाणां च साधर्म्येणैव तिष्ठति ॥
3.4.m: When it has dissolved together with the evolutes, the guṇa exists in equilibrium; / and pradhāna remains solely by similarity of nature with the puruṣas.

3.4.s:
dharmādharmauṃ pralīyete hyavyakte prāṇināṃ sadā /
sattvamātrātmako dharmo guṇe sattve pratiṣṭhitaḥ //
3.4.d:
धर्माधर्मौं प्रलीयेते ह्यव्यक्ते प्राणिनां सदा ।
सत्त्वमात्रात्मको धर्मो गुणे सत्त्वे प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
3.4.m: Dharma and adharma of living beings are always dissolved in the unmanifest; / dharma, consisting solely of sattva, is established in the sattva guṇa;

3.4.s:
tamomātrātmako dharmo guṇe tamasi tiṣṭhati /
avibhāgena tāvetau guṇasāmye sthitāvubhau //
3.4.d:
तमोमात्रात्मको धर्मो गुणे तमसि तिष्ठति ।
अविभागेन तावेतौ गुणसाम्ये स्थितावुभौ ॥
3.4.m: adharma, consisting solely of tamas, rests in the tamas guṇa; / both of them abide undivided in the equilibrium of the guṇas.

3.4.s:
sarvaṃ kāryaṃ buddhipūrvaṃ pradhānasya prapatsyate /
buddhipūrvaṃ kṣetrajña adhiṣṭhāsyati tānguṇān //
3.4.d:
सर्वं कार्यं बुद्धिपूर्वं प्रधानस्य प्रपत्स्यते ।
बुद्धिपूर्वं क्षेत्रज्ञ अधिष्ठास्यति तान्गुणान् ॥
3.4.m: Every effect of pradhāna will proceed preceded by intellect; / preceded by intellect, the knower of the field will preside over those guṇas.

3.4.s:
evaṃ tānabhimānena prapatsyati punastadā /
yadā pravarttitavyaṃ tu kṣetrakṣetrajñayor dvayoḥ //
3.4.d:
एवं तानभिमानेन प्रपत्स्यति पुनस्तदा ।
यदा प्रवर्त्तितव्यं तु क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर् द्वयोः ॥
3.4.m: Thus, through self-conceit, it will then grasp them again / when the two, the field and the knower of the field, are to be set in motion.

3.4.s:
bhojyabhoktṛtvasaṃbandhāḥ prapatsyante ca tāvubhau /
tasmādakṣaramavyaktaṃ sāmye sthitvā guṇātmakam //
3.4.d:
भोज्यभोक्तृत्वसंबन्धाः प्रपत्स्यन्ते च तावुभौ ।
तस्मादक्षरमव्यक्तं साम्ये स्थित्वा गुणात्मकम् ॥
3.4.m: And the two will assume the relations of the consumed and the consumer; / therefore, the imperishable unmanifest, consisting of the guṇas, having remained in equilibrium,

3.4.s:
kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitaṃ tatra vaipamyaṃ bhajate tu tat /
tataḥ prapatsyate vyaktaṃ kṣetrakṣetrajñayordvayoḥ //
3.4.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञाधिष्ठितं तत्र वैपम्यं भजते तु तत् ।
ततः प्रपत्स्यते व्यक्तं क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्द्वयोः ॥
3.4.m: presided over by the knower of the field, undergoes disequilibrium there. / Then the manifest will proceed from the two, the field and the knower of the field.

3.4.s:
kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitaṃ sattvaṃ vikāraṃ janayiṣyati /
mahadādyaṃ viśeṣāntaṃ caturviṃśaguṇātmakam //
3.4.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञाधिष्ठितं सत्त्वं विकारं जनयिष्यति ।
महदाद्यं विशेषान्तं चतुर्विंशगुणात्मकम् ॥
3.4.m: Sattva presided over by the knower of the field will produce the evolute / consisting of the twenty-four qualities, beginning with the cosmic intellect and ending with the specific elements.

3.4.s:
kṣetrajñasya pradhānasya puruṣasya pravartsyataḥ /
ādidevaḥ pradhānasyānugrahāya prajakṣate //
3.4.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञस्य प्रधानस्य पुरुषस्य प्रवर्त्स्यतः ।
आदिदेवः प्रधानस्यानुग्रहाय प्रजक्षते ॥
3.4.m: Of the knower of the field, of pradhāna, and of the puruṣa about to proceed, / the primordial god is proclaimed for the grace of pradhāna.

3.4.s:
anādyau varamutpādau ubhau sūkṣmau tu tau smṛtau /
anādisaṃyogayutau sarvaṃ kṣetrajñameva ca //
3.4.d:
अनाद्यौ वरमुत्पादौ उभौ सूक्ष्मौ तु तौ स्मृतौ ।
अनादिसंयोगयुतौ सर्वं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च ॥
3.4.m: Both are known to be beginningless, excellent in origin, and subtle, / endowed with a beginningless union, and all is indeed the knower of the field.

3.4.s:
abuddhipūrvakaṃ yuktamāśaktau tu varau tadā /
apratyayamamoghaṃ ca sthitāvudakamatsyavat //
3.4.d:
अबुद्धिपूर्वकं युक्तमाशक्तौ तु वरौ तदा ।
अप्रत्ययममोघं च स्थितावुदकमत्स्यवत् ॥
3.4.m: Unpreceded by intellect, conjoined, but then incapable [of creation alone], both excellent, / devoid of conscious cognition and unfailing, they remain like water and a fish.

3.4.s:
pravṛttapūrvauṃ tau pūrvaṃ punaḥ sarvaṃ prapatsyate /
ajñā guṇaiḥ pravarttante rajaḥsattvatamo 'bhidhaiḥ //
3.4.d:
प्रवृत्तपूर्वौं तौ पूर्वं पुनः सर्वं प्रपत्स्यते ।
अज्ञा गुणैः प्रवर्त्तन्ते रजःसत्त्वतमो ऽभिधैः ॥
3.4.m: The two having been active before, everything will proceed again as before. / The ignorant proceed by means of the guṇas named rajas, sattva, and tamas.

3.4.s:
pravṛttikāle rajasābhipanno mahattvabhūtādiviśeṣatāṃ ca /
viśeṣatāṃ cendriyatāṃ ca yāti guṇāvasānauṣadhibhirmanuṣyaḥ //
3.4.d:
प्रवृत्तिकाले रजसाभिपन्नो महत्त्वभूतादिविशेषतां च ।
विशेषतां चेन्द्रियतां च याति गुणावसानौषधिभिर्मनुष्यः ॥
3.4.m: At the time of activity, overcome by rajas, [the self] attains the state of cosmic intellect, the origin of the elements, and the specific elements, / and attains the condition of the specific elements and the sense faculties; at the end of the guṇas, man [arises] through the plants.

3.4.s:
satyābhidhyāyinastasya dhyāyinaḥ sannimittakam /
rajaḥ sattvatamovyaktā vidharmāṇaḥ parasparam //
3.4.d:
सत्याभिध्यायिनस्तस्य ध्यायिनः सन्निमित्तकम् ।
रजः सत्त्वतमोव्यक्ता विधर्माणः परस्परम् ॥
3.4.m: For him who meditates on truth, meditating with good cause, / rajas, sattva, and tamas become manifest, having mutually distinct properties.

3.4.s:
ādyantaṃ vai pravatsyante kṣetramajñāmvu sarvaśaḥ /
saṃsiddhakāryakaraṇā utpadyante 'bhimāninaḥ //
3.4.d:
आद्यन्तं वै प्रवत्स्यन्ते क्षेत्रमज्ञाम्वु सर्वशः ।
संसिद्धकार्यकरणा उत्पद्यन्ते ऽभिमानिनः ॥
3.4.m: They will enter the beginning and the end, the field and the ignorant in every way; / possessing accomplished bodies and organs, endowed with self-conceit, they are born.

3.4.s:
sarve sattvāḥ prapadyante hyavyaktātpūrvameva ca /
prāksṛtau ye tvasuvahāḥ sādhakāścāpyasādhakāḥ //
3.4.d:
सर्वे सत्त्वाः प्रपद्यन्ते ह्यव्यक्तात्पूर्वमेव च ।
प्राक्सृतौ ये त्वसुवहाः साधकाश्चाप्यसाधकाः ॥
3.4.m: Indeed, all beings proceed from the unmanifest just as before; / those who were bearers of life in the previous creation, both successful and unsuccessful,

3.4.s:
asaṃśāntāstu te sarve sthānaprakaraṇaiḥ saha /
kāryāṇi pratipatsyante utpatsyante punaḥ punaḥ //
3.4.d:
असंशान्तास्तु ते सर्वे स्थानप्रकरणैः सह ।
कार्याणि प्रतिपत्स्यन्ते उत्पत्स्यन्ते पुनः पुनः ॥
3.4.m: all of them, not having been entirely extinguished, along with the topics of their positions, / will undertake their tasks and will be born again and again.

3.4.s:
guṇamātrātmakāveva dharmādharmauṃ parasparam /
ārapsaṃte hi cānyonyaṃ vareṇānugraheṇa vā //
3.4.d:
गुणमात्रात्मकावेव धर्माधर्मौं परस्परम् ।
आरप्संते हि चान्योन्यं वरेणानुग्रहेण वा ॥
3.4.m: Consisting solely of the guṇas, dharma and adharma / will mutually act upon each other, either through excellence or grace.

3.4.s:
śarvastulyaprasṛṣṭyartha sargādau yāti vikriyām /
guṇāstaṃ pratidhīyante tasmāttattasya rocate //
3.4.d:
शर्वस्तुल्यप्रसृष्ट्यर्थ सर्गादौ याति विक्रियाम् ।
गुणास्तं प्रतिधीयन्ते तस्मात्तत्तस्य रोचते ॥
3.4.m: At the beginning of creation, Śarva undergoes transformation for the sake of equal creation; / the guṇas are directed toward him, therefore that is pleasing to him.

3.4.s:
guṇāste yāni karmāṇi prāksṛṣṭyāṃ pratipedire /
tānyeva pratipadyante sṛjyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ //
3.4.d:
गुणास्ते यानि कर्माणि प्राक्सृष्ट्यां प्रतिपेदिरे ।
तान्येव प्रतिपद्यन्ते सृज्यमानाः पुनः पुनः ॥
3.4.m: Whatever actions those guṇas undertook in the previous creation, / those very same ones they undertake as they are created again and again:

3.4.s:
hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukūre dharmādharmāvṛtānṛte /
tadbhāvitāḥ prapadyante tasmāttattasya rocate //
3.4.d:
हिंस्राहिंस्रे मृदुकूरे धर्माधर्मावृतानृते ।
तद्भाविताः प्रपद्यन्ते तस्मात्तत्तस्य रोचते ॥
3.4.m: harmful and harmless, gentle and cruel, dharma and adharma, true and false; / conditioned by those, they proceed; therefore that is pleasing to him.

3.4.s:
mahābhūteṣu nānātvamindriyārtheṣu mūrttiṣu /
viprayogaśca bhūtānāṃ guṇebhyaḥ saṃpravarttate //
3.4.d:
महाभूतेषु नानात्वमिन्द्रियार्थेषु मूर्त्तिषु ।
विप्रयोगश्च भूतानां गुणेभ्यः संप्रवर्त्तते ॥
3.4.m: Diversity among the gross elements, sense objects, and bodily forms, / and the separation of beings, proceeds from the guṇas.

3.4.s:
ityeṣa vo mayā khyātaḥ punaḥ sargaḥ samāsataḥ /
samāsādeva vakṣyāmi brahmaṇo 'tha samudbhavam //
3.4.d:
इत्येष वो मया ख्यातः पुनः सर्गः समासतः ।
समासादेव वक्ष्यामि ब्रह्मणो ऽथ समुद्भवम् ॥
3.4.m: Thus has creation again been related to you by me in brief; / now I shall speak in brief of the birth of Brahmā.

3.4.s:
avyaktātkāraṇāttasmānnityātsadasadātmakāt /
pradhānapuruṣābhyāṃ tu jāyate ca maheśvaraḥ //
3.4.d:
अव्यक्तात्कारणात्तस्मान्नित्यात्सदसदात्मकात् ।
प्रधानपुरुषाभ्यां तु जायते च महेश्वरः ॥
3.4.m: From that unmanifest cause, eternal, consisting of both existence and non-existence, / and from pradhāna and puruṣa, Maheśvara is born.

3.4.s:
sa punaḥ saṃbhāvayitā jāyate brahmasaṃjñitaḥ /
sṛjate sa punarlokānabhimāna guṇātmakān //
3.4.d:
स पुनः संभावयिता जायते ब्रह्मसंज्ञितः ।
सृजते स पुनर्लोकानभिमान गुणात्मकान् ॥
3.4.m: He, the producer, is born again under the name of Brahmā; / he creates the worlds again, consisting of self-conceit and the guṇas.

3.4.s:
ahaṅkārastu mahatastasmādbhūtāni cātmanaḥ /
yugapatsaṃpravarttante bhūtānyevendriyāṇi ca //
3.4.d:
अहङ्कारस्तु महतस्तस्माद्भूतानि चात्मनः ।
युगपत्संप्रवर्त्तन्ते भूतान्येवेन्द्रियाणि च ॥
3.4.m: Ego arises from the cosmic intellect, and from that [arise] the elements and the self; / simultaneously the elements and the sense faculties proceed.

3.4.s:
bhūtabhedāśca bhūtebhya iti sargaḥ pravarttate /
vistarāvayavasteṣāṃ yathāprajñaṃ yathāśrutam /
kīrttyato vo yathāpūrvaṃ tathaivāpyupadhāryatām //
3.4.d:
भूतभेदाश्च भूतेभ्य इति सर्गः प्रवर्त्तते ।
विस्तरावयवस्तेषां यथाप्रज्ञं यथाश्रुतम् ।
कीर्त्त्यतो वो यथापूर्वं तथैवाप्युपधार्यताम् ॥
3.4.m: And varieties of beings arise from the elements; thus creation proceeds. / Their detailed arrangement, according to understanding and according to tradition, / has been recited to you just as before; let it be comprehended in the same manner.

3.4.s:
etacchrutvā naimiṣeyā stadānīṃ lokotpattiṃ susthitiṃ cāpyayaṃ ca /
tasminsatre 'vabhṛthaṃ prāpya śuddhāḥ puṇyaṃ lokamṛṣayaḥ prāpnuvanti //
3.4.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा नैमिषेया स्तदानीं लोकोत्पत्तिं सुस्थितिं चाप्ययं च ।
तस्मिन्सत्रे ऽवभृथं प्राप्य शुद्धाः पुण्यं लोकमृषयः प्राप्नुवन्ति ॥
3.4.m: Having heard this at that time, concerning the origin of the world, its stable preservation, and its dissolution, / having attained the concluding bath at that sacrifice, purified, the sages, inhabitants of Naimiṣa, attain the holy world.

3.4.s:
yathā yūyaṃ vidhinā devātādīniṣṭvā caivāvabhṛthaṃ prāpya śuddhāḥ /
tyaktvā dehānāyuṣoṃ'te kṛtārthāḥ puṇyaṃ lokaṃ prāpya modadhvamevam //
3.4.d:
यथा यूयं विधिना देवातादीनिष्ट्वा चैवावभृथं प्राप्य शुद्धाः ।
त्यक्त्वा देहानायुषोंऽते कृतार्थाः पुण्यं लोकं प्राप्य मोदध्वमेवम् ॥
3.4.m: Just as you, having sacrificed according to rule to the deities and others, and having attained the concluding bath, purified, / having cast off your bodies at the end of life, fulfilled in purpose, rejoice upon reaching the holy world!

3.4.s:
ete te naimiṣeyā vai dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā ca vai tadā /
jagmuścāvabhṛthasnātāḥ svargaṃ sarve tu satriṇaḥ //
3.4.d:
एते ते नैमिषेया वै दृष्ट्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च वै तदा ।
जग्मुश्चावभृथस्नाताः स्वर्गं सर्वे तु सत्रिणः ॥
3.4.m: Indeed, those inhabitants of Naimiṣa, having seen and touched [all things] then, / and having bathed in the concluding bath, all the sacrificers went to heaven.

3.4.s:
viprāstathā yūyamapi iṣṭā bahuvidhairmakhaiḥ /
āyuṣoṃ'te tataḥ svargaṃ gantāraḥ stha dvijottamāḥ //
3.4.d:
विप्रास्तथा यूयमपि इष्टा बहुविधैर्मखैः ।
आयुषोंऽते ततः स्वर्गं गन्तारः स्थ द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
3.4.m: Likewise you also, O brāhmaṇas, having sacrificed with manifold sacrifices, / will go to heaven at the end of life, O best of the twice-born!

3.4.s:
prakriyā prathamaḥ pādaḥ kathāyāstu parigrahaḥ /
anuṣaṅga upoddhāta upasaṃhāra eva ca //
3.4.d:
प्रक्रिया प्रथमः पादः कथायास्तु परिग्रहः ।
अनुषङ्ग उपोद्धात उपसंहार एव च ॥
3.4.m: Prakriyā is the first pāda, the introduction to the narrative, / then Anuṣaṅga, Upoddhāta, and Upasaṃhāra.

3.4.s:
evameva catuḥpādaṃ purāṇaṃ lokasammatam /
uvāca bhāgavānsakṣādvāyulokahite rataḥ //
3.4.d:
एवमेव चतुःपादं पुराणं लोकसम्मतम् ।
उवाच भागवान्सक्षाद्वायुलोकहिते रतः ॥
3.4.m: Just thus did the Lord himself, Vāyu, devoted to the welfare of the world, / speak the Purāṇa in four pādas, approved by the world.

3.4.s:
naimiṣe satramā sādya munibhyo munisattama /
tatprasādaṃ ca saṃsiddhaṃ bhūtotpattilayānvitam //
3.4.d:
नैमिषे सत्रमा साद्य मुनिभ्यो मुनिसत्तम ।
तत्प्रसादं च संसिद्धं भूतोत्पत्तिलयान्वितम् ॥
3.4.m: Having arrived at the sacrificial session in Naimiṣa, O best of sages, [he proclaimed] to the sages / this accomplished [work], through his grace, endowed with the origination and dissolution of beings.

3.4.s:
prādhānikīmimāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ tathaiveśvarakāritām /
samyagviditvā medhāvī na mohamadhigacchati //
3.4.d:
प्राधानिकीमिमां सृष्टिं तथैवेश्वरकारिताम् ।
सम्यग्विदित्वा मेधावी न मोहमधिगच्छति ॥
3.4.m: Having correctly understood this creation arising from the primary material cause and likewise brought about by the Lord, / a wise man does not fall into delusion.

3.4.s:
idaṃ yo brāhmaṇo vidvānitihāsaṃ purātanam /
śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi tathādhyāpayate 'pi ca //
3.4.d:
इदं यो ब्राह्मणो विद्वानितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
शृणुयाच्छ्रावयेद्वापि तथाध्यापयते ऽपि च ॥
3.4.m: Whatever learned brāhmaṇa should hear, recite, / or even teach this ancient history,

3.4.s:
sthāneṣu sa mahendrasya modate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ /
brahmasāyujyago bhūtvā brahmaṇā saha modate //
3.4.d:
स्थानेषु स महेन्द्रस्य मोदते शाश्वतीः समाः ।
ब्रह्मसायुज्यगो भूत्वा ब्रह्मणा सह मोदते ॥
3.4.m: he rejoices in the abodes of Mahendra for eternal years; / having attained union with Brahman, he rejoices with Brahmā.

3.4.s:
teṣāṃ kīrtimatāṃ kīrtiṃ prajeśānāṃ mahātmanām /
prathayanpṛthivīśānāṃ brahmabhūyāya gacchati //
3.4.d:
तेषां कीर्तिमतां कीर्तिं प्रजेशानां महात्मनाम् ।
प्रथयन्पृथिवीशानां ब्रह्मभूयाय गच्छति ॥
3.4.m: Proclaiming the renown of those renowned lords of creatures, the great-souled lords of the earth, / he attains the state of Brahman.

3.4.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ puṇyaṃ vedaiśca saṃmitam /
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanenoktaṃ purāṇa brahmavādinā //
3.4.d:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं पुण्यं वेदैश्च संमितम् ।
कृष्णद्वैपायनेनोक्तं पुराण ब्रह्मवादिना ॥
3.4.m: Auspiocious, fame-bestowing, life-giving, meritorious, and equal to the Vedas / is the Purāṇa spoken by Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, who proclaims Brahman.

3.4.s:
manvantareśvarāṇāṃ ca yaḥ kīrtiṃ prathayedimām /
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca bhūridravimatejasām //
3.4.d:
मन्वन्तरेश्वराणां च यः कीर्तिं प्रथयेदिमाम् ।
देवतानामृषीणां च भूरिद्रविमतेजसाम् ॥
3.4.m: And whoever should proclaim this renown of the rulers of the manvantaras, / and of the gods and sages endowed with immense wealth and splendor,

3.4.s:
sa sarvairmucyate pāpaiḥ puṇyaṃ ca mahadāpnuyāt /
yaścedaṃ śrāvayedvidvānsadā parvaṇi parvaṇi //
3.4.d:
स सर्वैर्मुच्यते पापैः पुण्यं च महदाप्नुयात् ।
यश्चेदं श्रावयेद्विद्वान्सदा पर्वणि पर्वणि ॥
3.4.m: he is freed from all sins and shall obtain great merit. / And whatever wise person should always recite this on every junction of the moon,

3.4.s:
dhūtapāpmā jitasvargo brahmabhūyāya kalpate /
yaścedaṃ śrāvayecchrāddhe brāhmaṇān pādamantataḥ //
3.4.d:
धूतपाप्मा जितस्वर्गो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ।
यश्चेदं श्रावयेच्छ्राद्धे ब्राह्मणान् पादमन्ततः ॥
3.4.m: his sins shaken off and heaven won, he is fit for the state of Brahman. / And whatever person should recite this to brāhmaṇas during an ancestral rite, even a single quarter-verse,

3.4.s:
akṣeyaṃ sarvakāmīyaṃ pitṝṃstacchopatiṣṭhate /
yasmātpurā hyaṇantīdaṃ purāṇaṃ tena cocyate //
3.4.d:
अक्षेयं सर्वकामीयं पितॄंस्तच्छोपतिष्ठते ।
यस्मात्पुरा ह्यणन्तीदं पुराणं तेन चोच्यते ॥
3.4.m: it serves his ancestors as imperishable and fulfilling all desires. / Because in ancient times they recited this, it is therefore called 'Purāṇa'.

3.4.s:
niruktamasya yo veda sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
tathaiva triṣu varṇeṣu ye manuṣyā adhīyate //
3.4.d:
निरुक्तमस्य यो वेद सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ।
तथैव त्रिषु वर्णेषु ये मनुष्या अधीयते ॥
3.4.m: Whoever knows its etymology is liberated from all sins. / Likewise, whatever men among the three castes study it,

3.4.s:
itihāsamimaṃ śrutvā dharmāya vidadhe matim /
yāvantyasya śarīreṣu romakūpāni sarvaśaḥ //
3.4.d:
इतिहासमिमं श्रुत्वा धर्माय विदधे मतिम् ।
यावन्त्यस्य शरीरेषु रोमकूपानि सर्वशः ॥
3.4.m: having heard this history, direct their minds to righteousness. / As many hair-pores as there are all over his body,

3.4.s:
tāvatkoṭisahasrāṇi varṣāṇi divi modate /
brahmasāyujyago bhūtvā daivataiḥ saha modate //
3.4.d:
तावत्कोटिसहस्राणि वर्षाणि दिवि मोदते ।
ब्रह्मसायुज्यगो भूत्वा दैवतैः सह मोदते ॥
3.4.m: for so many thousands of crores of years he rejoices in heaven; / having attained union with Brahman, he rejoices with the gods.

3.4.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ ca yaśasvi ca /
brahmā dadau śāstramidaṃ purāṇaṃ mātariśvane //
3.4.d:
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं पवित्रं च यशस्वि च ।
ब्रह्मा ददौ शास्त्रमिदं पुराणं मातरिश्वने ॥
3.4.m: Destructive of all sins, meritorious, purifying, and glorious— / Brahmā gave this teaching, the Purāṇa, to Mātariśvan.

3.4.s:
tasmāccośanasā prāptaṃ tasmāccāpi bṛhaspatiḥ /
bṛhaspatistu provāca savitre tadanantaram //
3.4.d:
तस्माच्चोशनसा प्राप्तं तस्माच्चापि बृहस्पतिः ।
बृहस्पतिस्तु प्रोवाच सवित्रे तदनन्तरम् ॥
3.4.m: From him it was obtained by Uśanas, and from him Bṛhaspati; / Bṛhaspati, in turn, told it to Savitṛ next.

3.4.s:
savitā mṛtyave prāha mṛtyuścendrāya vai punaḥ /
indraścāpi vasiṣṭhāya so 'pi sārasvatāya ca //
3.4.d:
सविता मृत्यवे प्राह मृत्युश्चेन्द्राय वै पुनः ।
इन्द्रश्चापि वसिष्ठाय सो ऽपि सारस्वताय च ॥
3.4.m: Savitṛ told it to Mṛtyu, and Mṛtyu again to Indra; / and Indra to Vasiṣṭha, and he to Sārasvata.

3.4.s:
sārasvatastridhāmne 'tha tridhāmā ca śaradvate /
śaradvāṃstu triviṣṭāya soṃ'tarikṣāya dattavān //
3.4.d:
सारस्वतस्त्रिधाम्ने ऽथ त्रिधामा च शरद्वते ।
शरद्वांस्तु त्रिविष्टाय सोंऽतरिक्षाय दत्तवान् ॥
3.4.m: Sārasvata then [gave it] to Tridhāman, and Tridhāman to Śaradvant; / Śaradvant gave it to Triviṣṭa, and he to Antarikṣa.

3.4.s:
carṣiṇe cāntarikṣo vai so 'pi trayyāruṇāya ca /
trayyāruṇāddhanañjayaḥ sa vai prādātkṛtañjaye //
3.4.d:
चर्षिणे चान्तरिक्षो वै सो ऽपि त्रय्यारुणाय च ।
त्रय्यारुणाद्धनञ्जयः स वै प्रादात्कृतञ्जये ॥
3.4.m: Antarikṣa gave it to Carṣiṇi, and he to Trayyāruṇa; / from Trayyāruṇa [it went] to Dhanañjaya, and he gave it to Kṛtañjaya.

3.4.s:
kṛtañjayāttṛṇañjayo bharadvājāya so 'pyatha /
gautamāya bharadvājaḥ so 'pi niryyantare punaḥ //
3.4.d:
कृतञ्जयात्तृणञ्जयो भरद्वाजाय सो ऽप्यथ ।
गौतमाय भरद्वाजः सो ऽपि निर्य्यन्तरे पुनः ॥
3.4.m: From Kṛtañjaya [it went] to Tṛṇañjaya, and he then to Bharadvāja; / Bharadvāja to Gautama, and he again to Niryantara.

3.4.s:
niryyantarastu provāca tathā vājaśravāya vai /
sa dadau somaśuṣmāya sa cādāttṛṇabindave //
3.4.d:
निर्य्यन्तरस्तु प्रोवाच तथा वाजश्रवाय वै ।
स ददौ सोमशुष्माय स चादात्तृणबिन्दवे ॥
3.4.m: Niryantara told it likewise to Vājaśravas; / he gave it to Somaśuṣma, and he gave it to Tṛṇabindu.

3.4.s:
tṛṇabindustu dakṣāya dakṣaḥ provāca śaktaye /
śakteḥ parāśaraścāpi garbhasthaḥ śrutavānidam //
3.4.d:
तृणबिन्दुस्तु दक्षाय दक्षः प्रोवाच शक्तये ।
शक्तेः पराशरश्चापि गर्भस्थः श्रुतवानिदम् ॥
3.4.m: Tṛṇabindu [gave it] to Dakṣa, and Dakṣa told it to Śakti; / Parāśara, while still in the womb, heard this from Śakti.

3.4.s:
parāśarājjātukarṇyastasmāddvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ /
dvaipāyanā tpunaścāpi mayā prāptaṃ dvijottama //
3.4.d:
पराशराज्जातुकर्ण्यस्तस्माद्द्वैपायनः प्रभुः ।
द्वैपायना त्पुनश्चापि मया प्राप्तं द्विजोत्तम ॥
3.4.m: From Parāśara, Jātūkarṇya [received it], and from him the lord Dvaipāyana; / and from Dvaipāyana, in turn, it was obtained by me, O best of the twice-born.

3.4.s:
mayā caitatpunaḥ proktaṃ putrāyāmitabuddhaye /
ityeva vākyaṃ brahmādiguruṇāṃ samudātdṛtam //
3.4.d:
मया चैतत्पुनः प्रोक्तं पुत्रायामितबुद्धये ।
इत्येव वाक्यं ब्रह्मादिगुरुणां समुदात्दृतम् ॥
3.4.m: And by me this was spoken again to my son of boundless intellect. / Thus indeed is this teaching held high by the lineage of teachers beginning with Brahmā.

3.4.s:
namaskāryāśca guravaḥ prayatnena manīṣibhiḥ /
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvārthasādhakam //
3.4.d:
नमस्कार्याश्च गुरवः प्रयत्नेन मनीषिभिः ।
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं पुण्यं सर्वार्थसाधकम् ॥
3.4.m: And the teachers must be saluted with effort by wise men. / Auspicious, fame-bestowing, life-giving, meritorious, achieving all aims,

3.4.s:
pāpaghnaṃ niyamenedaṃ śrotavyaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ sadā /
nāśucau nāpi pāpāya nāpyasaṃvatsaroṣite //
3.4.d:
पापघ्नं नियमेनेदं श्रोतव्यं ब्राह्मणैः सदा ।
नाशुचौ नापि पापाय नाप्यसंवत्सरोषिते ॥
3.4.m: destroying sins, this should always be heard with restraint by brāhmaṇas. / Not to the impure, nor to the sinful, nor to one who has not dwelt [as a student] for a year,

3.4.s:
nāśraddadhāne 'viduṣe nāputrāya kathañcana /
nāhitāya pradātavyaṃ pavitramidamuttamam //
3.4.d:
नाश्रद्दधाने ऽविदुषे नापुत्राय कथञ्चन ।
नाहिताय प्रदातव्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् ॥
3.4.m: not to the faithless, to the unlearned, nor ever to one without a son, / nor to one who is ill-disposed should this supreme purifier be given.

3.4.s:
avyaktaṃ vai yasya yoniṃ vadanti vyaktaṃ dehaṃ kālametaṃ gatiṃ ca /
vahnirvaktraṃ candrasūryauṃ ca netrediśaḥ śrotre ghrāṇamāhuśca vāyum //
3.4.d:
अव्यक्तं वै यस्य योनिं वदन्ति व्यक्तं देहं कालमेतं गतिं च ।
वह्निर्वक्त्रं चन्द्रसूर्यौं च नेत्रेदिशः श्रोत्रे घ्राणमाहुश्च वायुम् ॥
3.4.m: Whose origin they call the unmanifest, whose manifest body is time, and this movement; / fire is his mouth, the moon and the sun are his two eyes, the cardinal directions his ears, and wind, they say, his breath;

3.4.s:
vāco vedā antarikṣaṃ śarīraṃ kṣitiḥ pādāstārakā romakūpāḥ /
sarvāṇi dyaurmastakāni tvatho vai vidyāścaivopaniṣadyasya puccham //
3.4.d:
वाचो वेदा अन्तरिक्षं शरीरं क्षितिः पादास्तारका रोमकूपाः ।
सर्वाणि द्यौर्मस्तकानि त्वथो वै विद्याश्चैवोपनिषद्यस्य पुच्छम् ॥
3.4.m: the Vedas are his words, the intermediate space his body, the earth his feet, the stars his hair-pores; / heaven all of his heads, the sciences and the Upaniṣad his tail;

3.4.s:
taṃ devadevaṃ jananaṃ janānāṃ yajñātmakaṃ satyalokapratiṣṭham /
varaṃ varāṇāṃ varadaṃ maheśvaraṃ brahmāṇamādiṃ prayato namasye //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte dvādaśasāharsyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ uttarabhāge caturthaṃ upasaṃhārapāde brahmāṇḍāvarttaṃ nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
3.4.d:
तं देवदेवं जननं जनानां यज्ञात्मकं सत्यलोकप्रतिष्ठम् ।
वरं वराणां वरदं महेश्वरं ब्रह्माणमादिं प्रयतो नमस्ये ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते द्वादशसाहर्स्यां संहितायां उत्तरभागे चतुर्थं उपसंहारपादे ब्रह्माण्डावर्त्तं नाम चतुर्थो ऽध्यायः
3.4.m:
to that God of gods, the progenitor of beings, whose essence is sacrifice, established in Satyaloka, / the best among the best, the giver of boons, the great lord, Brahmā the primeval, I bow with devotion.

Thus ends the fourth chapter, named 'The Evolution of the Cosmic Egg', in the fourth section, the Upasaṃhārapāda, in the latter half of the twelve-thousand-verse Saṃhitā spoken by Vāyu, in the holy Mahāpurāṇa, the Brahmāṇḍa.

3.5.s:
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ /
atha śrīlalitopākhyānaṃ prārabhyate /
caturbhuje candrakalāvataṃse kuconnate kuṅkumarāgaśoṇe /
puṇḍrekṣupāśāṅkuśapuṣpabāṇahaste namaste jagadekamātaḥ //
3.5.d:
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ।
अथ श्रीललितोपाख्यानं प्रारभ्यते ।
चतुर्भुजे चन्द्रकलावतंसे कुचोन्नते कुङ्कुमरागशोणे ।
पुण्ड्रेक्षुपाशाङ्कुशपुष्पबाणहस्ते नमस्ते जगदेकमातः ॥
3.5.m: Homage to holy Gaṇeśa. / Now the holy Lalitopākhyāna is begun. / Four-armed, crested with the crescent moon, with elevated breasts, red as the hue of saffron, / holding the sugarcane bow, noose, goad, and flower arrows in your hands: homage to you, sole Mother of the universe!

3.5.s:
astu naḥ śreyase nityaṃ vastu vāmāṅgasundaram /
yatastṛtīyo viduṣāṃ tṛtīyastu paraṃ mahaḥ //
3.5.d:
अस्तु नः श्रेयसे नित्यं वस्तु वामाङ्गसुन्दरम् ।
यतस्तृतीयो विदुषां तृतीयस्तु परं महः ॥
3.5.m: May that entity, beautiful in the left side of its body, eternally lead to our welfare, / from which arises the third [state] of the wise, while the third is the supreme splendor.

3.5.s:
agastyo nāma devarṣirvedavedāṅgapāragaḥ /
sarvasiddhāntasārajño brahmānandarasātmakaḥ //
3.5.d:
अगस्त्यो नाम देवर्षिर्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ।
सर्वसिद्धान्तसारज्ञो ब्रह्मानन्दरसात्मकः ॥
3.5.m: A divine sage named Agastya, who had crossed over the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences, / who knew the essence of all established truths, and whose self was the bliss of Brahman,

3.5.s:
cacārādbhutahetūni tīrthānyāyatanāni ca /
śailāraṇyāpagāmukhyānsarvāñjanapadānapi //
3.5.d:
चचाराद्भुतहेतूनि तीर्थान्यायतनानि च ।
शैलारण्यापगामुख्यान्सर्वाञ्जनपदानपि ॥
3.5.m: wandered to miraculous sacred places and shrines, / and through all realms, headed by mountains, forests, and rivers.

3.5.s:
teṣu teṣvakhilāñjantūnajñānatimirāvṛtān /
śiśnodaraparāndṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa tānprati //
3.5.d:
तेषु तेष्वखिलाञ्जन्तूनज्ञानतिमिरावृतान् ।
शिश्नोदरपरान्दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास तान्प्रति ॥
3.5.m: Seeing all beings in those various places enveloped in the darkness of ignorance / and devoted only to the genitals and belly, he reflected upon them.

3.5.s:
tasya cintayamānasya carato vasudhāmimām /
prāptamāsīnmahāpuṇyaṃ kāñcīnagaramuttamam //
3.5.d:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य चरतो वसुधामिमाम् ।
प्राप्तमासीन्महापुण्यं काञ्चीनगरमुत्तमम् ॥
3.5.m: As he was wandering over this earth, full of concern, / he reached the most sacred and excellent city of Kāñcī.

3.5.s:
tatra vāraṇaśailenadramekāmranilayaṃ śivam /
kāmākṣīṃ karidoṣadhnīmapūjayadathātmavān //
3.5.d:
तत्र वारणशैलेनद्रमेकाम्रनिलयं शिवम् ।
कामाक्षीं करिदोषध्नीमपूजयदथात्मवान् ॥
3.5.m: There, the self-controlled sage worshipped Śiva, whose dwelling is the Ekāmra tree, / upon the Vāraṇa mountain, and Kāmākṣī, who destroys sins committed by beings.

3.5.s:
lokahetordayārdrasya dhīmataścintano muhuḥ /
cirakālena tapasā toṣito 'bhūjjanārdanaḥ //
3.5.d:
लोकहेतोर्दयार्द्रस्य धीमतश्चिन्तनो मुहुः ।
चिरकालेन तपसा तोषितो ऽभूज्जनार्दनः ॥
3.5.m: For the sake of the world, Janārdana was gratified by the wise sage, / moist with compassion, who contemplated repeatedly, by means of his long-practiced asceticism.

3.5.s:
hayagrīvāṃ tanuṃ kṛtvā sākṣāccinmātravigrahām /
śaṅkhacakrākṣavalayapustakojjvalabāhukām //
3.5.d:
हयग्रीवां तनुं कृत्वा साक्षाच्चिन्मात्रविग्रहाम् ।
शङ्खचक्राक्षवलयपुस्तकोज्ज्वलबाहुकाम् ॥
3.5.m: Assuming the form of Hayagrīva, which is consciousness alone personified, / with arms resplendent with the conch, discus, rosary, and book,

3.5.s:
pūrayitrīṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ prabhayā dehajātayā /
prādurbabhūva purato muneramitatejasā //
3.5.d:
पूरयित्रीं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रभया देहजातया ।
प्रादुर्बभूव पुरतो मुनेरमिततेजसा ॥
3.5.m: filling the entire universe with the radiance born of his body, / he appeared before the sage with boundless splendor.

3.5.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvānandabharitaḥ praṇamya ca muhurmuhuḥ /
vinayāvanato bhūtvā santuṣṭāva jagatpatim //
3.5.d:
तं दृष्ट्वानन्दभरितः प्रणम्य च मुहुर्मुहुः ।
विनयावनतो भूत्वा सन्तुष्टाव जगत्पतिम् ॥
3.5.m: Seeing him, filled with bliss and bowing repeatedly, / bending low in modesty, he praised the Lord of the universe.

3.5.s:
athovāca jagannāthastuṣṭo 'smi tapasā tava /
varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te bhavitā bhūsurottamaḥ //
3.5.d:
अथोवाच जगन्नाथस्तुष्टो ऽस्मि तपसा तव ।
वरं वरय भद्रं ते भविता भूसुरोत्तमः ॥
3.5.m: Then the Lord of the universe said: "I am pleased with your asceticism; / choose a boon; welfare shall be unto you, O best of brāhmaṇas!"

3.5.s:
iti pṛṣṭo bhagavatā provāca munisattamaḥ /
yadi tuṣṭo 'si bhagavannime pāmarajantavaḥ //
3.5.d:
इति पृष्टो भगवता प्रोवाच मुनिसत्तमः ।
यदि तुष्टो ऽसि भगवन्निमे पामरजन्तवः ॥
3.5.m: Thus asked by the Blessed Lord, the best of sages said: / "If you are pleased, O Lord, by what means may these wretched beings

3.5.s:
kenopāyena muktāḥ syuretanme vaktumarhasi /
iti pṛṣṭo dvijenātha devadevo janārdanaḥ //
3.5.d:
केनोपायेन मुक्ताः स्युरेतन्मे वक्तुमर्हसि ।
इति पृष्टो द्विजेनाथ देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
3.5.m: be liberated? You should tell me this." / Thus asked by the twice-born, the God of gods, Janārdana, [replied]:

3.5.s:
eṣa eva purā praśnaḥ śivena carito mama /
ayameva kṛtaḥ praśno brahmaṇā tu tataḥ param //
3.5.d:
एष एव पुरा प्रश्नः शिवेन चरितो मम ।
अयमेव कृतः प्रश्नो ब्रह्मणा तु ततः परम् ॥
3.5.m: "This very question was addressed to me formerly by Śiva; / this very question was asked after that by Brahmā;

3.5.s: kṛto durvāsasā paścādbhavatā tu tataḥ param //
3.5.d: कृतो दुर्वाससा पश्चाद्भवता तु ततः परम् ॥
3.5.m: it was asked later by Durvāsas, and after that, by you."

3.5.s:
bhavadbhiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ gurubhūtairmahātmabhiḥ /
mamopadeśo lokeṣu prathito 'stu varo mama //
3.5.d:
भवद्भिः सर्वभूतानां गुरुभूतैर्महात्मभिः ।
ममोपदेशो लोकेषु प्रथितो ऽस्तु वरो मम ॥
3.5.m:
“Through you, who are great-souled gurus of all beings,
may my instruction become renowned in the worlds; this is my boon.

3.5.s:
ahamādirhi bhūtānāmādikartā svayaṃ prabhuḥ /
sṛṣṭisthitilayānāṃ tu sarveṣāmapi kārakaḥ //
3.5.d:
अहमादिर्हि भूतानामादिकर्ता स्वयं प्रभुः ।
सृष्टिस्थितिलयानां तु सर्वेषामपि कारकः ॥
3.5.m:
For I am the beginning of all beings, the primal creator, the Lord himself,
and indeed the maker of all creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

3.5.s: trimūrtistriguṇātīto guṇahīno guṇāśrayaḥ //
3.5.d: त्रिमूर्तिस्त्रिगुणातीतो गुणहीनो गुणाश्रयः ॥
3.5.m: Possessing three forms, beyond the three guṇas, devoid of guṇas, the refuge of guṇas,

3.5.s:
icchāvihāro bhūtātmā pradhānapuruṣātmakaḥ /
evaṃ bhūtasya me brahmaṃstrijagadrūpadhāriṇaḥ //
3.5.d:
इच्छाविहारो भूतात्मा प्रधानपुरुषात्मकः ।
एवं भूतस्य मे ब्रह्मंस्त्रिजगद्रूपधारिणः ॥
3.5.m:
sporting at will, the self of all beings, consisting of pradhāna and puruṣa.
Of me, who am thus, O Brahman, bearing the form of the threefold world,

3.5.s:
dvidhākṛtamabhūdrūpaṃ pradhāna puruṣātmakam /
mama pradhānaṃ yadrūpaṃ sarvalokaguṇātmakam //
3.5.d:
द्विधाकृतमभूद्रूपं प्रधान पुरुषात्मकम् ।
मम प्रधानं यद्रूपं सर्वलोकगुणात्मकम् ॥
3.5.m:
the form was divided in two, consisting of pradhāna and puruṣa.
My form that is pradhāna consists of the guṇas of all the worlds;

3.5.s:
aparaṃ yadguṇātītaṃ parātparataraṃ mahat /
evameva tayorjñātvā mucyate te ubhe kimu //
3.5.d:
अपरं यद्गुणातीतं परात्परतरं महत् ।
एवमेव तयोर्ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते ते उभे किमु ॥
3.5.m:
the other, which is beyond the guṇas, is higher than the highest, great.
Having known both of them in this way, is one released?

3.5.s:
tapobhiścirakālotthairyamaiśca niyamairapi /
tyāgairduṣkarmanāśānte muktirāśveva labhyate //
3.5.d:
तपोभिश्चिरकालोत्थैर्यमैश्च नियमैरपि ।
त्यागैर्दुष्कर्मनाशान्ते मुक्तिराश्वेव लभ्यते ॥
3.5.m:
By austerities practiced for a long time, and by yamas and niyamas,
and by renunciations, at the end of the destruction of bad karma, liberation is quickly attained.

3.5.s:
yadrūpaṃ yadguṇayutaṃ tadguṇyaikyena labhyate /
anyatsarvajagadrūpaṃ karmabhogaparākramam //
3.5.d:
यद्रूपं यद्गुणयुतं तद्गुण्यैक्येन लभ्यते ।
अन्यत्सर्वजगद्रूपं कर्मभोगपराक्रमम् ॥
3.5.m:
Whatever form is endowed with whatever guṇa is attained through oneness with that possessor of guṇas;
the other is the form of the entire universe, displaying the valor of karmic experiences.

3.5.s:
karmabhirlabhyate tacca tattyāgenāpi labhyate /
dustarastu tayostyāgaḥ sakalairapi tāpasa //
3.5.d:
कर्मभिर्लभ्यते तच्च तत्त्यागेनापि लभ्यते ।
दुस्तरस्तु तयोस्त्यागः सकलैरपि तापस ॥
3.5.m:
And that is attained through works, or it is attained even through the abandonment thereof;
but the abandonment of both is hard to traverse for everyone, O ascetic.

3.5.s: anapāyaṃ ca sugamaṃ sadasatkarmagocaram //
3.5.d: अनपायं च सुगमं सदसत्कर्मगोचरम् ॥
3.5.m: It is imperishable and easily accessible, the domain of good and bad karma.

3.5.s:
ātmasthena guṇenaiva satā cāpyasatāpivā /
ātmaikyenaiva yajjñānaṃ sarvasiddhigradāyakam //
3.5.d:
आत्मस्थेन गुणेनैव सता चाप्यसतापिवा ।
आत्मैक्येनैव यज्ज्ञानं सर्वसिद्धिग्रदायकम् ॥
3.5.m:
By the quality present within oneself, whether real or unreal,
knowledge solely through oneness with the Self grants all supernatural powers.

3.5.s:
varṇatrayavihīnānāṃ pāpiṣṭhānāṃ nṛṇāmapi /
yadrūpadhyānamātreṇa duṣkṛtaṃ sukṛtāyate //
3.5.d:
वर्णत्रयविहीनानां पापिष्ठानां नृणामपि ।
यद्रूपध्यानमात्रेण दुष्कृतं सुकृतायते ॥
3.5.m:
Even for men who are devoid of the three varṇas and most sinful,
by the mere meditation on her form, bad action turns into good action.

3.5.s:
yer'cayanti parāṃ śaktiṃ vidhināvidhināpi vā /
na te saṃsāriṇo nūnaṃ muktā eva na saṃśayaḥ //
3.5.d:
येर्ऽचयन्ति परां शक्तिं विधिनाविधिनापि वा ।
न ते संसारिणो नूनं मुक्ता एव न संशयः ॥
3.5.m:
Those who worship the supreme Śakti, whether according to rule or not according to rule,
are certainly not transmigrating beings; they are truly liberated, without doubt.

3.5.s:
śivo vā yāṃ samārādhya dhyānayogabalena ca /
īśvaraḥ sarvasiddhānāmarddhanārīśvaro 'bhavat //
3.5.d:
शिवो वा यां समाराध्य ध्यानयोगबलेन च ।
ईश्वरः सर्वसिद्धानामर्द्धनारीश्वरो ऽभवत् ॥
3.5.m:
Worshiping whom, by the power of meditation and yoga,
Śiva became the Lord of all accomplished ones, the Lord Who is Half Woman.

3.5.s:
anye 'bjapramukhā devāḥ siddhāstaddhyānavaibhavāt /
tasmādaśeṣalokānāṃ tripurārādhanaṃ vinā //
3.5.d:
अन्ये ऽब्जप्रमुखा देवाः सिद्धास्तद्ध्यानवैभवात् ।
तस्मादशेषलोकानां त्रिपुराराधनं विना ॥
3.5.m:
Other gods, beginning with the lotus-born [Brahmā], became accomplished through the majesty of meditation upon her;
therefore, for all worlds, without the worship of Tripurā,

3.5.s:
na sto bhogāpavargauṃ tu yaugapadyena kutracit /
tanmanāstadgataprāṇastadyājī tadgatehakaḥ //
3.5.d:
न स्तो भोगापवर्गौं तु यौगपद्येन कुत्रचित् ।
तन्मनास्तद्गतप्राणस्तद्याजी तद्गतेहकः ॥
3.5.m:
enjoyment and liberation do not exist anywhere simultaneously.
Fixing your mind on her, devoting your life-breath to her, sacrificing to her, directing your efforts to her,

3.5.s:
tādātmyenaiva karmāṇi kurvanmuktimavāpsyasi /
etadrahasyamākhyātaṃ sarveṣāṃ hitakāmyayā //
3.5.d:
तादात्म्येनैव कर्माणि कुर्वन्मुक्तिमवाप्स्यसि ।
एतद्रहस्यमाख्यातं सर्वेषां हितकाम्यया ॥
3.5.m:
performing actions through identity with her alone, you shall attain liberation.
This secret has been declared out of a desire for the welfare of all,

3.5.s:
santuṣṭenaiva tapasā bhavato munisattama /
devāśca munayaḥ siddhā mānuṣāśca tathāpare /
tvanmukhāṃbhojato 'vāpyasiddhiṃ yāntu parātparām //
3.5.d:
सन्तुष्टेनैव तपसा भवतो मुनिसत्तम ।
देवाश्च मुनयः सिद्धा मानुषाश्च तथापरे ।
त्वन्मुखांभोजतो ऽवाप्यसिद्धिं यान्तु परात्पराम् ॥
3.5.m:
being pleased with your austerity, O best of sages.
May the gods, sages, perfected ones, and likewise other human beings,
receiving it from your lotus mouth, attain the highest accomplished state!”

3.5.s:
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā hayagrīvasya śārṅgiṇaḥ /
praṇipatya punarvākyamuvāca madhusūdanam //
3.5.d:
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हयग्रीवस्य शार्ङ्गिणः ।
प्रणिपत्य पुनर्वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनम् ॥
3.5.m:
Having heard these words of Hayagrīva, the bow-bearing Śārṅgin,
[Agastya] bowed down and again addressed words to Madhusūdana:

3.5.s:
bhagavankīdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ bhavatā yatpuroditam /
kiṃvihāraṃ kiṃprabhāvametanme vaktumarhasi //
3.5.d:
भगवन्कीदृशं रूपं भवता यत्पुरोदितम् ।
किंविहारं किंप्रभावमेतन्मे वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
3.5.m:
“O Lord, what kind of form is that which was described by you earlier?
What is its sport? What is its power? You ought to tell me this.”

3.5.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
eṣoṃ'śabhūto devarṣe hayagrīvo mamāparaḥ /
śrotumicchasiyadyattvaṃ tatsarvaṃ vaktumarhati //
3.5.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
एषोंऽशभूतो देवर्षे हयग्रीवो ममापरः ।
श्रोतुमिच्छसियद्यत्त्वं तत्सर्वं वक्तुमर्हति ॥
3.5.m:
Hayagrīva said:
“This other Hayagrīva, O divine sage, is a portion of me.
Whatever you wish to hear, he is able to tell it all.”

3.5.s:
ityādiśya jagannātho hayagrīvaṃ tapodhanam /
purataḥ kumbhajātasya munerantaradhāddhariḥ //
3.5.d:
इत्यादिश्य जगन्नाथो हयग्रीवं तपोधनम् ।
पुरतः कुम्भजातस्य मुनेरन्तरधाद्धरिः ॥
3.5.m:
Having thus instructed the ascetic Hayagrīva
in front of the sage born from the pitcher, Hari disappeared.

3.5.s:
tatastu vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā tapodhanaḥ /
hayagrīveṇa muninā svāśramaṃ pratyapadyata //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne agastyayātrājanārdanāvirbhāvo nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.5.d:
ततस्तु विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा तपोधनः ।
हयग्रीवेण मुनिना स्वाश्रमं प्रत्यपद्यत ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने अगस्त्ययात्राजनार्दनाविर्भावो नाम पञ्चमो ऽध्यायः
3.5.m:
Then, filled with wonder, his hair standing on end, that ascetic
went to his hermitage along with the sage Hayagrīva.

Thus in the venerable Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa, in the latter section, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the Lalitopākhyāna, the fifth chapter, named ‘The Journey of Agastya and the Manifestation of Janārdana.’

3.6.s:
athopaveśya caivainamāsane paramādbhute /
hayānanamupāgatyāgastyo vākyaṃ samabravīt //
3.6.d:
अथोपवेश्य चैवैनमासने परमाद्भुते ।
हयाननमुपागत्यागस्त्यो वाक्यं समब्रवीत् ॥
3.6.m:
Then, having seated him on a supremely wondrous seat,
approaching the horse-faced one, Agastya spoke these words:

3.6.s:
bhagavansarvadharmajña sarvasiddhāntavittam /
lokābhyudayaheturhi darśanaṃ hi bhavādṛśām //
3.6.d:
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ सर्वसिद्धान्तवित्तम् ।
लोकाभ्युदयहेतुर्हि दर्शनं हि भवादृशाम् ॥
3.6.m:
“O Lord, knower of all dharmas, best among knowers of all doctrines,
the sight of those like you is indeed the cause of the world's elevation.

3.6.s:
āvirbhāvaṃ mahādevyāstasyā rūpāntarāṇi ca /
vihāraścaiva mukhyā ye tānno vistarato vada //
3.6.d:
आविर्भावं महादेव्यास्तस्या रूपान्तराणि च ।
विहारश्चैव मुख्या ये तान्नो विस्तरतो वद ॥
3.6.m:
The manifestation of the Great Goddess, and her other forms,
and those sports that are principal—tell us those in detail.”

3.6.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
anādirakhilādhārā sadasatkarmarūpiṇī /
dhyānaikadṛśyā dhyānāṅgī vidyāṅgī hṛdayāspadā //
3.6.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
अनादिरखिलाधारा सदसत्कर्मरूपिणी ।
ध्यानैकदृश्या ध्यानाङ्गी विद्याङ्गी हृदयास्पदा ॥
3.6.m:
Hayagrīva said:
“She is without beginning, the support of all, having the form of good and bad karma,
to be seen through meditation alone, whose limbs are meditation, whose limbs are knowledge, whose abode is the heart.

3.6.s: ātmaikyādvyaktimāyāti cirānuṣṭhānagauravāt //
3.6.d: आत्मैक्याद्व्यक्तिमायाति चिरानुष्ठानगौरवात् ॥
3.6.m: Through oneness with the Self, she comes to manifestation due to the dignity of long practice.

3.6.s:
ādau prādurabhūcchaktirbrahmaṇo dhyānayogataḥ /
prakṛtirnāma sā khyātā devānāmiṣṭasiddhidā //
3.6.d:
आदौ प्रादुरभूच्छक्तिर्ब्रह्मणो ध्यानयोगतः ।
प्रकृतिर्नाम सा ख्याता देवानामिष्टसिद्धिदा ॥
3.6.m:
In the beginning, Śakti manifested from the meditation and yoga of Brahmā;
she is known by the name Prakṛti, granting the desired accomplishment of the gods.

3.6.s:
dvitīyamudabhūdrūpaṃ pravṛtte 'mṛtamanthane /
śarvasaṃmohajanakamavāṅmanasagojaram //
3.6.d:
द्वितीयमुदभूद्रूपं प्रवृत्ते ऽमृतमन्थने ।
शर्वसंमोहजनकमवाङ्मनसगोजरम् ॥
3.6.m:
Her second form arose when the churning for nectar commenced,
producing delusion in Śarva, beyond the reach of speech and mind.

3.6.s:
yaddarśanādabhūdīśaḥ sarvajño 'pi vimohitaḥ /
visṛjya pārvatīṃ śīghrantayā ruddho 'tanodratam //
3.6.d:
यद्दर्शनादभूदीशः सर्वज्ञो ऽपि विमोहितः ।
विसृज्य पार्वतीं शीघ्रन्तया रुद्धो ऽतनोद्रतम् ॥
3.6.m:
By the sight of which the Lord, though omniscient, was utterly deluded;
abandoning Pārvatī, he quickly pursued her and engaged in union.

3.6.s: tasyāṃ vai janayāmāsa śāstāramasurārdanam //
3.6.d: तस्यां वै जनयामास शास्तारमसुरार्दनम् ॥
3.6.m: Upon her he indeed fathered Śāstṛ, the destroyer of the asuras.”

3.6.s:
agastya uvāca
kathaṃ vai sarvabhūteśo vaśī manmatha śāsanaḥ /
aho vimohito devyā janayāmāsa cātmajam //
3.6.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
कथं वै सर्वभूतेशो वशी मन्मथ शासनः ।
अहो विमोहितो देव्या जनयामास चात्मजम् ॥
3.6.m:
Agastya said:
“How indeed was the Lord of all beings, self-controlled, the punisher of Manmatha,
ah, deluded by the Goddess, and fathered a son?”

3.6.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
purāmarapurādhīśo vijayaśrīsamṛddhimān /
trailokyaṃ pālayāmāsa sadevāsuramānuṣam //
3.6.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
पुरामरपुराधीशो विजयश्रीसमृद्धिमान् ।
त्रैलोक्यं पालयामास सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥
3.6.m:
Hayagrīva said:
“Formerly, the lord of the city of the immortals, possessed of the prosperity of victory and fortune,
protected the three worlds together with gods, asuras, and humans.

3.6.s:
kailāsaśikharākāraṃ gajendramadhiruhya saḥ /
cacārākhilalokeṣu pūjyamāno 'khilairapi /
taṃ pramattaṃ viditvātha bhavānīpatikhyayaḥ //
3.6.d:
कैलासशिखराकारं गजेन्द्रमधिरुह्य सः ।
चचाराखिललोकेषु पूज्यमानो ऽखिलैरपि ।
तं प्रमत्तं विदित्वाथ भवानीपतिख्ययः ॥
3.6.m:
Having mounted the lord of elephants, which resembled the peak of Mount Kailāsa,
he roamed through all the worlds, being worshiped by all.
Knowing him to be intoxicated, the lord of Bhavānī,

3.6.s:
durvāsasamathāhūya prajighāya tadantikam /
khaṇḍājinadharo daṇḍīdhūridhūsaravigrahaḥ /
unmattarūpadhārī ca yayau vidyādharādhvanā //
3.6.d:
दुर्वाससमथाहूय प्रजिघाय तदन्तिकम् ।
खण्डाजिनधरो दण्डीधूरिधूसरविग्रहः ।
उन्मत्तरूपधारी च ययौ विद्याधराध्वना ॥
3.6.m:
having summoned Durvāsas, dispatched him to his presence.
Wearing a torn hide, holding a staff, his body grey with dust,
and wearing the appearance of a madman, he went by the path of the Vidyādharas.

3.6.s:
etasminnantare kāle kācidvidyādharāṅganā /
yadṛcchayāgatā tasya puraścārutarākṛtiḥ //
3.6.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे काले काचिद्विद्याधराङ्गना ।
यदृच्छयागता तस्य पुरश्चारुतराकृतिः ॥
3.6.m:
In the meantime, a certain Vidyādhara woman
of very charming form came before him by chance.

3.6.s:
cirakālena tapasā toṣayitvā parāṃbikām /
tatsamarpitamālyaṃ ca labdhvā saṃtuṣṭamānasā //
3.6.d:
चिरकालेन तपसा तोषयित्वा परांबिकाम् ।
तत्समर्पितमाल्यं च लब्ध्वा संतुष्टमानसा ॥
3.6.m:
Having gratified the Supreme Mother by long-standing austerity,
and having obtained a garland presented by her, her mind was delighted.

3.6.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛguśāvākṣīmuvāca munipuṅgavaḥ /
kutra vā gamyate bhīru kuto labdhamidaṃ tvayā //
3.6.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा मृगुशावाक्षीमुवाच मुनिपुङ्गवः ।
कुत्र वा गम्यते भीरु कुतो लब्धमिदं त्वया ॥
3.6.m:
Seeing her, whose eyes were like those of a young deer, the eminent sage said:
‘Where are you going, timid one? Whence was this obtained by you?’

3.6.s:
praṇamya sā mahātmānamuvāca vinayānvitā /
cireṇa tapasā brahmandevyā dattaṃ prasannayā //
3.6.d:
प्रणम्य सा महात्मानमुवाच विनयान्विता ।
चिरेण तपसा ब्रह्मन्देव्या दत्तं प्रसन्नया ॥
3.6.m:
Bowing to that great-souled one, she said with humility:
‘Through long austerity, O Brahman, it was given by the gracious Goddess.’

3.6.s:
tachrutvā vacanaṃ tasyāḥ so 'pṛcchanmālyamuttamam /
pṛṣṭamātreṇa sā tuṣṭā dadau tasmai mahātmane //
3.6.d:
तछ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्याः सो ऽपृच्छन्माल्यमुत्तमम् ।
पृष्टमात्रेण सा तुष्टा ददौ तस्मै महात्मने ॥
3.6.m:
Having heard those words of hers, he asked for that excellent garland;
as soon as it was requested, she, being pleased, gave it to that great-souled one.

3.6.s:
karābhyāṃ tatsamādāya kṛtārtho 'smīti satvaram /
dadhau svaśirasā bhaktyā tāmuvācātirṣitaḥ //
3.6.d:
कराभ्यां तत्समादाय कृतार्थो ऽस्मीति सत्वरम् ।
दधौ स्वशिरसा भक्त्या तामुवाचातिर्षितः ॥
3.6.m:
Taking it with both hands, thinking ‘I have achieved my purpose,’
he placed it quickly on his head with devotion and, extremely joyful, said to her:

3.6.s:
brahmādīnāmalabhyaṃ yattallabdhaṃ bhāgyato mayā /
bhaktirastu padāṃbhoje devyāstava samujjvalā //
3.6.d:
ब्रह्मादीनामलभ्यं यत्तल्लब्धं भाग्यतो मया ।
भक्तिरस्तु पदांभोजे देव्यास्तव समुज्ज्वला ॥
3.6.m:
‘That which is unattainable even to Brahmā and others has been obtained by me through good fortune;
may your devotion to the lotus feet of the Goddess remain radiant.

3.6.s:
bhaviṣyacchobhanākāre gaccha saumye yathāsukham /
sā taṃ praṇamya śirasā yayau tuṣṭā yathāgatam //
3.6.d:
भविष्यच्छोभनाकारे गच्छ सौम्ये यथासुखम् ।
सा तं प्रणम्य शिरसा ययौ तुष्टा यथागतम् ॥
3.6.m:
O gentle one of fair form to come, go as you please.’
Having bowed to him with her head, she went delighted as she had come.

3.6.s:
preṣayitvā sa tāṃ bhūyo yayau vidyādharādhvanā /
vidyādharavadhūhastātpratijagrāha vallakīm //
3.6.d:
प्रेषयित्वा स तां भूयो ययौ विद्याधराध्वना ।
विद्याधरवधूहस्तात्प्रतिजग्राह वल्लकीम् ॥
3.6.m:
Having sent her away, he again went by the path of the Vidyādharas;
from the hand of a Vidyādhara woman he took a lute,

3.6.s:
divyasraganulepāṃśca divyānyābharaṇāni ca /
kvacidgṛhṇankvacidgā yankvaciddhasan //
3.6.d:
दिव्यस्रगनुलेपांश्च दिव्यान्याभरणानि च ।
क्वचिद्गृह्णन्क्वचिद्गा यन्क्वचिद्धसन् ॥
3.6.m:
and divine garlands, ointments, and divine ornaments;
here taking, here singing, and here laughing,

3.6.s:
svecchāvihārī sa muniryayau yatra purandaraḥ /
svakarasthāṃ tato mālāṃ śakrāya pradadau muniḥ //
3.6.d:
स्वेच्छाविहारी स मुनिर्ययौ यत्र पुरन्दरः ।
स्वकरस्थां ततो मालां शक्राय प्रददौ मुनिः ॥
3.6.m:
roaming at his own will, that sage went where Purandara was.
Then the sage gave the garland resting in his hand to Śakra.

3.6.s:
tāṃ gṛhītvā gajaskandhe sthāpayāmāsa devarāṭ /
gajastu tāṃ gṛhītvātha preṣayāmāsa bhūtale //
3.6.d:
तां गृहीत्वा गजस्कन्धे स्थापयामास देवराट् ।
गजस्तु तां गृहीत्वाथ प्रेषयामास भूतले ॥
3.6.m:
Receiving it, the king of the gods placed it on the elephant’s shoulder;
and the elephant, taking it, threw it down onto the surface of the earth.”

3.6.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā preṣitāṃ mālāṃ tadā krodhena tāpasaḥ /
uvāca na dhṛtā mālā śirasā tu mayārpitā //
3.6.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा प्रेषितां मालां तदा क्रोधेन तापसः ।
उवाच न धृता माला शिरसा तु मयार्पिता ॥
3.6.m: Seeing that garland cast away, the ascetic then spoke in anger: / "The garland offered by me was not placed upon your head!

3.6.s:
trailokyaiśvaryamattena bhavatā hyavamānitā /
mahādevyā dhṛtā yā tu brahmādyaiḥ pūjyatehi sā //
3.6.d:
त्रैलोक्यैश्वर्यमत्तेन भवता ह्यवमानिता ।
महादेव्या धृता या तु ब्रह्माद्यैः पूज्यतेहि सा ॥
3.6.m: Intoxicated by sovereignty over the three worlds, you have insulted it; / it was worn by the Great Goddess, and is indeed worshipped by Brahmā and the rest.

3.6.s:
tvayā yacchāsito lokaḥ sadevāsuramānuṣaḥ /
aśobhano hyatejasko mama śāpādbhaviṣyati //
3.6.d:
त्वया यच्छासितो लोकः सदेवासुरमानुषः ।
अशोभनो ह्यतेजस्को मम शापाद्भविष्यति ॥
3.6.m: The world together with gods, asuras, and humans, which is ruled by you, / will by my curse become devoid of splendor and vigor!"

3.6.s:
iti śaptvā vinītena tena saṃpūjito 'pi saḥ /
tūṣṇīmeva yayau brahmanbhāvikāryamanusmaran //
3.6.d:
इति शप्त्वा विनीतेन तेन संपूजितो ऽपि सः ।
तूष्णीमेव ययौ ब्रह्मन्भाविकार्यमनुस्मरन् ॥
3.6.m: Having thus cursed him, though worshipped by him with humility, / he departed in silence, O Brahmin, keeping future events in mind.

3.6.s:
vijayaśrīstatastasya daityaṃ tu balimanvagāt /
nityaśrīrnityapuruṣaṃ vāsudevamathānvagāt //
3.6.d:
विजयश्रीस्ततस्तस्य दैत्यं तु बलिमन्वगात् ।
नित्यश्रीर्नित्यपुरुषं वासुदेवमथान्वगात् ॥
3.6.m: The Fortune of Victory then went from him to the Daitya Bali, / and eternal Fortune went to the eternal Puruṣa, Vāsudeva.

3.6.s:
indro 'pi svapuraṃ gatvā sarvadevasamanvitaḥ /
viṣaṇṇacetā niḥśrīkaścintayāmāsa devarāṭ //
3.6.d:
इन्द्रो ऽपि स्वपुरं गत्वा सर्वदेवसमन्वितः ।
विषण्णचेता निःश्रीकश्चिन्तयामास देवराट् ॥
3.6.m: Indra too went to his city accompanied by all the gods; / dejected at heart and stripped of fortune, the king of gods reflected.

3.6.s:
athāmarapure dṛṣṭvā nimittānyaśubhāni ca /
bṛhaspatiṃ samāhūya vākyametaduvāca ha //
3.6.d:
अथामरपुरे दृष्ट्वा निमित्तान्यशुभानि च ।
बृहस्पतिं समाहूय वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ॥
3.6.m: Then, seeing inauspicious omens in the city of the immortals, / he summoned Bṛhaspati and spoke these words:

3.6.s:
bhagavansarvadharmajña trikālajñānakovida /
dṛśyate 'dṛṣṭapūrvāṇi nimittānyaśubhāni ca //
3.6.d:
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ त्रिकालज्ञानकोविद ।
दृश्यते ऽदृष्टपूर्वाणि निमित्तान्यशुभानि च ॥
3.6.m: "O Blessed One, knower of all dharma, skilled in knowledge of the three times, / never-before-seen and inauspicious omens are being seen.

3.6.s:
kiṃphalāni ca tāni syurupāyo vātha kīdṛśaḥ /
iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devendrasya bṛhaspatiḥ /
pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ śubham //
3.6.d:
किंफलानि च तानि स्युरुपायो वाथ कीदृशः ।
इति तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवेन्द्रस्य बृहस्पतिः ।
प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं शुभम् ॥
3.6.m: What might their fruits be, and what is the remedy?" / Having heard those words of the king of gods, Bṛhaspati / then replied with words endowed with dharma and benefit, auspicious:

3.6.s:
kṛtasya karmaṇo rājankalpakoṭiśatairapi /
prāyaścittopabhogābhyāṃ vinā nāśo na jāyate //
3.6.d:
कृतस्य कर्मणो राजन्कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ।
प्रायश्चित्तोपभोगाभ्यां विना नाशो न जायते ॥
3.6.m: "Of an action committed, O king, even through hundreds of crores of kalpas, / destruction does not occur without expiation and experience [of its fruit]."

3.6.s:
indra uvāca
karma vā kīdṛśaṃ brahmanprāyaścittaṃ ca kīdṛśam /
tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi tanme vistarato vada //
3.6.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
कर्म वा कीदृशं ब्रह्मन्प्रायश्चित्तं च कीदृशम् ।
तत्सर्वं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तन्मे विस्तरतो वद ॥
3.6.m: Indra said: / "What kind of action [is it], O Brahmin, and what kind of expiation? / I wish to hear all that; tell me that in detail."

3.6.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
hananasteyahiṃsāśca pānamanyāṅganāratiḥ /
karma pañcavidhaṃ prāhurduṣkṛtaṃ dharaṇīpateḥ //
3.6.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
हननस्तेयहिंसाश्च पानमन्याङ्गनारतिः ।
कर्म पञ्चविधं प्राहुर्दुष्कृतं धरणीपतेः ॥
3.6.m: Bṛhaspati said: / "Killing, theft, injury, drinking, and sporting with another's woman: / they say the misdeed of a ruler of the earth is of five kinds.

3.6.s:
brahmakṣatriyaviṭśūdragoturaṅgakharoṣṭrakāḥ /
catuṣpado 'ṇḍajābjāśca tiryaco 'nasthikāstathā //
3.6.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रियविट्शूद्रगोतुरङ्गखरोष्ट्रकाः ।
चतुष्पदो ऽण्डजाब्जाश्च तिर्यचो ऽनस्थिकास्तथा ॥
3.6.m: [Killing] a Brahmin, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, Śūdra, cow, horse, donkey, camel, / quadrupeds, egg-born, water-born, animals, and bone-less creatures:

3.6.s:
ayutaṃ ca sahasraṃ ca śataṃ daśa tathā daśa /
daśapañcatrirekārdhamānupūrvyādidaṃ bhavet //
3.6.d:
अयुतं च सहस्रं च शतं दश तथा दश ।
दशपञ्चत्रिरेकार्धमानुपूर्व्यादिदं भवेत् ॥
3.6.m: Ten thousand, one thousand, one hundred, ten, and ten; / ten, five, three, one, and a half—this should be in succession.

3.6.s:
brahmakṣatraviśāṃ strīṇāmuktārthe pāpamādiśet /
pitṛmātṛgurusvāmi putrāṇāṃ caiva niṣkṛtiḥ //
3.6.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां स्त्रीणामुक्तार्थे पापमादिशेत् ।
पितृमातृगुरुस्वामि पुत्राणां चैव निष्कृतिः ॥
3.6.m: For women of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas, one should assign the sin in the stated manner; / and expiation is for fathers, mothers, gurus, masters, and sons.

3.6.s:
gurvājñayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tadājñālaṅghaner'thakam /
daśabrāhmaṇabhṛtyarthamekaṃ hanyāddvijaṃ nṛpaḥ //
3.6.d:
गुर्वाज्ञया कृतं पापं तदाज्ञालङ्घनेर्ऽथकम् ।
दशब्राह्मणभृत्यर्थमेकं हन्याद्द्विजं नृपः ॥
3.6.m: Sin committed by a guru's order becomes [meaningless] by transgressing his command. / A king may kill one twice-born for the sake of the maintenance of ten Brahmins.

3.6.s:
śatabrāhmaṇabhṛtyarthaṃ brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaṃ tu vā /
pañcabrahmavidāmarthe traiśyamekaṃ tu daṇḍayet //
3.6.d:
शतब्राह्मणभृत्यर्थं ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणं तु वा ।
पञ्चब्रह्मविदामर्थे त्रैश्यमेकं तु दण्डयेत् ॥
3.6.m: For the maintenance of a hundred Brahmins, a Brahmin [may kill] a Brahmin; / for the sake of five knowers of Brahman, one should punish a single [king].

3.6.s:
vaiśyaṃ daśaviśāmarthe viśāṃ vā daṇḍayettathā /
tathā śataviśāmarthe dvijamekaṃ tu daṇḍayet //
3.6.d:
वैश्यं दशविशामर्थे विशां वा दण्डयेत्तथा ।
तथा शतविशामर्थे द्विजमेकं तु दण्डयेत् ॥
3.6.m: [One should punish] a Vaiśya for the sake of ten Vaiśyas, or punish a Vaiśya likewise; / likewise, for the sake of a hundred Vaiśyas, one should punish a single twice-born.

3.6.s:
śūdrāṇāṃ tu sahasrāṇāṃ daṇḍayedbrāhmaṇaṃ tu vā /
tacchatārthaṃ tu vā vaiśyaṃ taddaśārddhaṃ tu śūdrakam //
3.6.d:
शूद्राणां तु सहस्राणां दण्डयेद्ब्राह्मणं तु वा ।
तच्छतार्थं तु वा वैश्यं तद्दशार्द्धं तु शूद्रकम् ॥
3.6.m: For [the sake of] thousands of Śūdras, one should punish a Brahmin; / or for the sake of a hundred of them, a Vaiśya; for half of ten of them, a Śūdra.

3.6.s:
bandhūnāṃ caiva mitrāṇāmiṣṭārthe tu tripādakam /
arthaṃ kalatraputrārthe svātmārthe na tu kiñcana //
3.6.d:
बन्धूनां चैव मित्राणामिष्टार्थे तु त्रिपादकम् ।
अर्थं कलत्रपुत्रार्थे स्वात्मार्थे न तु किञ्चन ॥
3.6.m: For the sake of the desired good of kinsmen and friends, three quarters; / [all] wealth for the sake of wife and son; but nothing for the sake of oneself.

3.6.s:
ātmānaṃ hantumārabdhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ viśam /
gāṃ vā turagamanyaṃ vā hatvā doṣairna lipyate //
3.6.d:
आत्मानं हन्तुमारब्धं ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रियं विशम् ।
गां वा तुरगमन्यं वा हत्वा दोषैर्न लिप्यते ॥
3.6.m: Having slain a Brahmin, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, / a cow, or a horse, or another who has undertaken to kill oneself, one is not stained by sins.

3.6.s:
ātmadārātmajabhrātṛbandhūnāṃ ca dvijottama /
kramāddaśaguṇo doṣo rakṣaṇe ca tathā phalam //
3.6.d:
आत्मदारात्मजभ्रातृबन्धूनां च द्विजोत्तम ।
क्रमाद्दशगुणो दोषो रक्षणे च तथा फलम् ॥
3.6.m: For oneself, wife, son, brother, and kinsmen, O best of the twice-born, / the sin is ten times greater in order, and likewise the fruit in protecting [them].

3.6.s:
bhūpadvijaśrotriyavedavidvratīvedāntavidvedavidāṃ vināśe /
ekadvipañcāśadathāyutaṃ ca syānniṣkṛtiśceti vadanti saṃtaḥ //
3.6.d:
भूपद्विजश्रोत्रियवेदविद्व्रतीवेदान्तविद्वेदविदां विनाशे ।
एकद्विपञ्चाशदथायुतं च स्यान्निष्कृतिश्चेति वदन्ति संतः ॥
3.6.m: In the destruction of a king, twice-born, Śrotriya, knower of the Veda, vows-keeper, knower of Vedānta, and [great] knowers of the Veda, / the expiation would be one, two, fifty, and ten thousand, so say the virtuous.

3.6.s:
teṣāṃ ca rakṣaṇavidhau hi kṛte ca dāne pūrvoditottaraguṇaṃ pravadanti puṇyam /
teṣāṃ ca darśanavidhau namane cakārye śūśrūṣaṇe 'pi caratāṃ sadṛśāṃśca teṣām //
3.6.d:
तेषां च रक्षणविधौ हि कृते च दाने पूर्वोदितोत्तरगुणं प्रवदन्ति पुण्यम् ।
तेषां च दर्शनविधौ नमने चकार्ये शूश्रूषणे ऽपि चरतां सदृशांश्च तेषाम् ॥
3.6.m: And when protection is performed and gift is given to them, they declare merit multiplied beyond what was stated before; / and in seeing them, bowing down, rendering service, and for those behaving similarly to them.

3.6.s:
siṃhavyāghramṛgādīni lokahiṃsākarāṇi tu /
nṛpo hanyācca satataṃ devārthe brāhmaṇārthake //
3.6.d:
सिंहव्याघ्रमृगादीनि लोकहिंसाकराणि तु ।
नृपो हन्याच्च सततं देवार्थे ब्राह्मणार्थके ॥
3.6.m: Lions, tigers, deer, and others that cause harm to people / a king should constantly kill for the sake of the gods and for the sake of Brahmins.

3.6.s: āpatsvātmārthake cāpi hatvā medhyāni bhakṣayet //
3.6.d: आपत्स्वात्मार्थके चापि हत्वा मेध्यानि भक्षयेत् ॥
3.6.m: Even in times of distress for his own sake, having killed sacrificial animals, he may eat them.

3.6.s:
nātmārthe pācayedanna nātmārthe pācayetpaśūn /
devārthe brāhmaṇārthe vā pacamāno na lipyate //
3.6.d:
नात्मार्थे पाचयेदन्न नात्मार्थे पाचयेत्पशून् ।
देवार्थे ब्राह्मणार्थे वा पचमानो न लिप्यते ॥
3.6.m: He should not cook food for himself, nor cook animals for himself; / cooking for the sake of the gods or for the sake of Brahmins, he is not stained.

3.6.s:
purā bhagavatī māyā jagadujjīvanonmukhī /
sasarja sarvadevāṃśca tathaivāsuramānuṣān //
3.6.d:
पुरा भगवती माया जगदुज्जीवनोन्मुखी ।
ससर्ज सर्वदेवांश्च तथैवासुरमानुषान् ॥
3.6.m: Long ago, the blessed Māyā, eager to sustain the world, / created all the gods, and likewise the asuras and human beings.

3.6.s:
teṣāṃ saṃrakṣaṇārthāya paśūnapi caturdaśa /
yajñāśca tadvidhānāni kṛtvā cainānuvāca ha //
3.6.d:
तेषां संरक्षणार्थाय पशूनपि चतुर्दश ।
यज्ञाश्च तद्विधानानि कृत्वा चैनानुवाच ह ॥
3.6.m: For their preservation, having also made fourteen beasts / and sacrifices and their rites, she said to them:

3.6.s:
yajadhvaṃ paśubhirdevānvidhinānena mānavāḥ /
iṣṭāni ye pradāsyanti puṣṭāste yajñabhāvitāḥ //
3.6.d:
यजध्वं पशुभिर्देवान्विधिनानेन मानवाः ।
इष्टानि ये प्रदास्यन्ति पुष्टास्ते यज्ञभाविताः ॥
3.6.m: "Worship the gods with beasts by this rite, O humans! / Nourished, consecrated by sacrifice, they will bestow desired things.

3.6.s:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ /
daridro nārakaścaiva bhavejjanmani janmani //
3.6.d:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।
दरिद्रो नारकश्चैव भवेज्जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥
3.6.m: Whoever does not follow the wheel thus set in motion here / becomes poor and a hell-dweller birth after birth.

3.6.s:
devatārthe ca pitrarthe tathaivābhyāgate gurau /
mahadāgamane caiva hanyānmedhyānpaśūndvijaḥ //
3.6.d:
देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थे तथैवाभ्यागते गुरौ ।
महदागमने चैव हन्यान्मेध्यान्पशून्द्विजः ॥
3.6.m: For the sake of the deities, for the sake of ancestors, likewise when a guru has arrived, / and upon the arrival of an eminent person, a twice-born may kill sacrificial beasts.

3.6.s:
āpatsu brāhmaṇo māṃsaṃ medhyamaśnanna doṣabhāk /
vihitāni tu kāryāṇi pratiṣiddhāni varjayet //
3.6.d:
आपत्सु ब्राह्मणो मांसं मेध्यमश्नन्न दोषभाक् ।
विहितानि तु कार्याणि प्रतिषिद्धानि वर्जयेत् ॥
3.6.m: In times of distress, a Brahmin eating sacrificial meat does not partake in sin; / but he should perform prescribed actions and avoid prohibited ones.

3.6.s:
purābhūdyuvanāśvasya devatānāṃ mahākratuḥ /
mamāyamiti devānāṃ kalahaḥ samajāyata //
3.6.d:
पुराभूद्युवनाश्वस्य देवतानां महाक्रतुः ।
ममायमिति देवानां कलहः समजायत ॥
3.6.m: Long ago, there was a great sacrifice of Yuvanāśva for the deities; / a dispute arose among the gods, saying, 'This is mine!'

3.6.s:
tadā vibhajya devānāṃ mānuṣāṃśca paśūnapi /
vibhajyaikaikaśaḥ pradādbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ //
3.6.d:
तदा विभज्य देवानां मानुषांश्च पशूनपि ।
विभज्यैकैकशः प्रदाद्ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ॥
3.6.m: Then Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, having apportioned to the gods / humans and beasts as well, gave them one by one.

3.6.s:
tatastu paramā śaktirbhūtasaṃdhasahāyinī /
kupitābhūttato brahmā tāmuvāca nayānvitaḥ //
3.6.d:
ततस्तु परमा शक्तिर्भूतसंधसहायिनी ।
कुपिताभूत्ततो ब्रह्मा तामुवाच नयान्वितः ॥
3.6.m: Thereupon the supreme Śakti, accompanied by the host of spirits, / became angry; then Brahmā, endowed with prudence, spoke to her.

3.6.s:
prādurbhūtā samudvīkṣya bhūtānandabhayānvitaḥ /
prāñjaliḥ praṇatastutvā prasīdeti punaḥ punaḥ //
3.6.d:
प्रादुर्भूता समुद्वीक्ष्य भूतानन्दभयान्वितः ।
प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतस्तुत्वा प्रसीदेति पुनः पुनः ॥
3.6.m: Beholding her manifest, filled with awe and fear before the spirits, / with joined palms, bowing down and praising, he said again and again: 'Be pleased!'

3.6.s:
prādurbhūtā yato 'si tvaṃ kṛtartho 'smi puro mama /
tvayaitadakhilaṃ karma nirmitaṃ suśubhāśubham //
3.6.d:
प्रादुर्भूता यतो ऽसि त्वं कृतर्थो ऽस्मि पुरो मम ।
त्वयैतदखिलं कर्म निर्मितं सुशुभाशुभम् ॥
3.6.m: "Since you have become manifest before me, I am fulfilled! / By you all this work, very auspicious and inauspicious, was fashioned.

3.6.s:
śrutayaḥ smṛtayaścaiva tvayaiva pratipāditāḥ /
tvayaiva kalpitā yāgā manmukhāttu mahākratau //
3.6.d:
श्रुतयः स्मृतयश्चैव त्वयैव प्रतिपादिताः ।
त्वयैव कल्पिता यागा मन्मुखात्तु महाक्रतौ ॥
3.6.m: The Vedas and the Smṛtis were indeed set forth by you; / by you indeed sacrifices were arranged through my mouth in the great sacrifice.

3.6.s:
ye vibhaktāstu paśavo devānāṃ parameśvari /
te sarve tāvakāḥ saṃtubhūtānāmapi tṛptaye //
3.6.d:
ये विभक्तास्तु पशवो देवानां परमेश्वरि ।
ते सर्वे तावकाः संतुभूतानामपि तृप्तये ॥
3.6.m: The beasts that were apportioned for the gods, O Supreme Lady, / let them all be yours, for the satisfaction of the spirits as well!"

3.6.s:
ityuktvāntardadhe teṣāṃ pura eva pitāmahaḥ /
taduktenaiva vidhinā cakāra ca mahākratūn //
3.6.d:
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे तेषां पुर एव पितामहः ।
तदुक्तेनैव विधिना चकार च महाक्रतून् ॥
3.6.m: Having said this, the Grandfather vanished right before them; / and he performed great sacrifices by the very rite spoken by her.

3.6.s:
iyāja ca parāṃ śaktiṃ hatvā medhyānpaśūnapi /
tattadvibhāgo vedeṣu proktatvādiha noditaḥ //
3.6.d:
इयाज च परां शक्तिं हत्वा मेध्यान्पशूनपि ।
तत्तद्विभागो वेदेषु प्रोक्तत्वादिह नोदितः ॥
3.6.m: And he worshipped the supreme Śakti, having also slaughtered sacrificial beasts; / their various divisions are not stated here because they are declared in the Vedas.

3.6.s:
striyaḥ śudrāstathā māṃsamādadyurbrāhmaṇaṃ vinā /
āpatsu brāhmaṇo vāpi bhakṣayedgurvanujñayā //
3.6.d:
स्त्रियः शुद्रास्तथा मांसमादद्युर्ब्राह्मणं विना ।
आपत्सु ब्राह्मणो वापि भक्षयेद्गुर्वनुज्ञया ॥
3.6.m: Women and Śūdras may take meat without a Brahmin; / in times of distress, even a Brahmin may eat [it] by the permission of a guru.

3.6.s:
śivodbhavamida piṇḍamatyatha śivatāṃ gatam /
udbudhyasva paśo tvaṃ hi nāśivaḥ sañchivo hyasi //
3.6.d:
शिवोद्भवमिद पिण्डमत्यथ शिवतां गतम् ।
उद्बुध्यस्व पशो त्वं हि नाशिवः सञ्छिवो ह्यसि ॥
3.6.m: "This body sprung from Śiva has gone beyond to the state of Śiva; / awaken, O beast! For you are not un-Śiva, you are indeed Śiva!

3.6.s:
īśaḥ sarvajagatkartā prabhavaḥ pralayastathā /
yato viśvādhiko rudrastena rudro 'si vai paśo //
3.6.d:
ईशः सर्वजगत्कर्ता प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ।
यतो विश्वाधिको रुद्रस्तेन रुद्रो ऽसि वै पशो ॥
3.6.m: The Lord is the creator of the entire universe, its origin as well as dissolution; / since Rudra is superior to the universe, therefore you are indeed Rudra, O beast!"

3.6.s:
anena turagaṃ gā vā gajoṣṭramahiṣādikam /
ātmārthaṃ vā parārthaṃ vā hatvā doṣairna lipyate //
3.6.d:
अनेन तुरगं गा वा गजोष्ट्रमहिषादिकम् ।
आत्मार्थं वा परार्थं वा हत्वा दोषैर्न लिप्यते ॥
3.6.m: Having killed with this [mantra] a horse, cow, elephant, camel, buffalo, and the like, / for one's own sake or for another's sake, one is not stained by sins.

3.6.s:
gṛhāniṣṭakarānvāpi nāgākhubalivṛścikān /
etadgṛhāśramasthānāṃ kriyāphalamabhīpsatām /
manaḥsaṃkalpasiddhānāṃ mahatāṃ śivavarcasām //
3.6.d:
गृहानिष्टकरान्वापि नागाखुबलिवृश्चिकान् ।
एतद्गृहाश्रमस्थानां क्रियाफलमभीप्सताम् ।
मनःसंकल्पसिद्धानां महतां शिववर्चसाम् ॥
3.6.m: Or even [by killing] snakes, mice, offerings-[stealing pests], and scorpions that bring harm to the house: / this is the fruit of action for those residing in the householder order who desire results, / who have attained their heart's resolves, who are great, and who have the splendor of Śiva.

3.6.s:
paśuyajñena cānyeṣāmiṣṭā pūrtikaraṃ bhavet /
japahomārcanādyaistu teṣāmiṣṭaṃ ca sidhyati //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne hiṃsādyasvarūpakathanaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ
3.6.d:
पशुयज्ञेन चान्येषामिष्टा पूर्तिकरं भवेत् ।
जपहोमार्चनाद्यैस्तु तेषामिष्टं च सिध्यति ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने हिंसाद्यस्वरूपकथनं नाम षष्ठो ऽध्यायः
3.6.m:
And for others, the fulfillment of desires comes through animal sacrifice, / but for these [great ones], their desire is accomplished through recitation, oblation, worship, and the like.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'The Description of the Nature of Violence and the Like,' in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the final part of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

3.7.s:
indra uvāca
bhagavansarvamākhyātaṃ hiṃsādyasya tu lakṣaṇam /
steyasya lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ vā tanme vistarato vada //
3.7.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
भगवन्सर्वमाख्यातं हिंसाद्यस्य तु लक्षणम् ।
स्तेयस्य लक्षणं किं वा तन्मे विस्तरतो वद ॥
3.7.m: Indra said: / Blessed Lord, everything concerning the characteristics of violence and the like has been told. / But what are the characteristics of theft? Tell me that in detail.

3.7.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
pāpānāmadhikaṃ pāpaṃ hananaṃ jīvajātinām /
etasmādadhikaṃ pāpaṃ viśvaste śaraṇaṃ gate //
3.7.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
पापानामधिकं पापं हननं जीवजातिनाम् ।
एतस्मादधिकं पापं विश्वस्ते शरणं गते ॥
3.7.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Greater than [other] sins is the sin of killing living creatures; / greater than this is the sin [committed] against one who is trusting and has sought refuge.

3.7.s:
viśvasya hatvā pāpiṣṭhaṃ śūdraṃ vāpyantyajātijam /
brahmahatyādhikaṃ pāpaṃ tasmānnāstyasya niṣkṛtiḥ //
3.7.d:
विश्वस्य हत्वा पापिष्ठं शूद्रं वाप्यन्त्यजातिजम् ।
ब्रह्महत्याधिकं पापं तस्मान्नास्त्यस्य निष्कृतिः ॥
3.7.m: If one slays even a very wicked person, a śūdra, or one born of an outcast caste after winning his trust, / the sin is greater than the killing of a brāhmaṇa; therefore, there is no expiation for it.

3.7.s:
brahmajñasya daridrasya kṛcchrārjitadhanasya ca /
bahuputrakalatrasya tena jīvitumicchataḥ /
taddravyasteyadoṣasya prāyaścittaṃ na vidyate //
3.7.d:
ब्रह्मज्ञस्य दरिद्रस्य कृच्छ्रार्जितधनस्य च ।
बहुपुत्रकलत्रस्य तेन जीवितुमिच्छतः ।
तद्द्रव्यस्तेयदोषस्य प्रायश्चित्तं न विद्यते ॥
3.7.m: For the sin of stealing the wealth of a knower of Brahman who is poor, whose wealth was acquired with hardship, / who has many children and a wife, and who desires to live by means of that [wealth], / there is no expiation.

3.7.s:
viśvastadravyaharaṇaṃ tasyāpyadhikamucyate /
viśvaste vāpyaviśvaste na daridradhanaṃ haret //
3.7.d:
विश्वस्तद्रव्यहरणं तस्याप्यधिकमुच्यते ।
विश्वस्ते वाप्यविश्वस्ते न दरिद्रधनं हरेत् ॥
3.7.m: The taking of the property of a trusting person is said to be greater even than that; / whether one is trusting or not, one must never take the wealth of a poor person.

3.7.s:
tato devadvijātīnāṃ hemaratnāpahārakam /
yo hanyādavicāreṇa so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet //
3.7.d:
ततो देवद्विजातीनां हेमरत्नापहारकम् ।
यो हन्यादविचारेण सो ऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥
3.7.m: Therefore, whoever kills without hesitation a stealer of gold and jewels belonging to the gods and the twice-born / obtains the fruit of an horse sacrifice.

3.7.s:
gurudevadvijasuhṛtputrasvātmasukheṣu ca /
steyādadhaḥkrameṇaiva daśottaraguṇaṃ tvagham //
3.7.d:
गुरुदेवद्विजसुहृत्पुत्रस्वात्मसुखेषु च ।
स्तेयादधःक्रमेणैव दशोत्तरगुणं त्वघम् ॥
3.7.m: With respect to the guru, gods, twice-born, friends, sons, and the happiness of one's own self, / the sin [increases] tenfold in successive descending order through theft.

3.7.s:
antyajātpādajādvaiśyātkṣatriyādbrāhmaṇādapi /
daśottaraguṇaiḥ pāpairlipyate dhanahārakaḥ //
3.7.d:
अन्त्यजात्पादजाद्वैश्यात्क्षत्रियाद्ब्राह्मणादपि ।
दशोत्तरगुणैः पापैर्लिप्यते धनहारकः ॥
3.7.m: From an outcast, from a śūdra, from a vaiśya, from a kṣatriya, and from a brāhmaṇa, / the stealer of wealth is tainted by sins multiplied tenfold in turn.

3.7.s:
atraivodāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam /
rahasyātirahasyaṃ ca sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
3.7.d:
अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
रहस्यातिरहस्यं च सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
3.7.m: In this very connection, they cite this ancient history, / most secret of secrets, which destroys all sins.

3.7.s:
purā kāñcīpure jāto vajrākhyo nāma corakaḥ /
tasminpuravare ramye sarvaiśvaryasamanvitāḥ /
sarve nīrogiṇo dāntāḥ sukhino dayayāñcitāḥ //
3.7.d:
पुरा काञ्चीपुरे जातो वज्राख्यो नाम चोरकः ।
तस्मिन्पुरवरे रम्ये सर्वैश्वर्यसमन्विताः ।
सर्वे नीरोगिणो दान्ताः सुखिनो दययाञ्चिताः ॥
3.7.m: Formerly, in the city of Kāñcī, there was born a thief named Vajra. / In that excellent and charming city, [the inhabitants] were endowed with all prosperity; / all were free from disease, self-restrained, happy, and adorned with compassion.

3.7.s:
sarvaiśvaryasamṛddhe 'sminnagare sa tu taskaraḥ /
stokāstokakrameṇaiva bahudravyamapāharat //
3.7.d:
सर्वैश्वर्यसमृद्धे ऽस्मिन्नगरे स तु तस्करः ।
स्तोकास्तोकक्रमेणैव बहुद्रव्यमपाहरत् ॥
3.7.m: In this city thriving with every kind of wealth, that thief, / by little and little, stole much property.

3.7.s:
tadaraṇye 'vaṭaṃ kṛtvā sthāpayāmāsa lobhataḥ /
tadgopanaṃ niśārdhāyāṃ tasmindūraṃ gate sati //
3.7.d:
तदरण्ये ऽवटं कृत्वा स्थापयामास लोभतः ।
तद्गोपनं निशार्धायां तस्मिन्दूरं गते सति ॥
3.7.m: Making a pit in that forest, he placed it [there] out of greed. / In concealing it at midnight, when he had gone far off,

3.7.s:
kirātaḥ kaścidāgatya taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu daśāṃśataḥ /
jahārāviditastena kāṣṭhabhāraṃ vahanyayau //
3.7.d:
किरातः कश्चिदागत्य तं दृष्ट्वा तु दशांशतः ।
जहाराविदितस्तेन काष्ठभारं वहन्ययौ ॥
3.7.m: a certain Kirāta came, saw him, and / unbeknownst to him, carried off a tenth part of it and went away bearing a load of wood.

3.7.s:
so 'pi tacchilayācchādya mṛdbhirāpūryayatnataḥ /
punaśca tatpuraṃ prāyādvajro 'pi dhanatṛṣmayā //
3.7.d:
सो ऽपि तच्छिलयाच्छाद्य मृद्भिरापूर्ययत्नतः ।
पुनश्च तत्पुरं प्रायाद्वज्रो ऽपि धनतृष्मया ॥
3.7.m: Vajra too, having covered it with a stone and carefully filled it with earth, / went back to that city out of thirst for wealth.

3.7.s:
evaṃ bahudhanaṃ tdṛtvā niścikṣepa mahītale /
kirāto 'pi gṛhaṃ prāpya babhāṣe muditaḥ priyām //
3.7.d:
एवं बहुधनं त्दृत्वा निश्चिक्षेप महीतले ।
किरातो ऽपि गृहं प्राप्य बभाषे मुदितः प्रियाम् ॥
3.7.m: Having thus taken much wealth, he buried it in the earth. / The Kirāta also, having reached home, said joyfully to his beloved:

3.7.s:
mayā kāṣṭhaṃ samāhartuṃ gacchatā pathi nirjane /
labdhaṃ dhanamidaṃ bhīru samādhatsva dhanārthini //
3.7.d:
मया काष्ठं समाहर्तुं गच्छता पथि निर्जने ।
लब्धं धनमिदं भीरु समाधत्स्व धनार्थिनि ॥
3.7.m: “As I was going along a deserted path to gather firewood, / this wealth was found by me, timid woman; receive it, you who desire wealth.”

3.7.s:
tacchrutvā tatsamādāya nidhāyābhyantare tataḥ /
cintayantī tato vākyamidaṃ svapatimabravīt //
3.7.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा तत्समादाय निधायाभ्यन्तरे ततः ।
चिन्तयन्ती ततो वाक्यमिदं स्वपतिमब्रवीत् ॥
3.7.m: Hearing that, taking it and placing it inside, / she then reflected and spoke these words to her husband:

3.7.s:
nityaṃ saṃcarate vipro māmakānāṃ gṛheṣu yaḥ /
māṃ vilokyaivamacirādbahubhāgyavatī bhavet //
3.7.d:
नित्यं संचरते विप्रो मामकानां गृहेषु यः ।
मां विलोक्यैवमचिराद्बहुभाग्यवती भवेत् ॥
3.7.m: “The brāhmaṇa who constantly visits the houses of my people, / on seeing me, [said]: ‘Before long she will be very fortunate.

3.7.s:
cāturvarṇyāsu narīṣu stheyaṃ cedrājavallabhā /
kiṃ tu bhille kirāte ca śailūṣe cāntyajātije /
lakṣmīrna tiṣṭhati ciraṃ śāpādvalmīkajanmanaḥ //
3.7.d:
चातुर्वर्ण्यासु नरीषु स्थेयं चेद्राजवल्लभा ।
किं तु भिल्ले किराते च शैलूषे चान्त्यजातिजे ।
लक्ष्मीर्न तिष्ठति चिरं शापाद्वल्मीकजन्मनः ॥
3.7.m: If she were among the women of the four castes, she would be beloved of a king. / But among a Bhilla, a Kirāta, an actor, and one born of an outcast caste, / Lakṣmī does not stay long, because of the curse of the one born of an anthill.’

3.7.s:
tathāpi bahubhāgyānāṃ puṇyānāmapi pātriṇe /
dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ na kadācidvṛthā bhavet //
3.7.d:
तथापि बहुभाग्यानां पुण्यानामपि पात्रिणे ।
दृष्टपूर्वं तु तद्वाक्यं न कदाचिद्वृथा भवेत् ॥
3.7.m: Even so, for a recipient of great fortunes and merits, / that statement seen previously can never be in vain.

3.7.s:
atha vātmaprayāsena kṛcchrādyallabhyate dhanam /
tadeva tiṣṭhati cirādanyadgacchati kālataḥ //
3.7.d:
अथ वात्मप्रयासेन कृच्छ्राद्यल्लभ्यते धनम् ।
तदेव तिष्ठति चिरादन्यद्गच्छति कालतः ॥
3.7.m: Or rather, that wealth which is obtained with hardship through one's own labor, / that alone remains for a long time; other [wealth] vanishes in time.

3.7.s:
svayamāgatavittaṃ tu dharmārthairviniyojayet /
kuruṣvaitena tasmāttvaṃ vāpīkūpādikāñchubhān //
3.7.d:
स्वयमागतवित्तं तु धर्मार्थैर्विनियोजयेत् ।
कुरुष्वैतेन तस्मात्त्वं वापीकूपादिकाञ्छुभान् ॥
3.7.m: One should apply wealth that has come of itself to purposes of dharma. / Therefore, construct auspicious stepped ponds, wells, and the like with this.”

3.7.s:
iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhāvibhāgyaprabodhitam /
bahūdakasamaṃ deśaṃ tatra tatra vyalokayat //
3.7.d:
इति तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भाविभाग्यप्रबोधितम् ।
बहूदकसमं देशं तत्र तत्र व्यलोकयत् ॥
3.7.m: Having heard her words, awakened to his future fortune, / he looked here and there for a level area with abundant water.

3.7.s:
nirmame 'tha mahendrasya digbhāge vimalodakam /
subahudravyasaṃ sādhyaṃ taṭākaṃ cākṣayodakam //
3.7.d:
निर्ममे ऽथ महेन्द्रस्य दिग्भागे विमलोदकम् ।
सुबहुद्रव्यसं साध्यं तटाकं चाक्षयोदकम् ॥
3.7.m: Then, in the direction of Mahendra, he constructed a reservoir with clear water, / which required a great deal of wealth to accomplish, and possessed inexhaustible water.

3.7.s:
datteṣu karmakāribhyo nikhileṣu dhaneṣu ca /
asaṃbūrṇaṃ tu tatkarma dṛṣṭvā cintākulo 'bhavat //
3.7.d:
दत्तेषु कर्मकारिभ्यो निखिलेषु धनेषु च ।
असंबूर्णं तु तत्कर्म दृष्ट्वा चिन्ताकुलो ऽभवत् ॥
3.7.m: When all the wealth had been given to the laborers, / seeing that work still incomplete, he became distressed with worry:

3.7.s:
taṃ cora vajranāmānamajñāto 'nucarāmyaham /
tenaiva bahudhā kṣiptaṃ dhanaṃ bhūri mahītale //
3.7.d:
तं चोर वज्रनामानमज्ञातो ऽनुचराम्यहम् ।
तेनैव बहुधा क्षिप्तं धनं भूरि महीतले ॥
3.7.m: “I will follow that thief named Vajra without being noticed; / much wealth has been buried in the ground in many places by him alone.

3.7.s:
stokaṃstokaṃ hariṣyāmi tatratatra dhanaṃ bahu /
iti niścitya manasā tenājñātastamanvagāt //
3.7.d:
स्तोकंस्तोकं हरिष्यामि तत्रतत्र धनं बहु ।
इति निश्चित्य मनसा तेनाज्ञातस्तमन्वगात् ॥
3.7.m: Little by little, I shall take much wealth here and there.” / Having thus resolved in his mind, he followed him unnoticed by him.

3.7.s:
tathaivātdṛtya taddravyaṃ tena setumapūrayat /
madhye jalāvṛtastena prāsādaścāpi śārṅgiṇaḥ //
3.7.d:
तथैवात्दृत्य तद्द्रव्यं तेन सेतुमपूरयत् ।
मध्ये जलावृतस्तेन प्रासादश्चापि शार्ङ्गिणः ॥
3.7.m: Taking that wealth in the very same way, he completed the embankment with it. / Surrounded by water in the middle, a palace for the wielder of the Śārṅga bow was also [built] by him.

3.7.s:
tattaṭākamabhūddivyamaśoṣitajalaṃ mahat /
setumadhye cakārāsau śaṅkarāyatanaṃ mahat //
3.7.d:
तत्तटाकमभूद्दिव्यमशोषितजलं महत् ।
सेतुमध्ये चकारासौ शङ्करायतनं महत् ॥
3.7.m: That reservoir became divine, extensive, and with water that never dried up. / In the middle of the embankment, he built a great temple to Śaṅkara.

3.7.s:
kānanaṃ ca kṣayaṃ nītaṃ bahusattvasamākulam /
tenāgryāṇi mahārhāṇi kṣetrāṇyapi cakāra saḥ //
3.7.d:
काननं च क्षयं नीतं बहुसत्त्वसमाकुलम् ।
तेनाग्र्याणि महार्हाणि क्षेत्राण्यपि चकार सः ॥
3.7.m: And the forest, teeming with many living creatures, was cleared; / from it he made excellent, highly valuable fields.

3.7.s:
devatābhyo dvijebhyaśca padattāni vibhajya vai /
brāhmaṇāṃśca samāmantrya devavrātamukhānbahūn //
3.7.d:
देवताभ्यो द्विजेभ्यश्च पदत्तानि विभज्य वै ।
ब्राह्मणांश्च समामन्त्र्य देवव्रातमुखान्बहून् ॥
3.7.m: Having divided them, he gave them to deities and the twice-born. / And having invited many brāhmaṇas headed by Devavrāta,

3.7.s:
saṃtoṣya hemavastrādyairidaṃ vacanamabravīt /
kva cāhaṃ vīradattākhyaḥ kirātaḥ kāṣṭhavikrayī //
3.7.d:
संतोष्य हेमवस्त्राद्यैरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
क्व चाहं वीरदत्ताख्यः किरातः काष्ठविक्रयी ॥
3.7.m: and satisfied them with gold, garments, and the like, he spoke these words: / “Where am I, a Kirāta named Vīradatta, a seller of firewood,

3.7.s:
kva vā mahāsetubandhaḥ kva devālayakalpanā /
kva vā kṣetrāṇi kḷptāni brāhmaṇāyatanāni ca //
3.7.d:
क्व वा महासेतुबन्धः क्व देवालयकल्पना ।
क्व वा क्षेत्राणि कॢप्तानि ब्राह्मणायतनानि च ॥
3.7.m: and where is the construction of a great embankment, where the fashioning of a temple, / and where are fields prepared and dwellings for brāhmaṇas?

3.7.s:
kṛpayaiva kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ bhavatāṃ bhūsurottamāḥ /
pratigṛhya tathaivaitaddevavrātamukhā dvijāḥ //
3.7.d:
कृपयैव कृतं सर्वं भवतां भूसुरोत्तमाः ।
प्रतिगृह्य तथैवैतद्देवव्रातमुखा द्विजाः ॥
3.7.m: All has been done through your grace alone, O best of earthly gods!” / Accepting it in that manner, the twice-born headed by Devavrāta,

3.7.s:
dvijavarmeti nāmāsmai tasyai śīlavatīti ca /
cakruḥ saṃtuṣṭamanaso mahātmāno mahaujasaḥ //
3.7.d:
द्विजवर्मेति नामास्मै तस्यै शीलवतीति च ।
चक्रुः संतुष्टमनसो महात्मानो महौजसः ॥
3.7.m: those high-souled, very powerful men, with hearts well pleased, / bestowed on him the name Dvijavarmā, and on her the name Śīlavatī.

3.7.s:
teṣāṃ saṃrakṣaṇārthāya bandhumiḥ sahito vaśī /
tatraiva vasatiṃ cakre mudito bhāryayā saha //
3.7.d:
तेषां संरक्षणार्थाय बन्धुमिः सहितो वशी ।
तत्रैव वसतिं चक्रे मुदितो भार्यया सह ॥
3.7.m: For their protection, the self-controlled man, together with his kinsmen, / took up residence in that very place, joyful, with his wife.

3.7.s:
purohitābhidhānena devarātapurantviti /
nāma cakre purasyāsya toṣa yannakhilāndvijān //
3.7.d:
पुरोहिताभिधानेन देवरातपुरन्त्विति ।
नाम चक्रे पुरस्यास्य तोष यन्नखिलान्द्विजान् ॥
3.7.m: After the name of his priest, he gave to this town / the name Devarātapura, pleasing all the twice-born.

3.7.s:
tataḥ kālavaśaṃ prāpto dvijavarmā mṛtastadā /
yamasya brahmaṇo viṣṇordūtā rudrasya cāgatāḥ //
3.7.d:
ततः कालवशं प्राप्तो द्विजवर्मा मृतस्तदा ।
यमस्य ब्रह्मणो विष्णोर्दूता रुद्रस्य चागताः ॥
3.7.m: Then, falling under the power of time, Dvijavarmā died. / The messengers of Yama, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra arrived.

3.7.s:
