anyo 'nyamabhavatteṣāṃ yuddhaṃ devāsuropamam /
atrāntare samāgatya nārado munirabravīt //
3.7.d:
अन्यो ऽन्यमभवत्तेषां युद्धं देवासुरोपमम् ।
अत्रान्तरे समागत्य नारदो मुनिरब्रवीत् ॥
3.7.m: There arose among them a battle resembling that between gods and asuras. / In the meantime, the sage Nārada arrived and said:

3.7.s:
mā kurvantu mitho yuddhaṃ śṛṇvantu vacanaṃ mama /
ayaṃ kirātaścairyeṇa setubandhaṃ purākarot //
3.7.d:
मा कुर्वन्तु मिथो युद्धं शृण्वन्तु वचनं मम ।
अयं किरातश्चैर्येण सेतुबन्धं पुराकरोत् ॥
3.7.m: “Do not fight with one another; hear my word! / Formerly, this Kirāta constructed the embankment through theft.

3.7.s:
vāyubhūtascaredeko yāvaddravyavato mṛtiḥ /
sa bahubhyo hareddravyaṃ teṣāṃ yāvattathā mṛtiḥ //
3.7.d:
वायुभूतस्चरेदेको यावद्द्रव्यवतो मृतिः ।
स बहुभ्यो हरेद्द्रव्यं तेषां यावत्तथा मृतिः ॥
3.7.m: He shall wander alone, having become wind, until the death of the owner of the wealth; / that one stole wealth from many, [so he must wander] until their death likewise.”

3.7.s:
gateṣvakhiladūteṣu śrutvā nāradabhāṣitam /
cacāra dvādaśābdaṃ tu vāyubhūtoṃ'tarikṣagaḥ //
3.7.d:
गतेष्वखिलदूतेषु श्रुत्वा नारदभाषितम् ।
चचार द्वादशाब्दं तु वायुभूतोंऽतरिक्षगः ॥
3.7.m: When all the messengers had departed upon hearing the words of Nārada, / he wandered for twelve years as wind, moving in the intermediate space.

3.7.s:
bhāryāṃ tasyāha sa munistava doṣo na kiñcana /
tvayā kṛtena puṇyena brahmalokamito vraja //
3.7.d:
भार्यां तस्याह स मुनिस्तव दोषो न किञ्चन ।
त्वया कृतेन पुण्येन ब्रह्मलोकमितो व्रज ॥
3.7.m: The sage said to his wife: “You have no fault whatsoever. / By the merit acquired by you, go from here to the world of Brahmā.”

3.7.s:
vāyubhūtaṃ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā necchati brahmamandiram /
nirvedaṃ paramāpannā munimevamabhāṣata //
3.7.d:
वायुभूतं पतिं दृष्ट्वा नेच्छति ब्रह्ममन्दिरम् ।
निर्वेदं परमापन्ना मुनिमेवमभाषत ॥
3.7.m: Seeing her husband turned into wind, she did not desire the abode of Brahmā. / Having reached utter dejection, she spoke thus to the sage:

3.7.s:
vinā patimahaṃ tena na gaccheyaṃ pitāmaham /
hahaivāste patiryāvatsvadehaṃ labhate tathā //
3.7.d:
विना पतिमहं तेन न गच्छेयं पितामहम् ।
हहैवास्ते पतिर्यावत्स्वदेहं लभते तथा ॥
3.7.m: "Without my husband, I will not go to the Grandfather. / Let me remain right here, as long as my husband regains his body in that way.

3.7.s:
tatastu yā gatistasya tāmevānucarāmyaham /
parihāro 'thavā kiṃ tu mayā kāryastu tena vā //
3.7.d:
ततस्तु या गतिस्तस्य तामेवानुचराम्यहम् ।
परिहारो ऽथवा किं तु मया कार्यस्तु तेन वा ॥
3.7.m: Then, whatever destiny is his, that very one shall I follow. / But what expiation must be performed by me, or by him?"

3.7.s:
iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā prītaḥ prāha tapodhanaḥ /
bhogātmakaṃ śarīraṃ tu karma kāryakaraṃ tava //
3.7.d:
इति तस्या वचः श्रुत्वा प्रीतः प्राह तपोधनः ।
भोगात्मकं शरीरं तु कर्म कार्यकरं तव ॥
3.7.m: Hearing her words, the ascetic, pleased, said: / "A body meant for enjoyment will act effectively for you through your deeds.

3.7.s:
mama prabhāvādbhavitā parihāraṃ vadāmi te /
nirāhāro mahātīrthesnātvā nityaṃ hi sāṃbikam //
3.7.d:
मम प्रभावाद्भविता परिहारं वदामि ते ।
निराहारो महातीर्थेस्नात्वा नित्यं हि सांबिकम् ॥
3.7.m: By my power it will come to be; I shall declare the expiation to you. / Fasting, having bathed at a great sacred place, ever [worshipping] Śiva with Ambikā,

3.7.s:
pūjayitvā śivaṃ bhaktyā kandamūlaphalāśanaḥ /
dhyātvā hṛdi maheśānaṃ śatarudramanuṃ japet //
3.7.d:
पूजयित्वा शिवं भक्त्या कन्दमूलफलाशनः ।
ध्यात्वा हृदि महेशानं शतरुद्रमनुं जपेत् ॥
3.7.m: worshipping Śiva with devotion, eating bulbs, roots, and fruits, / meditating in the heart upon the Great Lord, one should mutter the Śatarudra mantra.

3.7.s:
brahmahā mucyate pāpairaṣṭottarasahasrataḥ /
pāpairanyaiśca sakalairmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
3.7.d:
ब्रह्महा मुच्यते पापैरष्टोत्तरसहस्रतः ।
पापैरन्यैश्च सकलैर्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
3.7.m: A slayer of a Brahmin is freed from sins by a thousand and eight [recitations]; / he is freed from all other sins as well; of this there is no doubt."

3.7.s:
ityādiśya dadau tasyai rudrādhyāyaṃ tapodhanaḥ /
anugṛhyeti tāṃ nārīṃ tatraivāntarddhimāgamat //
3.7.d:
इत्यादिश्य ददौ तस्यै रुद्राध्यायं तपोधनः ।
अनुगृह्येति तां नारीं तत्रैवान्तर्द्धिमागमत् ॥
3.7.m: Having instructed thus, the ascetic gave her the Rudrādhyāya. / Having shown favor to that woman, he vanished right there.

3.7.s:
bhartuḥ priyārthe saṃkalpya jajāpa paramaṃ japam /
vimuktasteyadoṣeṇa svaśarīramavāpa saḥ //
3.7.d:
भर्तुः प्रियार्थे संकल्प्य जजाप परमं जपम् ।
विमुक्तस्तेयदोषेण स्वशरीरमवाप सः ॥
3.7.m: Resolving for the sake of her husband's well-being, she muttered the supreme recitation. / Freed from the fault of theft, he regained his own body.

3.7.s:
tato vajrābhidhaścauraḥ kāladharmamupāgataḥ /
anye taddravyavanto 'pi kāladharmamupāgatāḥ //
3.7.d:
ततो वज्राभिधश्चौरः कालधर्ममुपागतः ।
अन्ये तद्द्रव्यवन्तो ऽपि कालधर्ममुपागताः ॥
3.7.m: Then the thief named Vajra met his death. / The others who possessed that wealth also met their death.

3.7.s: yamastu tānsamāhūya vākyaṃ caitaduvāca ha //
3.7.d: यमस्तु तान्समाहूय वाक्यं चैतदुवाच ह ॥
3.7.m: Then Yama, having summoned them together, spoke this word:

3.7.s:
bhavadbhistu kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ daivātsukṛtamapyuta /
kimicchatha phalaṃ bhoktuṃ duṣkṛtasya śubhasya vā //
3.7.d:
भवद्भिस्तु कृतं पापं दैवात्सुकृतमप्युत ।
किमिच्छथ फलं भोक्तुं दुष्कृतस्य शुभस्य वा ॥
3.7.m: "Sin was committed by you, and by chance good deeds as well. / Which fruit do you desire to enjoy first, that of the evil deed or of the good?"

3.7.s:
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā procurvajrādikāstataḥ /
sukṛtasya phalaṃ tvādau paścātpāpasya bhujyate //
3.7.d:
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रोचुर्वज्रादिकास्ततः ।
सुकृतस्य फलं त्वादौ पश्चात्पापस्य भुज्यते ॥
3.7.m: Hearing his words, Vajra and the others said then: / "First let the fruit of good deeds be enjoyed, and afterward that of sin."

3.7.s:
punarāha yamo yūyaṃ putramitra kalatrakaiḥ /
etasyaiva balātsarve tridivaṃ gacchata drutam //
3.7.d:
पुनराह यमो यूयं पुत्रमित्र कलत्रकैः ।
एतस्यैव बलात्सर्वे त्रिदिवं गच्छत द्रुतम् ॥
3.7.m: Yama spoke again: "Together with your sons, friends, and wives, / through his power alone, go swiftly, all of you, to heaven."

3.7.s:
te 'dhiruhya vimānāgryaṃ dvijavarmāṇamāśritāḥ /
yathocitaphalopetāstridivaṃ jagmurañjasā //
3.7.d:
ते ऽधिरुह्य विमानाग्र्यं द्विजवर्माणमाश्रिताः ।
यथोचितफलोपेतास्त्रिदिवं जग्मुरञ्जसा ॥
3.7.m: Mounting an excellent aerial car, having resorted to Dvijavarma, / endowed with the appropriate fruit, they went straight to heaven.

3.7.s:
dvijavarmākhilāṃllokānatītya pramadāsakhaḥ /
gāṇapatyamanuprāpya kailāse 'dyāpi modate //
3.7.d:
द्विजवर्माखिलांल्लोकानतीत्य प्रमदासखः ।
गाणपत्यमनुप्राप्य कैलासे ऽद्यापि मोदते ॥
3.7.m: Dvijavarma, having surpassed all the worlds, accompanied by his wife, / having attained leadership of the Gaṇas, rejoices on Kailāsa even today.

3.7.s:
indra uvāca
tāratamyavibhāgaṃ ca kathaya tvaṃ mahāmate /
setubandhādikānāṃ ca puṇyānāṃ puṇyavardhanam //
3.7.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
तारतम्यविभागं च कथय त्वं महामते ।
सेतुबन्धादिकानां च पुण्यानां पुण्यवर्धनम् ॥
3.7.m: Indra said: / "O wise one, explain the distinction of degrees / of meritorious acts, such as the building of the causeway, which increase merit."

3.7.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
puṇyasyārddhaphalaṃ prāpya dvijavarmā mahāyaśāḥ /
vajraḥ prāpya tadardhaṃ tu tadardhena yutāḥ pare //
3.7.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
पुण्यस्यार्द्धफलं प्राप्य द्विजवर्मा महायशाः ।
वज्रः प्राप्य तदर्धं तु तदर्धेन युताः परे ॥
3.7.m: Bṛhaspati said: / "Having received half the fruit of the merit, Dvijavarma was illustrious; / Vajra received half of that, and the others were endowed with half of that.

3.7.s:
manovākkāyaceṣṭābhiścaturdhākriyate kṛtiḥ /
vinaśyettena tenaiva kṛtaistatparihārakaiḥ //
3.7.d:
मनोवाक्कायचेष्टाभिश्चतुर्धाक्रियते कृतिः ।
विनश्येत्तेन तेनैव कृतैस्तत्परिहारकैः ॥
3.7.m: Action is performed in four ways by the activities of mind, speech, and body; / it is destroyed through those very [expounding acts] performed as their remedies."

3.7.s:
indra uvāca
āsavasya tu kiṃ rūpaṃ ko doṣaḥ kaścavā guṇaḥ /
annaṃ doṣakaraṃ kiṃ tu tanme vistarato vada //
3.7.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
आसवस्य तु किं रूपं को दोषः कश्चवा गुणः ।
अन्नं दोषकरं किं तु तन्मे विस्तरतो वद ॥
3.7.m: Indra said: / "What is the nature of liquor, what is its fault, and what is its virtue? / And what food produces fault? Tell me that in detail."

3.7.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
paiṣṭikaṃ tālajaṃ kairaṃ mādhūkaṃ guḍasaṃbhavam /
kramānnyūnataraṃ pāpaṃ tadarddhārddhārddhatastathā //
3.7.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
पैष्टिकं तालजं कैरं माधूकं गुडसंभवम् ।
क्रमान्न्यूनतरं पापं तदर्द्धार्द्धार्द्धतस्तथा ॥
3.7.m: Bṛhaspati said: / "[Liquor] made from meal, from palm, from coconut, from madhūka flowers, and that produced from molasses: / the sin is progressively lesser, by half, half, and half again.

3.7.s:
kṣatriyāditrivarṇānāmāsavaṃ peyamucyate /
strīṇāmapi tṛtīyādi peyaṃ syādbrāhmaṇīṃ vinā //
3.7.d:
क्षत्रियादित्रिवर्णानामासवं पेयमुच्यते ।
स्त्रीणामपि तृतीयादि पेयं स्याद्ब्राह्मणीं विना ॥
3.7.m: For the three classes beginning with the Kṣatriya, liquor is said to be drinkable. / For women too, beginning from the third, it may be drinkable, except for a Brahmin woman.

3.7.s:
patihīnā ca kanyā ca tyajedṛtumatī tathā /
abhartṛsannidhau nārī madyaṃ pibati lolupā //
3.7.d:
पतिहीना च कन्या च त्यजेदृतुमती तथा ।
अभर्तृसन्निधौ नारी मद्यं पिबति लोलुपा ॥
3.7.m: A woman without a husband, an unmarried girl, and one in her menses should abandon it. / A greedy woman who drinks liquor in the absence of her husband

3.7.s: unmādinīti sākhyātā tāṃ tyajedantyajāmiva //
3.7.d: उन्मादिनीति साख्याता तां त्यजेदन्त्यजामिव ॥
3.7.m: is proclaimed 'mad'; one should abandon her like an outcaste.

3.7.s:
daśāṣṭaṣaṭcatasrastu dvijātīnāmayaṃ bhavet /
strīṇāṃ madyaṃ tadarddhaṃ syātpādaṃ syādbhartṛsaṅgame //
3.7.d:
दशाष्टषट्चतस्रस्तु द्विजातीनामयं भवेत् ।
स्त्रीणां मद्यं तदर्द्धं स्यात्पादं स्याद्भर्तृसङ्गमे ॥
3.7.m: Ten, eight, six, and four [measures] are for the twice-born; / for women, liquor should be half of that, and a quarter when uniting with the husband.

3.7.s:
madyaṃ pītvā dvijo mohātkṛcchracāndrāyamaṃ caret /
japeccāyutagāyatrīṃ jātavedasameva vā //
3.7.d:
मद्यं पीत्वा द्विजो मोहात्कृच्छ्रचान्द्रायमं चरेत् ।
जपेच्चायुतगायत्रीं जातवेदसमेव वा ॥
3.7.m: A twice-born who drinks liquor through delusion should perform the Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa penances, / and should mutter the Gāyatrī ten thousand times, or the Jātavedas verse.

3.7.s:
ambikā hṛdayaṃ vāpi japecchuddho bhavennaraḥ /
kṣatriyo 'pi trivarṇānāṃ dvijādardhor'dhataḥ kramāt //
3.7.d:
अम्बिका हृदयं वापि जपेच्छुद्धो भवेन्नरः ।
क्षत्रियो ऽपि त्रिवर्णानां द्विजादर्धोर्ऽधतः क्रमात् ॥
3.7.m: Or a man muttering the Ambikāhṛdaya will become purified. / A Kṣatriya also, among the three classes, [requires] half and half progressively from the twice-born.

3.7.s:
strīṇāmardhārdhakḷptiḥ syātkārayedvā dvijairapi /
antarjale sahasraṃ vā japecchuddhimavāpnuyāt //
3.7.d:
स्त्रीणामर्धार्धकॢप्तिः स्यात्कारयेद्वा द्विजैरपि ।
अन्तर्जले सहस्रं वा जपेच्छुद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
3.7.m: For women, there should be an allotment of half of half, or they should have it performed by twice-born; / or, muttering a thousand times submerged in water, one will attain purity.

3.7.s:
lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī gaurī caṇḍikā tripurāṃbikā /
bhairavo bhairavī kālī mahāśāstrī ca mātaraḥ //
3.7.d:
लक्ष्मीः सरस्वती गौरी चण्डिका त्रिपुरांबिका ।
भैरवो भैरवी काली महाशास्त्री च मातरः ॥
3.7.m: Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Gaurī, Caṇḍikā, Tripurāmbikā, / Bhairava, Bhairavī, Kālī, Mahāśāstrī, and the Mothers,

3.7.s:
anyāśca śaktayastāsāṃ pūjane madhu śasyate /
brāhmaṇastu vinā tena yajedvedāṅgapāragaḥ //
3.7.d:
अन्याश्च शक्तयस्तासां पूजने मधु शस्यते ।
ब्राह्मणस्तु विना तेन यजेद्वेदाङ्गपारगः ॥
3.7.m: and other Śaktis: in worshipping them, liquor is praised. / But a Brahmin who has mastered the Vedāṅgas should worship without it.

3.7.s:
tanniveditamaśnantastadananyāstadātmakāḥ /
tāsāṃ pravāhā gacchanti nirlepāste parāṃ gatim //
3.7.d:
तन्निवेदितमश्नन्तस्तदनन्यास्तदात्मकाः ।
तासां प्रवाहा गच्छन्ति निर्लेपास्ते परां गतिम् ॥
3.7.m: Eating what has been offered to them, devoted to no other, identifying with them, / their streams, undefiled, go to the supreme state.

3.7.s:
kṛtasyākhilapāpasya jñānato 'jñānato 'pi vā /
prāyaścittamidaṃ proktaṃ parāśakteḥ padasmṛtiḥ //
3.7.d:
कृतस्याखिलपापस्य ज्ञानतो ऽज्ञानतो ऽपि वा ।
प्रायश्चित्तमिदं प्रोक्तं पराशक्तेः पदस्मृतिः ॥
3.7.m: For all sin committed, whether knowingly or unknowingly, / this is declared the expiation: remembrance of the supreme Śakti's feet.

3.7.s:
anabhyarcya parāṃ śaktiṃ pibenmadyaṃ tu yo 'dhamaḥ /
raurave narake 'bdaṃ tu nivasedbrindusaṃkhyayā //
3.7.d:
अनभ्यर्च्य परां शक्तिं पिबेन्मद्यं तु यो ऽधमः ।
रौरवे नरके ऽब्दं तु निवसेद्ब्रिन्दुसंख्यया ॥
3.7.m: The vile person who drinks liquor without worshipping the supreme Śakti / will dwell in the Raurava hell for a year for every drop.

3.7.s:
bhogecchayā tu yo madyaṃ pibetsa mānuṣādhamaḥ /
prāyaścitaṃ na caivāsya śilāgnipatanādṛte //
3.7.d:
भोगेच्छया तु यो मद्यं पिबेत्स मानुषाधमः ।
प्रायश्चितं न चैवास्य शिलाग्निपतनादृते ॥
3.7.m: The vile man who drinks liquor out of a desire for pleasure / has no expiation other than falling into fire upon a rock.

3.7.s:
dvijo mohānna tu pibetsnehādvā kāmato 'pi vā /
anugrahācca mahatāmanutāpācca karmaṇaḥ //
3.7.d:
द्विजो मोहान्न तु पिबेत्स्नेहाद्वा कामतो ऽपि वा ।
अनुग्रहाच्च महतामनुतापाच्च कर्मणः ॥
3.7.m: A twice-born must not drink through delusion, affection, or desire. / Through the grace of the great and repentance for the deed,

3.7.s:
arcanācca parāśakteryamaiśca niyamairapi /
cāndrāyaṇena kṛcchreṇa dinasaṃkhyākṛtena ca /
śuddhyecca brāhmaṇo doṣāddviguṇādbuddhipūrvataḥ //
iti brahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne steyapānakathanaṃ nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.7.d:
अर्चनाच्च पराशक्तेर्यमैश्च नियमैरपि ।
चान्द्रायणेन कृच्छ्रेण दिनसंख्याकृतेन च ।
शुद्ध्येच्च ब्राह्मणो दोषाद्द्विगुणाद्बुद्धिपूर्वतः ॥
इति ब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने स्तेयपानकथनं नाम सप्तमो ऽध्यायः
3.7.m:
and through worshipping the supreme Śakti, through restraints and observances, / through Cāndrāyaṇa, Kṛcchra, and rites measured by number of days, / a Brahmin will be purified from the fault, which is double if done intentionally.

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Discussion of Theft and Drinking," in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

3.8.s:
indra uvāca
agamyāgamanaṃ kiṃ vā ko doṣaḥ kā ca niṣkṛtiḥ /
etanme muniśārdūla vistarādvaktumarhasi //
3.8.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
अगम्यागमनं किं वा को दोषः का च निष्कृतिः ।
एतन्मे मुनिशार्दूल विस्तराद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
3.8.m: Indra said: / "What is intercourse with forbidden women, what is the fault, and what is the expiation? / You ought to tell me this at length, O tiger among sages."

3.8.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
agamyāgamanaṃ nāma mātṛsvasṛgurustriyaḥ /
mātulasya priyā ceti gatvemā nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ //
3.8.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
अगम्यागमनं नाम मातृस्वसृगुरुस्त्रियः ।
मातुलस्य प्रिया चेति गत्वेमा नास्ति निष्कृतिः ॥
3.8.m: Bṛhaspati said: / "Intercourse with forbidden women means the mother, the sister, the teacher's wife, / and the maternal uncle's beloved; having approached these, there is no expiation.

3.8.s:
mātṛsaṅge tu yadaghaṃ tadeva svasṛsaṅgame /
gurustrīsaṃgame tadvadguravo bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ //
3.8.d:
मातृसङ्गे तु यदघं तदेव स्वसृसङ्गमे ।
गुरुस्त्रीसंगमे तद्वद्गुरवो बहवः स्मृताः ॥
3.8.m: Whatever sin is in union with the mother, that very same is in union with the sister; / likewise in union with the teacher's wife; many kinds of teachers are recorded.

3.8.s:
brahmopadeśamārabhya yāvadvedāntadarśanam /
ekena vakṣyate yena sa mahāgururucyate //
3.8.d:
ब्रह्मोपदेशमारभ्य यावद्वेदान्तदर्शनम् ।
एकेन वक्ष्यते येन स महागुरुरुच्यते ॥
3.8.m: He by whom instruction in the Brahman is spoken beginning from initiation / up to the realization of the Vedānta, he is called a supreme teacher.

3.8.s:
brahmopadeśamekatra vedaśāstrāṇyathaikataḥ /
ācāryaḥ sa tu vijñeyastadekaikāstu deśikāḥ //
3.8.d:
ब्रह्मोपदेशमेकत्र वेदशास्त्राण्यथैकतः ।
आचार्यः स तु विज्ञेयस्तदेकैकास्तु देशिकाः ॥
3.8.m: One who teaches the Brahman in one part, or the Vedas and scriptures in one part, / is to be known as an ācārya; and those teaching each individual subject are instructors.

3.8.s:
gurorātmāntameva syādāyāryasya priyāgame /
dvādaśābdaṃ caretkṛccha3mekaikaṃ tu ṣaḍabdataḥ //
3.8.d:
गुरोरात्मान्तमेव स्यादायार्यस्य प्रियागमे ।
द्वादशाब्दं चरेत्कृच्छ3मेकैकं तु षडब्दतः ॥
3.8.m: For approaching the guru's beloved, it ends only with one's life; for approaching the ācārya's beloved, / one should perform the Kṛcchra penance for twelve years, and for each [instructor's wife] for six years.

3.8.s:
mātulasya priyāṃ gatvā ṣaḍabdaṃ kṛcchramācaret /
brāhmaṇastu sajātīyāṃ pramadāṃ yadi gacchati //
3.8.d:
मातुलस्य प्रियां गत्वा षडब्दं कृच्छ्रमाचरेत् ।
ब्राह्मणस्तु सजातीयां प्रमदां यदि गच्छति ॥
3.8.m: Having approached the maternal uncle's beloved, one should perform the Kṛcchra penance for six years. / If a Brahmin approaches a woman of his own caste,

3.8.s:
upoṣitastrirātraṃ tu prāṇāyāmaśataṃ caret /
kulaṭāṃ tu sajātīyāṃ trirātreṇa viśudhyati //
3.8.d:
उपोषितस्त्रिरात्रं तु प्राणायामशतं चरेत् ।
कुलटां तु सजातीयां त्रिरात्रेण विशुध्यति ॥
3.8.m: fasting for three nights, he should perform a hundred breath-controls. / Approaching an unchaste woman of his own caste, he is purified in three nights.

3.8.s:
pañcāhātkṣatriyāṅgatvā saptāhā dvaiśyajāmapi /
cakrīkirātakaivartakarmakārādiyoṣitaḥ //
3.8.d:
पञ्चाहात्क्षत्रियाङ्गत्वा सप्ताहा द्वैश्यजामपि ।
चक्रीकिरातकैवर्तकर्मकारादियोषितः ॥
3.8.m: Having approached a Kṣatriya woman, [purification is] in five days; a Vaiśya woman, in seven days; / for the wives of oil-millers, Kirātas, fishermen, and laborers,

3.8.s:
śuddhiḥ syāddvādaśāhena dharāśaktyarcanena ca /
anantyajāṃ brāhmaṇo gatvā pramādādabdataḥ śuciḥ //
3.8.d:
शुद्धिः स्याद्द्वादशाहेन धराशक्त्यर्चनेन च ।
अनन्त्यजां ब्राह्मणो गत्वा प्रमादादब्दतः शुचिः ॥
3.8.m: purification will be in twelve days, along with the worship of the earth-power. / A Brahmin who has approached an outcaste woman through negligence is purified in a year.

3.8.s:
devadāsī brahmadāsī svatantrāśūdradāsikā /
dāsī caturvidhā proktā dve cādye kṣatriyāsame //
3.8.d:
देवदासी ब्रह्मदासी स्वतन्त्राशूद्रदासिका ।
दासी चतुर्विधा प्रोक्ता द्वे चाद्ये क्षत्रियासमे ॥
3.8.m:
A servant of the gods (devadāsī), a servant of Brahmins (brahmadāsī), an independent woman (svatantrā), and a Śūdra's servant woman:
a servant woman is declared to be of four kinds; the first two are equal to a Kṣatriya woman.

3.8.s:
anyāveśyāṅganātulyā tadanyā hīnajātivat /
ātmadāsīṃ dvijo mohāduktārthe doṣamāpnuyāt //
3.8.d:
अन्यावेश्याङ्गनातुल्या तदन्या हीनजातिवत् ।
आत्मदासीं द्विजो मोहादुक्तार्थे दोषमाप्नुयात् ॥
3.8.m:
Another is equal to a courtesan, and the other is like a woman of low caste.
If a twice-born man, through delusion, [approaches] his own female servant, he incurs the sin according to what has been stated.

3.8.s:
svastrīmṛtumatīṃ gatvā prājāpatyaṃ caredvratam /
dviguṇena parāṃ nārīṃ caturbhiḥ kṣatriyāṅganām //
3.8.d:
स्वस्त्रीमृतुमतीं गत्वा प्राजापत्यं चरेद्व्रतम् ।
द्विगुणेन परां नारीं चतुर्भिः क्षत्रियाङ्गनाम् ॥
3.8.m:
Having approached one's own wife in her fertile period [unlawfully], one should perform the Prājāpatya penance;
[approaching] another's woman, [a penance] twice as much; a Kṣatriya woman, four times [as much];

3.8.s:
aṣṭabhirvaiśyanārīṃ ca śūdrāṃ ṣauḍaśabhistathā /
dvātriṃśatā saṃkarajāṃ veśyāṃ śūdrāmivācaret //
3.8.d:
अष्टभिर्वैश्यनारीं च शूद्रां षौडशभिस्तथा ।
द्वात्रिंशता संकरजां वेश्यां शूद्रामिवाचरेत् ॥
3.8.m:
eight times for a Vaiśya woman, and sixteen times for a Śūdra woman;
thirty-two times for a mixed-caste woman; and for a courtesan, one should perform [the penance] as for a Śūdra woman.

3.8.s:
rajasvalāṃ tu yo bhāryāṃ mohato gantumicchati /
snātvānyavastrasaṃyuktamuktārthenaiva śudhyati //
3.8.d:
रजस्वलां तु यो भार्यां मोहतो गन्तुमिच्छति ।
स्नात्वान्यवस्त्रसंयुक्तमुक्तार्थेनैव शुध्यति ॥
3.8.m:
He who through delusion wishes to approach his menstruating wife,
becomes purified only by bathing, putting on other clothes, and according to what has been stated.

3.8.s:
upoṣya taccheṣadinaṃ snātvā karma samācaret /
tathaivānyāṅganāṃ gatvā taduktārthaṃ samācaret //
3.8.d:
उपोष्य तच्छेषदिनं स्नात्वा कर्म समाचरेत् ।
तथैवान्याङ्गनां गत्वा तदुक्तार्थं समाचरेत् ॥
3.8.m:
Fasting for the remainder of that day and having bathed, he should perform ritual action;
likewise, having approached another woman, he should perform what has been prescribed for that.

3.8.s:
pitroranujñayā kanyāṃ yo gacchedvidhinā vinā /
trirātropoṣaṇācchuddhistāmevodvāhayettadā //
3.8.d:
पित्रोरनुज्ञया कन्यां यो गच्छेद्विधिना विना ।
त्रिरात्रोपोषणाच्छुद्धिस्तामेवोद्वाहयेत्तदा ॥
3.8.m:
He who approaches a maiden with the permission of her parents, but without the [proper] rite,
becomes purified by fasting for three nights; then he should marry that very girl.

3.8.s:
kanyāṃ dattvā tu yo 'nyasmai dattā yaścānuyacchati /
pitroranujñayā pādadinārdhena viśudhyati //
3.8.d:
कन्यां दत्त्वा तु यो ऽन्यस्मै दत्ता यश्चानुयच्छति ।
पित्रोरनुज्ञया पाददिनार्धेन विशुध्यति ॥
3.8.m:
He who, having given a maiden to one, [gives her] to another, and he who accepts the one who has been given,
becomes purified in half of a quarter-day (three muhūrtas) with the permission of the parents.

3.8.s:
jñātaḥ pitṛbhyāṃ yo māsaṃ kanyābhāve tu gacchati /
vṛṣalaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ sarvakarmabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
3.8.d:
ज्ञातः पितृभ्यां यो मासं कन्याभावे तु गच्छति ।
वृषलः स तु विज्ञेयः सर्वकर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥
3.8.m:
He who is known by the parents, but who approaches [another woman] for a month in the absence of a maiden,
is to be known as an outcaste (vṛṣala), excluded from all religious rites.

3.8.s:
jñātaḥ pitṛbhyāṃ yo gatvā paroḍhāṃ tadvināśane /
vidhavā jāyate neyaṃ pūrvagantāramāpnuyāt //
3.8.d:
ज्ञातः पितृभ्यां यो गत्वा परोढां तद्विनाशने ।
विधवा जायते नेयं पूर्वगन्तारमाप्नुयात् ॥
3.8.m:
He who approaches another's married wife with the parents' knowledge, upon his destruction
she does not become a widow, [but] should go to the previous approacher.

3.8.s:
anugrahāddvijātīnāmudvāhavidhinā tathā /
tyāgakarmāṇi kurvīta śrautasmārtādikāni ca //
3.8.d:
अनुग्रहाद्द्विजातीनामुद्वाहविधिना तथा ।
त्यागकर्माणि कुर्वीत श्रौतस्मार्तादिकानि च ॥
3.8.m:
By the grace of the twice-born, and according to the rites of marriage,
he should perform the rites of abandonment as well as those ordained by the Śruti and Smṛti.

3.8.s:
ādāvudvāhitā vāpi tadvināśe 'nyadaḥ pitā /
bhogecchoḥ sādhanaṃ sā tu na yegyākhilakarmasu //
3.8.d:
आदावुद्वाहिता वापि तद्विनाशे ऽन्यदः पिता ।
भोगेच्छोः साधनं सा तु न येग्याखिलकर्मसु ॥
3.8.m:
Even if she was married in the beginning, upon his death, her father gives her to another;
she is a means of enjoyment for one desiring pleasure, but she is not fit for all sacred rites.

3.8.s:
brahmādipipīlakāntaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
pañcabhūtātmakaṃ proktaṃ caturvāsanayānvitam //
3.8.d:
ब्रह्मादिपिपीलकान्तं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
पञ्चभूतात्मकं प्रोक्तं चतुर्वासनयान्वितम् ॥
3.8.m:
From Brahmā down to an ant, the world of the immovable and movable
is declared to consist of the five elements and to be accompanied by four innate drives:

3.8.s:
janmādyāhāramathananidrābhītyaśca sarvadā /
āhāreṇa vinā janturnāhāro madanātsmṛtaḥ //
3.8.d:
जन्माद्याहारमथननिद्राभीत्यश्च सर्वदा ।
आहारेण विना जन्तुर्नाहारो मदनात्स्मृतः ॥
3.8.m:
Birth, food, sexual intercourse (churning), sleep, and fear at all times.
Without food a creature cannot exist; [and] food is held to proceed from desire.

3.8.s:
dustaro madanastasmātsarveṣāṃ prāṇināmapi /
punnārīrūpavatkṛtvā madananenaiva viśvasṛk //
3.8.d:
दुस्तरो मदनस्तस्मात्सर्वेषां प्राणिनामपि ।
पुन्नारीरूपवत्कृत्वा मदननेनैव विश्वसृक् ॥
3.8.m:
Therefore, desire is insurmountable for all living beings as well.
Having made them in the form of male and female, by desire alone the creator of the universe

3.8.s:
pravṛttimakarodādau sṛṣṭisthitilayātmikām /
tatpravṛttyā pravartante tannivṛttyākṣayāṃ gatim //
3.8.d:
प्रवृत्तिमकरोदादौ सृष्टिस्थितिलयात्मिकाम् ।
तत्प्रवृत्त्या प्रवर्तन्ते तन्निवृत्त्याक्षयां गतिम् ॥
3.8.m:
performed at the beginning engagement [in action] consisting of creation, preservation, and dissolution;
by that engagement beings engage, [and] by its cessation they attain an imperishable state.

3.8.s:
pravṛttyaiva yathā muktiṃ prāpnuyurye na dhīyutāḥ /
tadrahasyaṃ tadopāyaṃ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam //
3.8.d:
प्रवृत्त्यैव यथा मुक्तिं प्राप्नुयुर्ये न धीयुताः ।
तद्रहस्यं तदोपायं शृणु वक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम् ॥
3.8.m:
How those who are not endowed with [transcendental] intellect may attain liberation through engagement itself,
listen to that secret and its means; I shall describe it now.

3.8.s:
sarvātmako vāsudevaḥ puruṣastu purātanaḥ /
iyaṃ hi mūlaprakṛtirlakṣmīḥ sarvajagatprasūḥ //
3.8.d:
सर्वात्मको वासुदेवः पुरुषस्तु पुरातनः ।
इयं हि मूलप्रकृतिर्लक्ष्मीः सर्वजगत्प्रसूः ॥
3.8.m:
Vāsudeva, the ancient Puruṣa, is the soul of all;
this indeed is primordial nature (mūlaprakṛti), Lakṣmī, the mother of the entire universe.

3.8.s:
pañcāpañcātmatṛptyarthaṃ mathanaṃ kriyatetarām /
evaṃ mantrānubhāvātsyānmathanaṃ kriyate yadi //
3.8.d:
पञ्चापञ्चात्मतृप्त्यर्थं मथनं क्रियतेतराम् ।
एवं मन्त्रानुभावात्स्यान्मथनं क्रियते यदि ॥
3.8.m:
The churning is performed especially for the satisfaction of the five elements.
If churning is performed thus by the power of the mantra,

3.8.s: tāvubhau mantrakarmāṇau na doṣo vidyate tayoḥ //
3.8.d: तावुभौ मन्त्रकर्माणौ न दोषो विद्यते तयोः ॥
3.8.m: both of them become performers of mantra action, [and] no fault exists in the two of them.

3.8.s:
tapobalavatāmetatkevalānāmadhogatiḥ /
svastrīviṣaya evedaṃ tayorapi vidherbalāt //
3.8.d:
तपोबलवतामेतत्केवलानामधोगतिः ।
स्वस्त्रीविषय एवेदं तयोरपि विधेर्बलात् ॥
3.8.m:
This belongs to those possessing the power of austerity; for ordinary men there is a downward fall.
This applies only to one's own wife, for both of them, by the power of injunction.

3.8.s:
parasparātmyaikyahṛdordevyā bhaktyārdracetasoḥ /
tayorapi manākcenna niṣiddhadivaseṣvagham //
3.8.d:
परस्परात्म्यैक्यहृदोर्देव्या भक्त्यार्द्रचेतसोः ।
तयोरपि मनाक्चेन्न निषिद्धदिवसेष्वघम् ॥
3.8.m:
For those two whose hearts are united in mutual oneness, whose minds are softened by devotion to the Goddess,
even slightly, if it is not on forbidden days, there is no sin.

3.8.s:
iyamaṃbā jagaddhātrī puruṣo 'yaṃ sadāśivaḥ /
pañcaviṃśatitattvānāṃ prītaye mathyate 'dhunā //
3.8.d:
इयमंबा जगद्धात्री पुरुषो ऽयं सदाशिवः ।
पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वानां प्रीतये मथ्यते ऽधुना ॥
3.8.m:
This is the Mother, the supporter of the world; this is Puruṣa, Sadāśiva;
now churning is performed for the gratification of the twenty-five principles.

3.8.s:
etanmantrānubhāvācca mathanaṃ kriyate yadi /
tāvubhau puṇyakarmāṇau na doṣo vidyate tayoḥ //
3.8.d:
एतन्मन्त्रानुभावाच्च मथनं क्रियते यदि ।
तावुभौ पुण्यकर्माणौ न दोषो विद्यते तयोः ॥
3.8.m:
And if churning is performed through the power of this mantra,
both of them become performers of meritorious action; no fault exists in the two of them.

3.8.s:
idaṃ ca śṛṇu devendra rahasyaṃ paramaṃ mahat /
sarveṣāmeva pāpānāṃ yaugapadyena nāśanam //
3.8.d:
इदं च शृणु देवेन्द्र रहस्यं परमं महत् ।
सर्वेषामेव पापानां यौगपद्येन नाशनम् ॥
3.8.m:
Listen also to this, O lord of gods, the supreme, great secret,
the simultaneous destroyer of all sins whatsoever.

3.8.s:
bhaktiśraddhāsamāyuktaḥ snātvāntarjalasaṃsthitaḥ /
aṣṭottarasahasraṃ tu japetpañcadaśākṣarīm //
3.8.d:
भक्तिश्रद्धासमायुक्तः स्नात्वान्तर्जलसंस्थितः ।
अष्टोत्तरसहस्रं तु जपेत्पञ्चदशाक्षरीम् ॥
3.8.m:
Endowed with devotion and faith, having bathed and standing in water,
one should recite the fifteen-syllabled mantra one thousand and eight times.

3.8.s:
ārādhya ca parāṃ śaktiṃ mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ /
tena naśyanti pāpāni kalpakoṭikṛtānyapi /
sarvāpadbhyo vimucyeta sarvābhīṣṭaṃ ca vindati //
3.8.d:
आराध्य च परां शक्तिं मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ।
तेन नश्यन्ति पापानि कल्पकोटिकृतान्यपि ।
सर्वापद्भ्यो विमुच्येत सर्वाभीष्टं च विन्दति ॥

3.8.s:
indra uvāca
bhagavansarvadharmajña sarvabhūtahite rata /
saṃyogajasya pāpasya viśeṣaṃ vaktumarhasi //
3.8.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ सर्वभूतहिते रत ।
संयोगजस्य पापस्य विशेषं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
3.8.m:
Indra said:
O blessed one, knower of all righteousness, devoted to the welfare of all beings,
you ought to tell the distinction regarding the sin born of contact.

3.8.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
saṃyogajaṃ tu yatpāpaṃ taccaturdhā nigadyate /
kartā pradhānaḥ sahakṛnnimitto 'numataḥ kramāt //
3.8.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
संयोगजं तु यत्पापं तच्चतुर्धा निगद्यते ।
कर्ता प्रधानः सहकृन्निमित्तो ऽनुमतः क्रमात् ॥
3.8.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
The sin born of contact is said to be of four kinds:
the direct perpetrator, the instigator, the accomplice, and the approver, in order.

3.8.s: kramāddaśāṃśato 'ghaṃ syācchuddhiḥ pūrvoktamārgataḥ //
3.8.d: क्रमाद्दशांशतो ऽघं स्याच्छुद्धिः पूर्वोक्तमार्गतः ॥
3.8.m: The sin is reduced by a tenth part respectively, and purification is by the path stated previously.

3.8.s:
madyaṃ kalañjaṃ niryāsaṃ chatrākaṃ gṛñjanaṃ tathā /
laśunaṃ ca kaliṅgaṃ ca mahākośātakīṃ tathā //
3.8.d:
मद्यं कलञ्जं निर्यासं छत्राकं गृञ्जनं तथा ।
लशुनं च कलिङ्गं च महाकोशातकीं तथा ॥
3.8.m:
Liquor, red garlic (kalañja), exudations, mushrooms, carrots,
garlic, kaliṅga, and the large loofah (mahākośātakī),

3.8.s:
biṃbīṃ ca kavakaṃ caiva hastinīṃ śiśulaṃbikām /
auduṃbaraṃ ca vārtākaṃ katakaṃ bilvamallikā //
3.8.d:
बिंबीं च कवकं चैव हस्तिनीं शिशुलंबिकाम् ।
औदुंबरं च वार्ताकं कतकं बिल्वमल्लिका ॥
3.8.m:
biṃbī, fungi, hastinī, hanging gourds,
figs, brinjals, kataka, and bilva-jasmine:

3.8.s:
kramāddaśaguṇaṃ nyūnamaghameṣāṃ vinirdiśet /
puragrāmāṅgavaiśyāṅgaveśyopāyanavikrayī //
3.8.d:
क्रमाद्दशगुणं न्यूनमघमेषां विनिर्दिशेत् ।
पुरग्रामाङ्गवैश्याङ्गवेश्योपायनविक्रयी ॥
3.8.m:
one should indicate the sin of these as being tenfold less in succession.
One who sells women of town, village, or Vaiśya caste, or courtesans as gifts,

3.8.s:
sevakaḥ purasaṃsthaśca kugrāmastho 'bhiśastakaḥ /
vaidyo vaikhānasaḥ śaivo nārījīvo 'nnavikrayī //
3.8.d:
सेवकः पुरसंस्थश्च कुग्रामस्थो ऽभिशस्तकः ।
वैद्यो वैखानसः शैवो नारीजीवो ऽन्नविक्रयी ॥
3.8.m:
a servant, a resident of a town, one residing in a wretched village, an accuser,
a physician, a Vaikhānasa, a Śaiva, one who lives off women, a food seller,

3.8.s:
śastrajīvī parivrāṭ ca vaidikācāranindakaḥ /
kramāddaśaguṇānnyūnameṣāmannādane bhavet //
3.8.d:
शस्त्रजीवी परिव्राट् च वैदिकाचारनिन्दकः ।
क्रमाद्दशगुणान्न्यूनमेषामन्नादने भवेत् ॥
3.8.m:
one living by weapons, a wandering mendicant, and a reviler of Vedic practice:
in eating the food of these, [the sin] decreases tenfold successively.

3.8.s:
svatantraṃ tailakḷptaṃ tu hyuktārthaṃ pāpamādiśet /
taireva dṛṣṭaṃ tadbhuktamuktapāpaṃ vinirdiśet //
3.8.d:
स्वतन्त्रं तैलकॢप्तं तु ह्युक्तार्थं पापमादिशेत् ।
तैरेव दृष्टं तद्भुक्तमुक्तपापं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
3.8.m:
Food prepared independently with oil carries the sin according to what has been said;
eaten when seen by those very persons, one should specify the stated sin.

3.8.s:
brahmakṣatraviśāṃ caiva saśūdrāṇāṃ yathaudanam /
tailapakvamadṛṣṭaṃ ca bhuñjanpādamaghaṃ bhavet //
3.8.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां चैव सशूद्राणां यथौदनम् ।
तैलपक्वमदृष्टं च भुञ्जन्पादमघं भवेत् ॥
3.8.m:
Eating the rice of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas, along with Śūdras,
cooked in oil and unseen, incurs a quarter of the sin.

3.8.s:
dvijātmadāsīkḷptaṃ ca tayā dṛṣṭe tadardhake /
veśyāyāstu tripādaṃ syāttathā dṛṣṭe tadodane //
3.8.d:
द्विजात्मदासीकॢप्तं च तया दृष्टे तदर्धके ।
वेश्यायास्तु त्रिपादं स्यात्तथा दृष्टे तदोदने ॥
3.8.m:
When prepared by a twice-born's own female servant, if seen by her, it is half of that;
for a courtesan's [food], it is three quarters, when her rice is likewise seen.

3.8.s:
śūdrāvatsyāttu gopānnaṃ vinā gavyacatuṣṭayam /
tailājyaguḍasaṃyuktaṃ pakvaṃ vaiśyānna duṣyati //
3.8.d:
शूद्रावत्स्यात्तु गोपान्नं विना गव्यचतुष्टयम् ।
तैलाज्यगुडसंयुक्तं पक्वं वैश्यान्न दुष्यति ॥
3.8.m:
The cowherd's food is like a Śūdra's, except for the four products of the cow;
food mixed with oil, clarified butter, or molasses and cooked is like a Vaiśya's and does not defile.

3.8.s: vaiśyāvadbrāhmaṇī bhraṣṭā tayā dṛṣṭena kiñcana //
3.8.d: वैश्यावद्ब्राह्मणी भ्रष्टा तया दृष्टेन किञ्चन ॥
3.8.m: A fallen Brahmin woman is like a Vaiśya woman; nothing [is spoiled] by her glance.

3.8.s:
bruvasyānnaṃ dvijo bhuktvā prāṇāyāmaśataṃ caret /
athavāntarjale japtvādrupadāṃ vā trivārakam //
3.8.d:
ब्रुवस्यान्नं द्विजो भुक्त्वा प्राणायामशतं चरेत् ।
अथवान्तर्जले जप्त्वाद्रुपदां वा त्रिवारकम् ॥
3.8.m:
Having eaten the food of a fraudulent man (bruva), a twice-born should perform a hundred breath-controls,
or recite the Drupadā mantra three times while standing in water.

3.8.s:
idaṃ viṣṇustryaṃbakaṃ vā tthaivāntarjale japet /
upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ tataḥ pāpādviśudhyati //
3.8.d:
इदं विष्णुस्त्र्यंबकं वा त्थैवान्तर्जले जपेत् ।
उपोष्य रजनीमेकां ततः पापाद्विशुध्यति ॥
3.8.m:
Or he should recite the mantra 'idaṃ viṣṇuḥ' or the Tryambaka hymn in the water in the same way;
having fasted for one night, he is thereupon purified from the sin.

3.8.s:
athavā prokṣayedannamabliṅgaiḥ pāvamānikaiḥ /
annasūktaṃ japitvā tu bhṛgurvai vāruṇīti ca //
3.8.d:
अथवा प्रोक्षयेदन्नमब्लिङ्गैः पावमानिकैः ।
अन्नसूक्तं जपित्वा तु भृगुर्वै वारुणीति च ॥
3.8.m:
Or he should sprinkle the food with the water hymns and the purifying verses (pāvamānī),
and having recited the Annasūkta and the hymn 'bhṛgurvai vāruṇiḥ',

3.8.s:
brahmārpaṇamiti ślokaṃ japtvā niyamamāśritaḥ /
upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ tataḥ śuddho bhaviṣyati //
3.8.d:
ब्रह्मार्पणमिति श्लोकं जप्त्वा नियममाश्रितः ।
उपोष्य रजनीमेकां ततः शुद्धो भविष्यति ॥
3.8.m:
and reciting the verse 'brahmārpaṇam' while observing self-restraint,
having fasted for one night, he will thereupon become pure.

3.8.s:
strī bhuktvā tu bruvādyannamekādyānbhojaye ddvijān /
āpadi brāhmaṇo hyeṣāmannaṃ bhuktvā na doṣabhāk //
3.8.d:
स्त्री भुक्त्वा तु ब्रुवाद्यन्नमेकाद्यान्भोजये द्द्विजान् ।
आपदि ब्राह्मणो ह्येषामन्नं भुक्त्वा न दोषभाक् ॥
3.8.m:
A woman who eats the food of a fraudulent man should feed one or more twice-born men;
in times of distress, a Brahmin who eats their food incurs no fault.

3.8.s:
idaṃ viṣṇuriti mantreṇa saptavārābhimantritam /
so 'haṃbhāvena taddhyātvā bhuktvā doṣairna lipyate //
3.8.d:
इदं विष्णुरिति मन्त्रेण सप्तवाराभिमन्त्रितम् ।
सो ऽहंभावेन तद्ध्यात्वा भुक्त्वा दोषैर्न लिप्यते ॥
3.8.m:
Consecrated seven times with the mantra 'idaṃ viṣṇuḥ',
meditating on it with the conviction 'I am He', eating it, he is not tainted by faults.

3.8.s:
athavā śaṅkaraṃ dhyāyañjaptvā traiyyaṃbakaṃ manum /
so 'haṃbhāvena tajjñānānna doṣaiḥ pravilipyate //
3.8.d:
अथवा शङ्करं ध्यायञ्जप्त्वा त्रैय्यंबकं मनुम् ।
सो ऽहंभावेन तज्ज्ञानान्न दोषैः प्रविलिप्यते ॥
3.8.m:
Or meditating upon Śaṅkara and reciting the Tryambaka mantra,
through knowledge of that with the conviction 'I am He', he is not at all tainted by faults.

3.8.s:
idaṃ rahasyaṃ devendra śṛṇuṣva vacanaṃ mama /
dhyātvā devīṃ parāṃ śaktiṃ japtvā pañcadaśākṣarīm //
3.8.d:
इदं रहस्यं देवेन्द्र शृणुष्व वचनं मम ।
ध्यात्वा देवीं परां शक्तिं जप्त्वा पञ्चदशाक्षरीम् ॥
3.8.m:
Listen to this secret, my word, O lord of gods:
having meditated upon the Goddess, the Supreme Śakti, and recited the fifteen-syllabled mantra,

3.8.s:
tanniveditabuddhyādau yo 'śnāti pratyahaṃ dvijaḥ /
nāsyānnadoṣajaṃ kiñcinna dāridrayabhayaṃ tathā //
3.8.d:
तन्निवेदितबुद्ध्यादौ यो ऽश्नाति प्रत्यहं द्विजः ।
नास्यान्नदोषजं किञ्चिन्न दारिद्रयभयं तथा ॥
3.8.m: The twice-born who eats daily, aware that it is first offered to her, / has no [affliction] arising from the fault of food, nor any fear of poverty.

3.8.s:
na vyādhijaṃ bhayaṃ tasya na ca śatrubhayaṃ tathā /
japato muktirevāsya sadā sarvatra maṅgalam //
3.8.d:
न व्याधिजं भयं तस्य न च शत्रुभयं तथा ।
जपतो मुक्तिरेवास्य सदा सर्वत्र मङ्गलम् ॥
3.8.m: He has no fear arising from disease, nor fear of enemies; / for one who recites [it], there is indeed liberation, and always good fortune everywhere.

3.8.s:
eṣa te kathitaḥ śakra pāpānāmapi vistaraḥ /
prāyaścittaṃ tathā teṣāṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne 'ṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.8.d:
एष ते कथितः शक्र पापानामपि विस्तरः ।
प्रायश्चित्तं तथा तेषां किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने ऽष्टमो ऽध्यायः
3.8.m:
This detailed account of sins has thus been related to you, Śakra, / as well as their expiation; what else do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the eighth chapter in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the final part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

3.9.s:
indra uvāca
bhagavansarva dharmajña trikālajñānavittama /
duṣkṛtaṃ tatpratīkāro bhavatā samyagīritaḥ //
3.9.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
भगवन्सर्व धर्मज्ञ त्रिकालज्ञानवित्तम ।
दुष्कृतं तत्प्रतीकारो भवता सम्यगीरितः ॥
3.9.m: Indra said: / Blessed lord, knower of all righteousness, best among those possessing knowledge of the three times, / the evil deed and its remedy have been well spoken by you.

3.9.s:
kena karmavipākena mamāpadi yamāgatā /
prāyaścittaṃ ca kiṃ tasya gadasva vadatāṃ vara //
3.9.d:
केन कर्मविपाकेन ममापदि यमागता ।
प्रायश्चित्तं च किं तस्य गदस्व वदतां वर ॥
3.9.m: By the fruition of what karma did this misfortune come upon me? / And what is its expiation? Tell [me], O best of speakers!

3.9.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
kāśyapasya tato jajñe dityāṃ danuriti smṛtaḥ /
kanyā rūpavatī nāma dhātre tāṃ pradadau pitā //
3.9.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
काश्यपस्य ततो जज्ञे दित्यां दनुरिति स्मृतः ।
कन्या रूपवती नाम धात्रे तां प्रददौ पिता ॥
3.9.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Then to Kaśyapa, by Ditī, was born one known as Danu; / the father gave the daughter named Rūpavatī to Dhātṛ.

3.9.s:
tasyāḥ putrastato jāto viśvarūpo mahādyutiḥ /
nārāyaṇaparo nityaṃ vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ //
3.9.d:
तस्याः पुत्रस्ततो जातो विश्वरूपो महाद्युतिः ।
नारायणपरो नित्यं वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ॥
3.9.m: From her was then born a son, Viśvarūpa of great splendor, / ever devoted to Nārāyaṇa, having crossed to the further shore of the Vedas and auxiliary sciences.

3.9.s:
tato daityeśvaro vavre bhṛguputraṃ purohitam /
bhavānadhikṛto rājye devānāmiva vāsavaḥ //
3.9.d:
ततो दैत्येश्वरो वव्रे भृगुपुत्रं पुरोहितम् ।
भवानधिकृतो राज्ये देवानामिव वासवः ॥
3.9.m: Then the lord of Daityas chose the son of Bhṛgu as priest: / 'You are appointed over the kingdom, like Vāsava over the gods.'

3.9.s:
tataḥ pūrve ca kāle tu sudharmāyāṃ tvayi sthite /
tvayā kaścitkṛtaḥ praśna ṛṣīṇāṃ sannidhau tadā //
3.9.d:
ततः पूर्वे च काले तु सुधर्मायां त्वयि स्थिते ।
त्वया कश्चित्कृतः प्रश्न ऋषीणां सन्निधौ तदा ॥
3.9.m: Then at an earlier time, while you were seated in the Sudharmā hall, / a question was posed by you then in the presence of the ṛṣis:

3.9.s:
saṃsārastīrthayātrā vā ko 'dhiko 'sti tayorgumaḥ /
vadantu tadviniścitya bhavanto madanugrahāt //
3.9.d:
संसारस्तीर्थयात्रा वा को ऽधिको ऽस्ति तयोर्गुमः ।
वदन्तु तद्विनिश्चित्य भवन्तो मदनुग्रहात् ॥
3.9.m: 'Samsara or pilgrimage to sacred places—which virtue of these two is greater? / Having determined that, may you speak out of favor toward me.'

3.9.s:
tatpraśnasyottaraṃ vaktuṃ te sarva upacakrire /
tatpūrvameva kathitaṃ mayā vidhibalena vai //
3.9.d:
तत्प्रश्नस्योत्तरं वक्तुं ते सर्व उपचक्रिरे ।
तत्पूर्वमेव कथितं मया विधिबलेन वै ॥
3.9.m: They all began to speak an answer to that question; / indeed, prior to them it was spoken by me by the force of destiny:

3.9.s:
tīrtha yātrā samadhikā saṃsārāditi ca drutam /
tacchrutvā te prakupitāḥ śepurmāmṛṣayo 'khilāḥ //
3.9.d:
तीर्थ यात्रा समधिका संसारादिति च द्रुतम् ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा ते प्रकुपिताः शेपुर्मामृषयो ऽखिलाः ॥
3.9.m: 'Pilgrimage to sacred places is far superior to samsara!' / Hearing that, all those ṛṣis became enraged and cursed me:

3.9.s:
karmabhūmiṃ vrajeḥ śīghraṃ dārirdyeṇa mitaiḥ sutaiḥ /
evaṃ prakupitaiḥ śaptaḥ khinnaḥ kāñcīṃ samāviśam //
3.9.d:
कर्मभूमिं व्रजेः शीघ्रं दारिर्द्येण मितैः सुतैः ।
एवं प्रकुपितैः शप्तः खिन्नः काञ्चीं समाविशम् ॥
3.9.m: 'Go quickly to the realm of action with poverty and few sons!' / Thus cursed by the enraged [ṛṣis], sorrowful, I entered Kāñcī.

3.9.s:
purīṃ purodhasā hīnāṃ vīkṣya cintākulātmanā /
bhavatā saha devaistu paurohityārthamādarāt //
3.9.d:
पुरीं पुरोधसा हीनां वीक्ष्य चिन्ताकुलात्मना ।
भवता सह देवैस्तु पौरोहित्यार्थमादरात् ॥
3.9.m: Seeing the city bereft of a family priest, with your mind agitated by worry, / for the sake of the priesthood, with respect, together with the gods,

3.9.s:
prārthito viśvarūpastu babhūva tapatāṃ varaḥ /
svasrīyo dānavānāṃ tu devānāṃ ca purohitaḥ //
3.9.d:
प्रार्थितो विश्वरूपस्तु बभूव तपतां वरः ।
स्वस्रीयो दानवानां तु देवानां च पुरोहितः ॥
3.9.m: you requested Viśvarūpa, the best of ascetics; / and he became the sister's son of the Dānavas and the priest of the gods.

3.9.s:
nātyarthama karodvairaṃ daityeṣvapi mahātapāḥ /
babhūvatustulyabalau tadā detyendravāsavau //
3.9.d:
नात्यर्थम करोद्वैरं दैत्येष्वपि महातपाः ।
बभूवतुस्तुल्यबलौ तदा देत्येन्द्रवासवौ ॥
3.9.m: The great ascetic did not harbor excessive hostility even toward the Daityas; / then the lord of Daityas and Vāsava became equal in strength.

3.9.s:
tatastvaṃ kupito rājansvaklīyaṃ dānaveśituḥ /
hantumicchannagāścāśu tapasaḥ sādhanaṃ vanam //
3.9.d:
ततस्त्वं कुपितो राजन्स्वक्लीयं दानवेशितुः ।
हन्तुमिच्छन्नगाश्चाशु तपसः साधनं वनम् ॥
3.9.m: Then you, O king, becoming angry and wishing to slay the sister's son of the Dānava lord, / quickly went to the forest, the place for performing asceticism.

3.9.s:
tamāsanasthaṃ munibhistriśṛṅgamiva parvatam /
trayī mukharadigbhāgaṃ brahmānadaikaniṣṭhitam //
3.9.d:
तमासनस्थं मुनिभिस्त्रिशृङ्गमिव पर्वतम् ।
त्रयी मुखरदिग्भागं ब्रह्मानदैकनिष्ठितम् ॥
3.9.m: Him seated on an ascetic's seat like a three-peaked mountain, / his quarters resounding with the three Vedas, firmly fixed on the bliss of Brahman alone,

3.9.s:
sarvabhūtahitaṃ taṃ tu matvā ceśānukūlitaḥ /
śirāṃsi yaugapadyena chinnātyāsaṃstvayaiva tu //
3.9.d:
सर्वभूतहितं तं तु मत्वा चेशानुकूलितः ।
शिरांसि यौगपद्येन छिन्नात्यासंस्त्वयैव तु ॥
3.9.m: regarding him as beneficial to all beings, yet favored by the Lord, / his heads were simultaneously severed by you alone.

3.9.s:
tena pāpena saṃyuktaḥ pīḍitaśca muhurmuhuḥ /
tato meruguhāṃ nītvā bahūnabdānhi saṃsthitaḥ //
3.9.d:
तेन पापेन संयुक्तः पीडितश्च मुहुर्मुहुः ।
ततो मेरुगुहां नीत्वा बहूनब्दान्हि संस्थितः ॥
3.9.m: Afflicted by that sin and tormented again and again, / having then gone to a cave of Meru, [you] stayed there for many years.

3.9.s:
tatastasya vacaḥ śrutvā jñātvā tu munivākyataḥ /
putra śokena saṃtaptastvāṃ śaśāpa ruṣānvitaḥ //
3.9.d:
ततस्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ज्ञात्वा तु मुनिवाक्यतः ।
पुत्र शोकेन संतप्तस्त्वां शशाप रुषान्वितः ॥
3.9.m: Then, hearing his word and learning [of it] from the words of the sages, / [Tvaṣṭṛ], burning with grief for his son, cursed you in anger:

3.9.s:
niḥśrīko bhavatu kṣipraṃ mama śāpena vāsavaḥ /
anāthakāstato devā viṣaṇṇā daityapīḍitāḥ //
3.9.d:
निःश्रीको भवतु क्षिप्रं मम शापेन वासवः ।
अनाथकास्ततो देवा विषण्णा दैत्यपीडिताः ॥
3.9.m: 'Let Vāsava quickly become devoid of fortune through my curse!' / Bereft of a protector, the gods then became despondent, oppressed by the Daityas.

3.9.s:
tvayā mayā ca rahitāḥ sarve devāḥ palāyitāḥ /
gatvā tu brahmasadanaṃ natvā tadvṛttamūcire //
3.9.d:
त्वया मया च रहिताः सर्वे देवाः पलायिताः ।
गत्वा तु ब्रह्मसदनं नत्वा तद्वृत्तमूचिरे ॥
3.9.m: Bereft of you and me, all the gods fled; / having gone to the abode of Brahmā and bowed, they related that event.

3.9.s:
tatastu cintayā māsa tadaghasya pratikriyām /
tasya pratikriyāṃ vettuṃ na śaśākātmabhūstadā //
3.9.d:
ततस्तु चिन्तया मास तदघस्य प्रतिक्रियाम् ।
तस्य प्रतिक्रियां वेत्तुं न शशाकात्मभूस्तदा ॥
3.9.m: Then he considered the counteracting of that sin; / the self-born [Brahmā] was unable then to know the remedy for it.

3.9.s: tato devaiḥ parivṛto nārāyaṇamupāgamat //
3.9.d: ततो देवैः परिवृतो नारायणमुपागमत् ॥
3.9.m: Then, surrounded by the gods, he approached Nārāyaṇa.

3.9.s:
natvā stutvā caturvakrastadvṛttāntaṃ vyajijñapat /
vicintya so 'pi bahudhā kṛpayā lokanāyakaḥ //
3.9.d:
नत्वा स्तुत्वा चतुर्वक्रस्तद्वृत्तान्तं व्यजिज्ञपत् ।
विचिन्त्य सो ऽपि बहुधा कृपया लोकनायकः ॥
3.9.m: Bowing and praising [him], the four-faced [Brahmā] made known the account; / having considered [it] in many ways, that lord of the worlds, out of compassion,

3.9.s:
tadaghaṃ tu tridhā bhittvā triṣu sthāneṣvathārpayat /
strīṣu bhūmyāṃ ca vṛkṣeṣu teṣāmapi varaṃ dadau //
3.9.d:
तदघं तु त्रिधा भित्त्वा त्रिषु स्थानेष्वथार्पयत् ।
स्त्रीषु भूम्यां च वृक्षेषु तेषामपि वरं ददौ ॥
3.9.m: split that sin into three parts and then placed it in three places: / in women, in the earth, and in trees; and he granted them boons as well:

3.9.s:
tadā bharttṛsamāyogaṃ putrāvāptimṛtuṣvapi /
chede punarbhavatvaṃ tu sarveṣāmapi śākhinām //
3.9.d:
तदा भर्त्तृसमायोगं पुत्रावाप्तिमृतुष्वपि ।
छेदे पुनर्भवत्वं तु सर्वेषामपि शाखिनाम् ॥
3.9.m: Union with a husband and obtaining a son even in menstrual periods, / and regrowth for all trees upon being cut;

3.9.s:
khātapūrtiṃ dharaṇyaśca pradadau madhusūdanaḥ /
teṣvaghaṃ prababhūvāśu rajoniryāsamūṣaram //
3.9.d:
खातपूर्तिं धरण्यश्च प्रददौ मधुसूदनः ।
तेष्वघं प्रबभूवाशु रजोनिर्यासमूषरम् ॥
3.9.m: and the slayer of Madhu granted to the earth the filling up of excavations; / among them, the sin quickly manifested as menses, sap, and barren saline soil.

3.9.s:
nirgato gahvarāttasmāttvamindro devanāyakaḥ /
rājyaśriyaṃ ca saṃprāptaḥ prasādātparameṣṭhinaḥ //
3.9.d:
निर्गतो गह्वरात्तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रो देवनायकः ।
राज्यश्रियं च संप्राप्तः प्रसादात्परमेष्ठिनः ॥
3.9.m: Emerging from that cavern, you, Indra, leader of the gods, / attained the splendor of the kingdom by the grace of the Supreme Lord.

3.9.s:
tenaiva sāṃtvito dhātā jagāda ca janārdanam /
mama śāpo vṛthā na syādastu kālāntare mune //
3.9.d:
तेनैव सांत्वितो धाता जगाद च जनार्दनम् ।
मम शापो वृथा न स्यादस्तु कालान्तरे मुने ॥
3.9.m: Comforted by him alone, the creator said to Janārdana: / 'May my curse not be in vain; let it come to pass at another time, O sage!'

3.9.s:
bhagavāṃstadvacaḥ śrutvā muneramitatejasaḥ /
prahṛṣṭo bhāvikāryajñastūṣṇīmeva tadā yayau //
3.9.d:
भगवांस्तद्वचः श्रुत्वा मुनेरमिततेजसः ।
प्रहृष्टो भाविकार्यज्ञस्तूष्णीमेव तदा ययौ ॥
3.9.m: Hearing that word of the sage of immeasurable splendor, the Blessed One, / pleased and knowing what was to happen, departed in silence then.

3.9.s:
etāvantamimaṃ kālaṃ trilokīṃ pālayanbhavān /
eśvaryamadamattatvātkailāsādrimapīḍayata //
3.9.d:
एतावन्तमिमं कालं त्रिलोकीं पालयन्भवान् ।
एश्वर्यमदमत्तत्वात्कैलासाद्रिमपीडयत ॥
3.9.m: Protecting the three worlds for so long a time, / intoxicated with the arrogance of power, you oppressed Mount Kailāsa.

3.9.s:
sarvajñena śivenātha preṣito bhagavānmuniḥ /
durvāsāstvanmadabhraṃśaṃ karttukāmaḥ śaśāpa ha //
3.9.d:
सर्वज्ञेन शिवेनाथ प्रेषितो भगवान्मुनिः ।
दुर्वासास्त्वन्मदभ्रंशं कर्त्तुकामः शशाप ह ॥
3.9.m: Then, sent by the omniscient Śiva, the venerable sage / Durvāsas, desiring to bring about the destruction of your arrogance, indeed cursed [you].

3.9.s:
ekameva phalaṃ jātamubhayoḥ śāpayorapi /
adhunā paśyaniḥ śrīkantrailokyaṃ samajāyata //
3.9.d:
एकमेव फलं जातमुभयोः शापयोरपि ।
अधुना पश्यनिः श्रीकन्त्रैलोक्यं समजायत ॥
3.9.m: A single result arose from both of those curses; / now see, the three worlds have become bereft of fortune.

3.9.s:
na yajñāḥ saṃpravarttante na dānāni ca vāsava /
na yamā nāpi niyamā na tapāsi ca kutracit //
3.9.d:
न यज्ञाः संप्रवर्त्तन्ते न दानानि च वासव ।
न यमा नापि नियमा न तपासि च कुत्रचित् ॥
3.9.m: No sacrifices are performed, nor gifts [given], O Vāsava; / there are no restraints, nor observances, nor ascetic austerities anywhere.

3.9.s:
viprāḥ sarve 'pi niḥśrīkā lobhopahatacetasaḥ /
niḥsttvā dhairyahīnāśca nāstikāḥ prāyaśo 'bhavan //
3.9.d:
विप्राः सर्वे ऽपि निःश्रीका लोभोपहतचेतसः ।
निःस्त्त्वा धैर्यहीनाश्च नास्तिकाः प्रायशो ऽभवन् ॥
3.9.m: All the brahmins are devoid of fortune, their minds ruined by greed; / they have mostly become devoid of vitality, lacking courage, and unbelievers.

3.9.s:
nirauṣadhirasā bhūmirnivīrya jāyatetarām /
bhāskaro dhūsarākāraścandramāḥ kāntivarjitaḥ //
3.9.d:
निरौषधिरसा भूमिर्निवीर्य जायतेतराम् ।
भास्करो धूसराकारश्चन्द्रमाः कान्तिवर्जितः ॥
3.9.m: The earth has become completely devoid of the essence of medicinal herbs and devoid of vigor; / the sun has an ashen appearance, and the moon is bereft of luster.

3.9.s:
nistejasko havirbhoktā manuddhūlikṛtākṛtiḥ /
na prasannā diśāṃ bhāgā nabho naiva ca nirmalam //
3.9.d:
निस्तेजस्को हविर्भोक्ता मनुद्धूलिकृताकृतिः ।
न प्रसन्ना दिशां भागा नभो नैव च निर्मलम् ॥
3.9.m: The consumer of oblations lacks brilliance, its form reduced to fine dust; / the quarters of space are not clear, nor is the sky spotless.

3.9.s:
durbalā devatāḥ sarvā vibhāntyanyādṛśā iva /
vinaṣṭaprayamevāsti trailokyaṃ sacarācaram //
3.9.d:
दुर्बला देवताः सर्वा विभान्त्यन्यादृशा इव ।
विनष्टप्रयमेवास्ति त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
3.9.m: All the deities are weak, appearing as if altered; / the three worlds, with the moving and unmoving, are almost destroyed.

3.9.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
itthaṃ kathayatoreva bṛhaspatipahendrayoḥ /
malakādyā mahādaityāḥ svargalokaṃ babādhire //
3.9.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
इत्थं कथयतोरेव बृहस्पतिपहेन्द्रयोः ।
मलकाद्या महादैत्याः स्वर्गलोकं बबाधिरे ॥
3.9.m: Hayagrīva said: / Even as Bṛhaspati and the great Indra were speaking thus, / the great Daityas, headed by Malaka, tormented the celestial realm.

3.9.s:
nandanodyāna makhilaṃ cicchidurbalagarvitāḥ /
udyānapālakānsarvānāyudhaiḥ samatāḍayan //
3.9.d:
नन्दनोद्यान मखिलं चिच्छिदुर्बलगर्विताः ।
उद्यानपालकान्सर्वानायुधैः समताडयन् ॥
3.9.m: Arrogant with strength, they cut down the entire Nandana garden; / they struck all the keepers of the garden with weapons.

3.9.s:
prākāramavabhidyaiva praviśya nagarāntaram /
mandirasthānsurānsarvānatyantaṃ paryapīḍayan //
3.9.d:
प्राकारमवभिद्यैव प्रविश्य नगरान्तरम् ।
मन्दिरस्थान्सुरान्सर्वानत्यन्तं पर्यपीडयन् ॥
3.9.m: Breaching the outer wall and entering within the city, / they exceedingly tormented all the gods residing in their palaces.

3.9.s:
ājahurapsaroratnānyaśeṣāṇi viśeṣataḥ /
tato devāḥ samastāśca cakrurbhṛśamabādhitāḥ //
3.9.d:
आजहुरप्सरोरत्नान्यशेषाणि विशेषतः ।
ततो देवाः समस्ताश्च चक्रुर्भृशमबाधिताः ॥
3.9.m: They seized the precious jewels of apsarases without exception, especially; / then all the gods cried out intensely, sorely afflicted.

3.9.s:
tādṛśaṃ ghoṣamākarmya vāsavaḥ projjhitāsanaḥ /
sarvairanugato devaiḥ palāyanaparo 'bhavat //
3.9.d:
तादृशं घोषमाकर्म्य वासवः प्रोज्झितासनः ।
सर्वैरनुगतो देवैः पलायनपरो ऽभवत् ॥
3.9.m: Hearing such an uproar, Vāsava abandoned his seat, / and, followed by all the gods, became bent on flight.

3.9.s:
brāhmaṃ dhāma samabhyetya viṣaṇmavadano vṛṣā /
yathāvatkathayāmāsa nikhilaṃ daityaceṣṭitam //
3.9.d:
ब्राह्मं धाम समभ्येत्य विषण्मवदनो वृषा ।
यथावत्कथयामास निखिलं दैत्यचेष्टितम् ॥
3.9.m: Approaching the realm of Brahmā, his face downcast, Indra / recounted truthfully the entire deed of the Daityas.

3.9.s:
vidhātāpi tadākarṇya sarvadevasamanvitam /
hataśrīkaṃ harihayamālokyedamuvāca ha //
3.9.d:
विधातापि तदाकर्ण्य सर्वदेवसमन्वितम् ।
हतश्रीकं हरिहयमालोक्येदमुवाच ह ॥
3.9.m: Hearing that, and seeing Harihaya, accompanied by all the gods, / stripped of his fortune, the creator spoke this:

3.9.s:
indratvamakhilairddevairmukundaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja /
daityārātirjagatkartā sa te śreyo vidhāsyati //
3.9.d:
इन्द्रत्वमखिलैर्द्देवैर्मुकुन्दं शरणं व्रज ।
दैत्यारातिर्जगत्कर्ता स ते श्रेयो विधास्यति ॥
3.9.m: “Indra, together with all the gods, take refuge in Mukunda; / he who is the enemy of the Daityas and maker of the world will bring about your welfare.”

3.9.s:
ityuktvā tena sahitaḥ svayaṃ brahmā pitāmahaḥ /
samastadevasahitaḥ kṣīrodadhimupāyayau //
3.9.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तेन सहितः स्वयं ब्रह्मा पितामहः ।
समस्तदेवसहितः क्षीरोदधिमुपाययौ ॥
3.9.m: Having spoken thus, Brahmā the Grandsire himself, accompanied by him / and all the gods, went to the Ocean of Milk.

3.9.s:
atha brahmādayo devā bhagavantaṃ janārdanam /
tuṣṭuvurvāgvariṣṭhābhiḥ sarvalokamaheśvaram //
3.9.d:
अथ ब्रह्मादयो देवा भगवन्तं जनार्दनम् ।
तुष्टुवुर्वाग्वरिष्ठाभिः सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् ॥
3.9.m: Then the gods, led by Brahmā, praised the blessed Janārdana, / the great lord of all the worlds, with the most excellent words.

3.9.s:
atha prasanno bhagavānvāsudevaḥ sanātanaḥ /
jagāda sa kalāndevāñjagadrakṣaṇalaṃpaṭaḥ //
3.9.d:
अथ प्रसन्नो भगवान्वासुदेवः सनातनः ।
जगाद स कलान्देवाञ्जगद्रक्षणलंपटः ॥
3.9.m: Then the eternal blessed Vāsudeva was pleased, / and eager to protect the world, he spoke clearly to the gods:

3.9.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
bhavatāṃ suvidhāsyāmi tejasaivopabṛṃhamam /
yaducyate mayedānīṃ yuṣmābhista dvidhīyatām //
3.9.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
भवतां सुविधास्यामि तेजसैवोपबृंहमम् ।
यदुच्यते मयेदानीं युष्माभिस्त द्विधीयताम् ॥
3.9.m: The Holy One said: / “I will well arrange the enhancement of your splendor. / What is spoken by me now, let that be carried out by you.

3.9.s:
oṣadhipravarāḥ sarvāḥ kṣipata kṣīrasāgare /
asurairapi saṃdhāya samameva ca tairiha //
3.9.d:
ओषधिप्रवराः सर्वाः क्षिपत क्षीरसागरे ।
असुरैरपि संधाय सममेव च तैरिह ॥
3.9.m: Throw all the foremost herbs into the Ocean of Milk; / having made peace even with the Asuras, right alongside them here,

3.9.s:
manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā kṛtvā yoktraṃ ca vāsukim /
mayi sthite sahāye tu mathyatāmamṛtaṃ surāḥ //
3.9.d:
मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा कृत्वा योक्त्रं च वासुकिम् ।
मयि स्थिते सहाये तु मथ्यताममृतं सुराः ॥
3.9.m: making Mandara the churning rod and making Vāsuki the churning rope, / while I stand by as your helper, O gods, churn the nectar of immortality!

3.9.s:
samastadānavāścāpi vaktavyāḥ sāṃtvapūrvakam /
sāmānyameva yuṣmākamasmākaṃ ca phalaṃ tviti //
3.9.d:
समस्तदानवाश्चापि वक्तव्याः सांत्वपूर्वकम् ।
सामान्यमेव युष्माकमस्माकं च फलं त्विति ॥
3.9.m: All the Dānavas must also be spoken to with soothing words: / ‘The fruit is indeed common to you and to us.’

3.9.s:
mathyamāne tu dugdhābdhau yā samutpadyate sudhā /
tatpānādbalino yūyamamartyāśca bhaviṣyatha //
3.9.d:
मथ्यमाने तु दुग्धाब्धौ या समुत्पद्यते सुधा ।
तत्पानाद्बलिनो यूयममर्त्याश्च भविष्यथ ॥
3.9.m: When the Ocean of Milk is churned, the nectar that is produced— / from drinking it, you will become strong and immortal.

3.9.s:
yathā daityāśca pīyūṣaṃ naitatprāpsyanti kiñcana /
kevalaṃ kleśavantaśca kariṣyāmi tathā hyaham //
3.9.d:
यथा दैत्याश्च पीयूषं नैतत्प्राप्स्यन्ति किञ्चन ।
केवलं क्लेशवन्तश्च करिष्यामि तथा ह्यहम् ॥
3.9.m: I will act in such a way that the Daityas / will not obtain any of this nectar and will only have their toil.”

3.9.s:
iti śrīvāsudevena kathitā nikhilāḥ surāḥ /
saṃdhānaṃ tvatulairdaityaiḥ kṛtavantastadā surāḥ /
nānāvidhauṣadhigaṇaṃ samānīya surāsurāḥ //
3.9.d:
इति श्रीवासुदेवेन कथिता निखिलाः सुराः ।
संधानं त्वतुलैर्दैत्यैः कृतवन्तस्तदा सुराः ।
नानाविधौषधिगणं समानीय सुरासुराः ॥
3.9.m: Having been spoken to thus by the venerable Vāsudeva, all the gods / then made an alliance with the peerless Daityas. / Bringing together various kinds of herbs, the gods and Asuras,

3.9.s:
śrīrābdhipayasi kṣiptvā candramo 'dhikanirmalam /
manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā kṛtvā yoktraṃ tu vāsukim /
prārebhire prayatnena manthituṃ yādasāṃ patim //
3.9.d:
श्रीराब्धिपयसि क्षिप्त्वा चन्द्रमो ऽधिकनिर्मलम् ।
मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा कृत्वा योक्त्रं तु वासुकिम् ।
प्रारेभिरे प्रयत्नेन मन्थितुं यादसां पतिम् ॥
3.9.m: threw them into the water of the Ocean of Milk, which was purer than the moon; / making Mandara the churning rod and Vāsuki the churning rope, / they began with great effort to churn the lord of aquatic creatures.

3.9.s:
vāsukeḥ pucchabhāge tu sahitāḥ sarvadevatāḥ /
śirobhāge tu daiteyā niyuktāstatra śauriṇā //
3.9.d:
वासुकेः पुच्छभागे तु सहिताः सर्वदेवताः ।
शिरोभागे तु दैतेया नियुक्तास्तत्र शौरिणा ॥
3.9.m: All the deities together were placed at the tail of Vāsuki, / while the Daityas were assigned to the head by Śauri.

3.9.s:
balavanto 'pi te daityāstanmukhocchvāsapāvakaiḥ /
nirdagdhavapuṣaḥ sarve nistejaskāstadābhavan //
3.9.d:
बलवन्तो ऽपि ते दैत्यास्तन्मुखोच्छ्वासपावकैः ।
निर्दग्धवपुषः सर्वे निस्तेजस्कास्तदाभवन् ॥
3.9.m: Though powerful, all those Daityas, their bodies scorched / by the fires exhaled from his mouth, then became devoid of splendor.

3.9.s:
pucchadeśe tu karṣanto muhurāpyāyitāḥ surāḥ /
anukūlena vātena viṣṇunā preritena tu //
3.9.d:
पुच्छदेशे तु कर्षन्तो मुहुराप्यायिताः सुराः ।
अनुकूलेन वातेन विष्णुना प्रेरितेन तु ॥
3.9.m: Pulling at the tail, the gods were constantly invigorated / by a favorable wind sent forth by Viṣṇu.

3.9.s:
ādikūrmākṛtiḥ śrīmānmadhye kṣīrapayonidheḥ /
bhramato mandarādrestu tasyā dhiṣṭānatāmagāt //
3.9.d:
आदिकूर्माकृतिः श्रीमान्मध्ये क्षीरपयोनिधेः ।
भ्रमतो मन्दराद्रेस्तु तस्या धिष्टानतामगात् ॥
3.9.m: Taking the form of the primordial tortoise, the glorious [Lord] in the midst of the Ocean of Milk / became the base for Mount Mandara as it spun.

3.9.s:
madhye ca sarvadevānāṃ rūpeṇānyena mādhavaḥ /
cakarṣa vāsukiṃ vegāddaityamadhye pareṇa ca //
3.9.d:
मध्ये च सर्वदेवानां रूपेणान्येन माधवः ।
चकर्ष वासुकिं वेगाद्दैत्यमध्ये परेण च ॥
3.9.m: And in the midst of all the gods, Mādhava in another form / vigorously pulled Vāsuki, and in the midst of the Daityas in yet another form.

3.9.s:
brahmarūpeṇa taṃ śailaṃ vidhāryākrāntavāridhim /
apareṇa ca devarṣirmahatā tejasā muhuḥ //
3.9.d:
ब्रह्मरूपेण तं शैलं विधार्याक्रान्तवारिधिम् ।
अपरेण च देवर्षिर्महता तेजसा मुहुः ॥
3.9.m: Holding that mountain in the form of Brahmā as it pressed upon the sea, / and in another form, O divine sage, with great splendor constantly

3.9.s:
upavṛṃhitavāndevānyena te balaśālinaḥ /
tejasā punaranyena balātkārasahena saḥ //
3.9.d:
उपवृंहितवान्देवान्येन ते बलशालिनः ।
तेजसा पुनरन्येन बलात्कारसहेन सः ॥
3.9.m: he invigorated the gods, by which they became powerful; / then with another splendor capable of enduring violent force, he,

3.9.s:
upabṛṃhitavānnāgaṃ sarvaśaktijanārdanaḥ /
mathyamāne tatastasminkṣīrabdhau devadānavaiḥ //
3.9.d:
उपबृंहितवान्नागं सर्वशक्तिजनार्दनः ।
मथ्यमाने ततस्तस्मिन्क्षीरब्धौ देवदानवैः ॥
3.9.m: Janārdana, who possesses all powers, strengthened the serpent. / Then, as that Ocean of Milk was being churned by the gods and Dānavas,

3.9.s:
āvirbabhūva purataḥ surabhiḥ surapūjitā /
mudaṃ jagmustadā devā daiteyāśca tapodhana //
3.9.d:
आविर्बभूव पुरतः सुरभिः सुरपूजिता ।
मुदं जग्मुस्तदा देवा दैतेयाश्च तपोधन ॥
3.9.m: Surabhi, worshipped by the gods, appeared before them; / the gods and the Daityas then rejoiced, O you rich in asceticism.

3.9.s:
mathyamāne punastasminkṣīrābdau devadānavaiḥ /
kimetaditi siddhānāṃ divi cintayatāṃ tadā //
3.9.d:
मथ्यमाने पुनस्तस्मिन्क्षीराब्दौ देवदानवैः ।
किमेतदिति सिद्धानां दिवि चिन्तयतां तदा ॥
3.9.m: As that Ocean of Milk was churned again by the gods and Dānavas, / while the Siddhas in heaven were wondering, “What is this?”,

3.9.s:
utthitā vāruṇī devī madāllolavilocanā /
asurāṇāṃ purastātsā smayamānā vyatiṣṭhata //
3.9.d:
उत्थिता वारुणी देवी मदाल्लोलविलोचना ।
असुराणां पुरस्तात्सा स्मयमाना व्यतिष्ठत ॥
3.9.m: the goddess Vāruṇī arose, her eyes rolling from intoxication; / smiling, she stood before the Asuras.

3.9.s:
jagṛhurnaiva tāṃ daityā asurāścābhavaṃstataḥ /
surā na vidyate yeṣāṃ tenaivāsuraśabditāḥ //
3.9.d:
जगृहुर्नैव तां दैत्या असुराश्चाभवंस्ततः ।
सुरा न विद्यते येषां तेनैवासुरशब्दिताः ॥
3.9.m: The Daityas did not accept her, and thus they became Asuras; / because there is no wine (surā) for them, they are called Asuras.

3.9.s:
athasā sarvadevānāmagrataḥ samatiṣṭhata /
jagṛhustāṃ mudā devāḥ sūcitāḥ parameṣṭhinā /
surāgrahaṇato 'pyete suraśabdena kīrtitāḥ //
3.9.d:
अथसा सर्वदेवानामग्रतः समतिष्ठत ।
जगृहुस्तां मुदा देवाः सूचिताः परमेष्ठिना ।
सुराग्रहणतो ऽप्येते सुरशब्देन कीर्तिताः ॥
3.9.m: Then she stood before all the gods; / instructed by Parameṣṭhin, the gods accepted her with joy; / because of accepting the wine (surā), they are celebrated by the word Sura.

3.9.s:
mathyamāne tato bhūyaḥ pārijāto mahādrumaḥ /
āvirāsītsuṃgadhena parito vāsayañjagat //
3.9.d:
मथ्यमाने ततो भूयः पारिजातो महाद्रुमः ।
आविरासीत्सुंगधेन परितो वासयञ्जगत् ॥
3.9.m: As [the ocean] was churned further, the great pārijāta tree / appeared, perfuming the world all around with its fragrance.

3.9.s:
atyarthasuṃdarākārā dhīrāścāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ /
āvirbhūtāśca devarṣe sarvalokamanoharāḥ //
3.9.d:
अत्यर्थसुंदराकारा धीराश्चाप्सरसां गणाः ।
आविर्भूताश्च देवर्षे सर्वलोकमनोहराः ॥
3.9.m: Hosts of Apsarases of exceedingly beautiful form, resolute / and captivating to all the worlds, also appeared, O divine sage.

3.9.s:
tataḥ śītāṃśurudabhūttaṃ jagrāha maheśvaraḥ /
viṣajātaṃ tadutpannaṃ jagṛhurnāgajātayaḥ //
3.9.d:
ततः शीतांशुरुदभूत्तं जग्राह महेश्वरः ।
विषजातं तदुत्पन्नं जगृहुर्नागजातयः ॥
3.9.m: Then the cool-rayed moon arose, which Maheśvara took; / the kinds of serpents took the mass of poison that was produced then.

3.9.s:
kaustubhākhyaṃ tato ratnamādade tajjanārdanaḥ /
tataḥ svapatragandhena madayantī mahauṣadhīḥ /
vijayā nāma saṃjajñe bhairavastāmupādade //
3.9.d:
कौस्तुभाख्यं ततो रत्नमाददे तज्जनार्दनः ।
ततः स्वपत्रगन्धेन मदयन्ती महौषधीः ।
विजया नाम संजज्ञे भैरवस्तामुपाददे ॥
3.9.m: Then Janārdana took the jewel named Kaustubha; / then the great herb named Vijayā arose, intoxicating with the scent of its leaves, / and Bhairava took it.

3.9.s:
tato divyāṃbaradharo devo dhanvantariḥ svayam /
upasthitaḥ kare bibhradamṛtāḍhyaṃ kamaṇḍalum //
3.9.d:
ततो दिव्यांबरधरो देवो धन्वन्तरिः स्वयम् ।
उपस्थितः करे बिभ्रदमृताढ्यं कमण्डलुम् ॥
3.9.m: Then the divine Dhanvantari himself, wearing celestial garments, / appeared, holding in his hand a water pot filled with the nectar of immortality.

3.9.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭamanaso devā daityāśca sarvataḥ /
munayaścābhavaṃstuṣṭāstadānīṃ tapasāṃ nidhe //
3.9.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टमनसो देवा दैत्याश्च सर्वतः ।
मुनयश्चाभवंस्तुष्टास्तदानीं तपसां निधे ॥
3.9.m: Then the gods and Daityas everywhere were joyful in mind, / and the sages became pleased, O treasure of asceticism.

3.9.s:
tato vikasitāṃbhojavāsinī varadāyinī /
utthitā padmahastā śrīstasmātkṣīramahārmavāt //
3.9.d:
ततो विकसितांभोजवासिनी वरदायिनी ।
उत्थिता पद्महस्ता श्रीस्तस्मात्क्षीरमहार्मवात् ॥
3.9.m: Then Śrī, who dwells on an open lotus, who grants boons, / arose from that great Ocean of Milk with a lotus in her hand.

3.9.s:
atha tāṃ munayaḥ sarve śrīsuktena śriyaṃ parām /
tuṣṭuvustuṣṭa hṛdayā gandharvāśca jaguḥ param //
3.9.d:
अथ तां मुनयः सर्वे श्रीसुक्तेन श्रियं पराम् ।
तुष्टुवुस्तुष्ट हृदया गन्धर्वाश्च जगुः परम् ॥
3.9.m: Then all the sages, their hearts delighted, praised the supreme Śrī / with the Śrīsūkta, and the Gandharvas sang supremely.

3.9.s:
viśvājīpramukhāḥ sarve nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ /
gaṅgādyāḥ puṇyanadyaśca snānārthamupatasthire //
3.9.d:
विश्वाजीप्रमुखाः सर्वे ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः ।
गङ्गाद्याः पुण्यनद्यश्च स्नानार्थमुपतस्थिरे ॥
3.9.m: All the hosts of Apsarases, led by Viśvācī, danced, / and sacred rivers such as the Gaṅgā came forward for her bath.

3.9.s:
aṣṭau digdantinaścaiva medhyapātrasthitaṃ jalam /
ādāya snāpayāñcakrustāṃ śriyaṃ padmavāsinīm //
3.9.d:
अष्टौ दिग्दन्तिनश्चैव मेध्यपात्रस्थितं जलम् ।
आदाय स्नापयाञ्चक्रुस्तां श्रियं पद्मवासिनीम् ॥
3.9.m: And the eight elephants of the quarters, taking water held in pure vessels, / bathed that Śrī who dwells on the lotus.

3.9.s:
tulasīṃ ca samutpannāṃ parārdhyā maikyajāṃ hareḥ /
padmamālāṃ dadau tasyai mūrtimānkṣīrasāgaraḥ //
3.9.d:
तुलसीं च समुत्पन्नां परार्ध्या मैक्यजां हरेः ।
पद्ममालां ददौ तस्यै मूर्तिमान्क्षीरसागरः ॥
3.9.m: The Ocean of Milk in person gave her a garland of lotuses, / and the precious Tulasī that had arisen, an object of supreme union for Hari.

3.9.s:
bhūṣaṇāni ca divyāni viśvakarmā samarpayat /
divyamālyāṃ baradharā divyabhūṣaṇabhūṣitā /
yayau vakṣasthalaṃ viṣṇoḥ sarveṣāṃ paśyatāṃ ramā //
3.9.d:
भूषणानि च दिव्यानि विश्वकर्मा समर्पयत् ।
दिव्यमाल्यां बरधरा दिव्यभूषणभूषिता ।
ययौ वक्षस्थलं विष्णोः सर्वेषां पश्यतां रमा ॥
3.9.m: Viśvakarman presented divine ornaments; / wearing divine garlands and garments, adorned with divine ornaments, / Ramā went to the chest of Viṣṇu as all looked on.

3.9.s:
tulasī tu dhṛtā tena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā /
paśyati sma ca sā devī viṣṇuvakṣathalālayā /
devāndayārdrayā dṛṣṭyā sarvalokamaheśvarī //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne amṛtamanthanaṃ nāma navamo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.9.d:
तुलसी तु धृता तेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ।
पश्यति स्म च सा देवी विष्णुवक्षथलालया ।
देवान्दयार्द्रया दृष्ट्या सर्वलोकमहेश्वरी ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने अमृतमन्थनं नाम नवमो ऽध्यायः
3.9.m:
The Tulasī was worn by the mighty Viṣṇu; / and that goddess, whose abode is on Viṣṇu's chest, / the sovereign lady of all the worlds, looked upon the gods with a glance moist with compassion.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled “The Churning for Nectar,” in the Lalitopākhyāna within the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the venerable and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

3.10.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
atha devā mahendrādyā viṣṇunā prabhaviṣmunā /
aṅgīkṛtā mahādhīrāḥ pramodaṃ paramaṃ yayuḥ //
3.10.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
अथ देवा महेन्द्राद्या विष्णुना प्रभविष्मुना ।
अङ्गीकृता महाधीराः प्रमोदं परमं ययुः ॥
3.10.m: Hayagrīva said: / Then the gods, Mahendra and the rest, accepted / by the mighty Viṣṇu, highly steadfast, experienced supreme joy.

3.10.s:
malakādyāstu te sarve daityā viṣṇuparāṅmukhāḥ /
saṃtyaktāśca śriyā devyā bhṛśamudvegamāgatāḥ //
3.10.d:
मलकाद्यास्तु ते सर्वे दैत्या विष्णुपराङ्मुखाः ।
संत्यक्ताश्च श्रिया देव्या भृशमुद्वेगमागताः ॥
3.10.m: All those Daityas, however, led by Malaka, averse to Viṣṇu / and abandoned by the goddess Śrī, were overwhelmed with great distress.

3.10.s:
tato jagṛhire daityā dhanvantarikarasthitam /
paramāmṛtasārāḍhyaṃ kalaśaṃ kanakodbhavam /
athāsurāṇāṃ devānāmanyonyaṃ kalaho 'bhavat //
3.10.d:
ततो जगृहिरे दैत्या धन्वन्तरिकरस्थितम् ।
परमामृतसाराढ्यं कलशं कनकोद्भवम् ।
अथासुराणां देवानामन्योन्यं कलहो ऽभवत् ॥
3.10.m: Then the Daityas seized the golden pot / containing the supreme essence of nectar that was in Dhanvantari’s hand; / then a dispute arose between the Asuras and the gods.

3.10.s:
etasminnantare viṣṇuḥ sarvalokaikarakṣakaḥ /
samyagārādhayāmāsalalitāṃ svaikyarūpiṇīm //
3.10.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे विष्णुः सर्वलोकैकरक्षकः ।
सम्यगाराधयामासललितां स्वैक्यरूपिणीम् ॥
3.10.m: In the meantime, Viṣṇu, the sole protector of all the worlds, / duly worshipped Lalitā, whose form is identical with his own.

3.10.s:
surāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca raṇaṃ vīkṣya sudāruṇam /
brahmā nijapadaṃ prāpa śaṃbhuḥ kailāsamāsthitaḥ //
3.10.d:
सुराणामसुराणां च रणं वीक्ष्य सुदारुणम् ।
ब्रह्मा निजपदं प्राप शंभुः कैलासमास्थितः ॥
3.10.m: Seeing the terrible battle between the gods and Asuras, / Brahmā went to his own abode and Śambhu retired to Kailāsa.

3.10.s:
malakaṃ yodhayāmāsa daityānāmadhipaṃ vṛṣā /
asuraiśca surāḥ sarve sāṃparāyamakurvata //
3.10.d:
मलकं योधयामास दैत्यानामधिपं वृषा ।
असुरैश्च सुराः सर्वे सांपरायमकुर्वत ॥
3.10.m: Vṛṣan fought Malaka, the lord of the Daityas, / and all the gods engaged in battle with the Asuras.

3.10.s:
bhagavānapi yogīndraḥ samārādhya maheśvarīm /
tadekadhyānayogena tadrūpaḥ samajāyata //
3.10.d:
भगवानपि योगीन्द्रः समाराध्य महेश्वरीम् ।
तदेकध्यानयोगेन तद्रूपः समजायत ॥
3.10.m: The Blessed One too, the lord of yogins, having worshipped the Great Goddess, / through the yoga of meditation solely upon Her, assumed Her very form.

3.10.s:
sarvasaṃmohinī sā tu sākṣācchṛṅgāranāyikā /
sarvaśṛṅgāraveṣāḍhyā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā //
3.10.d:
सर्वसंमोहिनी सा तु साक्षाच्छृङ्गारनायिका ।
सर्वशृङ्गारवेषाढ्या सर्वाभरणभूषिता ॥
3.10.m: She indeed was the enchantress of all, the very goddess of love incarnate, / rich in every amorous attire, adorned with all ornaments.

3.10.s:
surāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca nivārya raṇamulvaṇam /
mandasmitena daiteyānmohayantī jagada ha //
3.10.d:
सुराणामसुराणां च निवार्य रणमुल्वणम् ।
मन्दस्मितेन दैतेयान्मोहयन्ती जगद ह ॥
3.10.m: Having halted the fierce battle between the gods and the asuras, / enchanting the sons of Diti with a gentle smile, she said:

3.10.s:
alaṃ yuddhena kiṃ śastrermarmasthānavibhedibhiḥ /
niṣṭhuraiḥ kiṃ vṛthālāpaiḥ kaṇṭhaśoṣaṇahetubhiḥ //
3.10.d:
अलं युद्धेन किं शस्त्रेर्मर्मस्थानविभेदिभिः ।
निष्ठुरैः किं वृथालापैः कण्ठशोषणहेतुभिः ॥
3.10.m: “Enough with fighting! What use are weapons that pierce vital spots? / What use are harsh words spoken in vain that only dry the throat?

3.10.s:
ahamevātra madhyasthā yuṣmākaṃ ca divaukasām /
yūyaṃ tathāmī nitarāmatra hi kleśabhāginaḥ //
3.10.d:
अहमेवात्र मध्यस्था युष्माकं च दिवौकसाम् ।
यूयं तथामी नितरामत्र हि क्लेशभागिनः ॥
3.10.m: I alone will be the mediator here between you and the celestials; / you and they alike are suffering exceedingly in this struggle.

3.10.s:
sarveṣāṃ samamevādya dāsyāmyamṛtamadbhutam /
mama haste pradātavyaṃ sudhāpātramanuttamam //
3.10.d:
सर्वेषां सममेवाद्य दास्याम्यमृतमद्भुतम् ।
मम हस्ते प्रदातव्यं सुधापात्रमनुत्तमम् ॥
3.10.m: Today I will distribute the wondrous nectar equally among you all; / you must place the peerless vessel of nectar into my hand.”

3.10.s:
iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā daityāstadvākyamohitāḥ /
pīyūṣakalaśaṃ tasyai daduste mugdhacetasaḥ //
3.10.d:
इति तस्या वचः श्रुत्वा दैत्यास्तद्वाक्यमोहिताः ।
पीयूषकलशं तस्यै ददुस्ते मुग्धचेतसः ॥
3.10.m: Hearing her words, the daityas, enchanted by her speech, / their minds infatuated, handed the jar of nectar over to her.

3.10.s:
sā tatpātraṃ samādāya jaganmohanarūpiṇī /
surāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca vṛthakpaṅktiṃ cakāra ha //
3.10.d:
सा तत्पात्रं समादाय जगन्मोहनरूपिणी ।
सुराणामसुराणां च वृथक्पङ्क्तिं चकार ह ॥
3.10.m: Taking that vessel, she whose form enchanted the universe / arranged separate rows for the gods and for the asuras.

3.10.s:
dvayoḥ paṅktyośca madhyasthāstānuvāca surāsurān /
tūṣṇīṃ bhavantu sarve 'pi kramaśo dīyate mayā //
3.10.d:
द्वयोः पङ्क्त्योश्च मध्यस्थास्तानुवाच सुरासुरान् ।
तूष्णीं भवन्तु सर्वे ऽपि क्रमशो दीयते मया ॥
3.10.m: Standing between the two rows, she said to those gods and asuras: / “Let all be quiet; it will be distributed by me in turn.”

3.10.s:
tadvākyamurarīcakruste sarve samavāyinaḥ /
sā tu saṃmohitāśleṣalokā dātuṃ pracakrame //
3.10.d:
तद्वाक्यमुररीचक्रुस्ते सर्वे समवायिनः ।
सा तु संमोहिताश्लेषलोका दातुं प्रचक्रमे ॥
3.10.m: All those assembled agreed to her words; / and she, who had enchanted all the worlds, began to distribute [it].

3.10.s:
kvaṇatkanakadarvīkā kvaṇanmaṅgalakaṅkaṇā /
kamanīyavibhūṣāḍhyā kalā sā paramā babhau //
3.10.d:
क्वणत्कनकदर्वीका क्वणन्मङ्गलकङ्कणा ।
कमनीयविभूषाढ्या कला सा परमा बभौ ॥
3.10.m: With a tinkling golden ladle, with jingling auspicious bracelets, / rich in lovely ornaments, that supreme portion shone brightly.

3.10.s:
vāme vāme karāṃbhoje sudhākalaśamujjvalam /
sudhāṃ tāṃ devatāpaṅktau pūrvaṃ darvyā tadādiśat //
3.10.d:
वामे वामे करांभोजे सुधाकलशमुज्ज्वलम् ।
सुधां तां देवतापङ्क्तौ पूर्वं दर्व्या तदादिशत् ॥
3.10.m: Holding the radiant jar of nectar in her left lotus-hand, / she first served that nectar with the ladle to the row of deities.

3.10.s:
diśantī kramaśāstatra candrabhāskarasūcitam /
darvīkareṇa ciccheda saiṃhikeyaṃ tu madhyagam /
pītāmṛtaśiromātraṃ tasya vyoma jagāma ca //
3.10.d:
दिशन्ती क्रमशास्तत्र चन्द्रभास्करसूचितम् ।
दर्वीकरेण चिच्छेद सैंहिकेयं तु मध्यगम् ।
पीतामृतशिरोमात्रं तस्य व्योम जगाम च ॥
3.10.m: As she was serving them in turn, pointed out by the moon and the sun, / with the hand holding the ladle she cut off the son of Siṃhikā who sat among them; / and his head alone, having drunk the nectar, rose into the sky.

3.10.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvāpyasurāstatra tūṣṇīmāsanvimohitāḥ /
evaṃ krameṇa tatsarvaṃ vibudhebhyo vitīrya sā /
asurāṇāṃ puraḥ pātraṃ sānināya tirodadhe //
3.10.d:
तं दृष्ट्वाप्यसुरास्तत्र तूष्णीमासन्विमोहिताः ।
एवं क्रमेण तत्सर्वं विबुधेभ्यो वितीर्य सा ।
असुराणां पुरः पात्रं सानिनाय तिरोदधे ॥
3.10.m: Even on seeing that, the asuras there remained silent, completely bewitched; / thus, having distributed all of it to the gods in order, / she brought the vessel before the asuras and vanished.

3.10.s:
riktapātraṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve daiteyadānavāḥ /
udvelaṃ kevalaṃ krodhaṃ prāptā yuddhacikīrṣayā //
3.10.d:
रिक्तपात्रं तु तं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे दैतेयदानवाः ।
उद्वेलं केवलं क्रोधं प्राप्ता युद्धचिकीर्षया ॥
3.10.m: Seeing that vessel empty, all the sons of Diti and Dānavas / fell into boundless rage, eager to fight.

3.10.s:
indrādayaḥ surāḥ sarve sudhāpānādbalottarāḥ /
durvalairasuraiḥ sārdhaṃ samayuddhyanta sāyudhāḥ //
3.10.d:
इन्द्रादयः सुराः सर्वे सुधापानाद्बलोत्तराः ।
दुर्वलैरसुरैः सार्धं समयुद्ध्यन्त सायुधाः ॥
3.10.m: All the gods, Indra and the others, superior in strength from drinking the nectar, / fought, armed with weapons, alongside the weakened asuras.

3.10.s:
te vidhyamānāḥ śataśo dānavendrāḥ surottamaiḥ /
digantānkaticijjagmuḥ pātālaṃ katicidyayuḥ //
3.10.d:
ते विध्यमानाः शतशो दानवेन्द्राः सुरोत्तमैः ।
दिगन्तान्कतिचिज्जग्मुः पातालं कतिचिद्ययुः ॥
3.10.m: Pierced by the hundreds by the foremost gods, / some of the lords of the Dānavas fled to the ends of the earth, and some went to Pātāla.

3.10.s:
daityaṃ malakanāmānaṃ vijitya vibudheśvaraḥ /
ātmīyāṃ śriyamājahre śrīkaṭākṣa samīkṣitaḥ //
3.10.d:
दैत्यं मलकनामानं विजित्य विबुधेश्वरः ।
आत्मीयां श्रियमाजह्रे श्रीकटाक्ष समीक्षितः ॥
3.10.m: Having conquered the daitya named Malaka, the lord of the gods, / gazed upon by the side-glance of Śrī, recovered his own prosperity.

3.10.s:
punaḥ siṃhāsanaṃ prāpya mahendraḥ surasevitaḥ /
trailokyaṃ pālayāmāsa pūrvavatpūrvadevajit //
3.10.d:
पुनः सिंहासनं प्राप्य महेन्द्रः सुरसेवितः ।
त्रैलोक्यं पालयामास पूर्ववत्पूर्वदेवजित् ॥
3.10.m: Having regained his throne, served by the gods, the great Indra, / the conqueror of the elder gods, protected the three worlds as before.

3.10.s:
nirbhayā nikhilā devāstrailokye sacarācare /
yathākāmaṃ caranti sma sarvadā hṛṣṭacetasaḥ //
3.10.d:
निर्भया निखिला देवास्त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे ।
यथाकामं चरन्ति स्म सर्वदा हृष्टचेतसः ॥
3.10.m: All the gods, freed from fear throughout the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings, / roamed at will, ever joyful in heart.

3.10.s:
tadā tadakhilaṃ dṛṣṭvā mohinīcaritaṃ muniḥ /
vismitaḥ kāmacārī tu kailāsaṃ nārado gataḥ //
3.10.d:
तदा तदखिलं दृष्ट्वा मोहिनीचरितं मुनिः ।
विस्मितः कामचारी तु कैलासं नारदो गतः ॥
3.10.m: Then, having seen all that deed of Mohinī, the sage Nārada, / roaming at will and filled with wonder, went to Kailāsa.

3.10.s:
nandinā ca kṛtānujñaḥ praṇamya parameśvaram /
tena saṃbhāvyamāno 'sau tuṣṭo viṣṭaramāsta saḥ //
3.10.d:
नन्दिना च कृतानुज्ञः प्रणम्य परमेश्वरम् ।
तेन संभाव्यमानो ऽसौ तुष्टो विष्टरमास्त सः ॥
3.10.m: Permitted by Nandin and having bowed to the Supreme Lord, / honoured by him, he gladly sat down upon a seat.

3.10.s:
āsanasthaṃ mahādevo muniṃ svecchāvihāriṇam /
papraccha pārvatījāniḥ svacchasphaṭikasannibhaḥ //
3.10.d:
आसनस्थं महादेवो मुनिं स्वेच्छाविहारिणम् ।
पप्रच्छ पार्वतीजानिः स्वच्छस्फटिकसन्निभः ॥
3.10.m: To the sage seated upon the seat, who roamed at his own pleasure, / Mahādeva, the husband of Pārvatī, resembling clear crystal, asked:

3.10.s:
bhagavansarvavṛttajña pavitrīkṛtaviṣṭara /
kalahapriya devarṣe kiṃ vṛttaṃ tatra nākinām //
3.10.d:
भगवन्सर्ववृत्तज्ञ पवित्रीकृतविष्टर ।
कलहप्रिय देवर्षे किं वृत्तं तत्र नाकिनाम् ॥
3.10.m: “O Blessed One, knower of all events, who sanctify your seat, / O divine sage fond of disputes, what took place there among the celestials?

3.10.s:
surāṇāmasurāṇāṃ vā vijayaḥ samajāyata /
kiṃ vāpyamṛtavṛttāntaṃ viṣṇunā vāpi kiṃ kṛtam //
3.10.d:
सुराणामसुराणां वा विजयः समजायत ।
किं वाप्यमृतवृत्तान्तं विष्णुना वापि किं कृतम् ॥
3.10.m: Did victory fall to the gods or to the asuras? / What became of the nectar, or what was done by Viṣṇu?”

3.10.s:
iti pṛṣṭo maheśena nārado munisattamaḥ /
uvāca vismayāviṣṭaḥ prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ //
3.10.d:
इति पृष्टो महेशेन नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ।
उवाच विस्मयाविष्टः प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणः ॥
3.10.m: Thus questioned by Maheśa, Nārada, the best of sages, / filled with wonder, his face and eyes serene, replied:

3.10.s:
sarvaṃ jānāsi bhagavansarvajño 'si yatastataḥ /
tathāpi paripṛṣṭena mayā tadvakṣyate 'dhunā //
3.10.d:
सर्वं जानासि भगवन्सर्वज्ञो ऽसि यतस्ततः ।
तथापि परिपृष्टेन मया तद्वक्ष्यते ऽधुना ॥
3.10.m: “You know everything, O Blessed One, since you are omniscient; / nevertheless, since I am asked, I shall now tell it.

3.10.s:
tādṛśe samare ghore sati daityadivaukasām /
ādinārāyamaḥ śrīmānmohinīrūpamādadhe //
3.10.d:
तादृशे समरे घोरे सति दैत्यदिवौकसाम् ।
आदिनारायमः श्रीमान्मोहिनीरूपमादधे ॥
3.10.m: While such a dreadful battle between the daityas and the celestials was underway, / the glorious Ādinārāyaṇa assumed the form of Mohinī.

3.10.s:
tāmudāravibhūṣāḍhyāṃ mūrtāṃ śṛṅgāradevatām /
surāsurāḥ samālokya viratāḥ samarodhyamāt //
3.10.d:
तामुदारविभूषाढ्यां मूर्तां शृङ्गारदेवताम् ।
सुरासुराः समालोक्य विरताः समरोध्यमात् ॥
3.10.m: Beholding her, rich in magnificent ornaments, the deity of erotic love incarnate, / the gods and asuras desisted from their efforts in battle.

3.10.s:
tanmāyāmohitā daityāḥ sudhāpātraṃ ca yācitāḥ /
kṛtvā tāmeva madhyasthāmarpayāmāsurañjasā //
3.10.d:
तन्मायामोहिता दैत्याः सुधापात्रं च याचिताः ।
कृत्वा तामेव मध्यस्थामर्पयामासुरञ्जसा ॥
3.10.m: Bewitched by her māyā, when requested for the vessel of nectar, / making her the mediator, the daityas handed it over directly.

3.10.s:
tadā devī tadādāya mandasmitamanoharā /
devebhya eva pīyūṣamaśeṣaṃ vitatāra sā //
3.10.d:
तदा देवी तदादाय मन्दस्मितमनोहरा ।
देवेभ्य एव पीयूषमशेषं विततार सा ॥
3.10.m: Then, taking it, the goddess, charming with a gentle smile, / distributed the entire nectar only to the gods.

3.10.s:
tirohitāmadṛṣṭvā tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śūnyaṃ ca pātrakam /
jvalanmanyumukhā daityā yuddhāya punarutthitāḥ //
3.10.d:
तिरोहितामदृष्ट्वा तां दृष्ट्वा शून्यं च पात्रकम् ।
ज्वलन्मन्युमुखा दैत्या युद्धाय पुनरुत्थिताः ॥
3.10.m: Not seeing her when she vanished, and seeing the vessel empty, / their faces blazing with fury, the daityas rose again for battle.

3.10.s:
amarairamṛtāsvādādatyulvaṇaparākramaiḥ /
parājitā mahādaityā naṣṭāḥ pātālamabhyayuḥ //
3.10.d:
अमरैरमृतास्वादादत्युल्वणपराक्रमैः ।
पराजिता महादैत्या नष्टाः पातालमभ्ययुः ॥
3.10.m: Defeated by the immortals, who possessed exceedingly fierce prowess from tasting the nectar, / the great daityas perished and fled to Pātāla.”

3.10.s:
imaṃ vṛttāntamākarṇya bhavānīpatikhyayaḥ /
nāradaṃ preṣayitvāśu taduktaṃ satataṃ smaran //
3.10.d:
इमं वृत्तान्तमाकर्ण्य भवानीपतिख्ययः ।
नारदं प्रेषयित्वाशु तदुक्तं सततं स्मरन् ॥
3.10.m: Hearing this report, the husband of Bhavānī, / having quickly dismissed Nārada, constantly remembered what he had said.

3.10.s:
ajñātaḥ pramathaiḥ sarvaiḥ skandanandivināyakaiḥ /
pārvatīsahito viṣṇumājagāma savismayaḥ //
3.10.d:
अज्ञातः प्रमथैः सर्वैः स्कन्दनन्दिविनायकैः ।
पार्वतीसहितो विष्णुमाजगाम सविस्मयः ॥
3.10.m: Unnoticed by all the pramathas, by Skanda, Nandin, and Vināyaka, / together with Pārvatī he went, full of wonder, to Viṣṇu.

3.10.s:
kṣīrodatīragaṃ dṛṣṭvā sastrīkaṃ vṛṣavāhanam /
bhogibhogāsanādviṣṇuḥ samutthāya samāgataḥ //
3.10.d:
क्षीरोदतीरगं दृष्ट्वा सस्त्रीकं वृषवाहनम् ।
भोगिभोगासनाद्विष्णुः समुत्थाय समागतः ॥
3.10.m: Seeing the rider of the bull arrived at the shore of the ocean of milk with his wife, / Viṣṇu rose from his seat upon the serpent’s coils and came forward.

3.10.s:
vāhanādavaruhyeśaḥ pārvatyā sahitaḥ sthitam /
taṃ dṛṣṭvā śīghramāgatya saṃpūjyārghyādito mudā //
3.10.d:
वाहनादवरुह्येशः पार्वत्या सहितः स्थितम् ।
तं दृष्ट्वा शीघ्रमागत्य संपूज्यार्घ्यादितो मुदा ॥
3.10.m: Having descended from his mount, the Lord stood with Pārvatī; / seeing him, [Acyuta] quickly approached and worshipped him joyfully with water offerings and the rest.

3.10.s:
sasnehaṃ gāḍhamāliṅgya bhavānīpatimacyutaḥ /
tadāgamanakāryaṃ ca pṛṣṭavānviṣṭaraśravāḥ //
3.10.d:
सस्नेहं गाढमालिङ्ग्य भवानीपतिमच्युतः ।
तदागमनकार्यं च पृष्टवान्विष्टरश्रवाः ॥
3.10.m: Acyuta, the one with lotus-grass ears, having embraced the husband of Bhavānī tightly and affectionately, / asked the purpose of his coming.

3.10.s:
tamuvāca mahādevo bhagavanpuruṣottama /
mahāyogeśvara śrīmansarvasaubhāgyasundaram //
3.10.d:
तमुवाच महादेवो भगवन्पुरुषोत्तम ।
महायोगेश्वर श्रीमन्सर्वसौभाग्यसुन्दरम् ॥
