3.10.m: Mahādeva said to him: “O Blessed One, Supreme Person, / O glorious lord of great yoga, beautiful with all auspiciousness,

3.10.s:
sarvasaṃmohajanakamavāṅmanasagocaram /
yadrūpaṃ bhavatopāttaṃ tanmahyaṃ saṃpradarśaya //
3.10.d:
सर्वसंमोहजनकमवाङ्मनसगोचरम् ।
यद्रूपं भवतोपात्तं तन्मह्यं संप्रदर्शय ॥
3.10.m: that form which was assumed by you, causing infatuation in everyone / and beyond the reach of speech and mind—display that to me!

3.10.s:
draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpaṃ śṛṅgārasyādhidaivatam /
avaśyaṃ darśanīyaṃ me tvaṃ hi prārthitakāmadhṛk //
3.10.d:
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपं शृङ्गारस्याधिदैवतम् ।
अवश्यं दर्शनीयं मे त्वं हि प्रार्थितकामधृक् ॥
3.10.m: I desire to see your form, the presiding deity of erotic love; / it must certainly be shown to me, for you fulfil what is requested.”

3.10.s:
iti saṃprārthitaḥ śaśvanmahādevena tena saḥ /
yaddhyānavaibhavāllabdhaṃ rūpamadvaitamadbhutam //
3.10.d:
इति संप्रार्थितः शश्वन्महादेवेन तेन सः ।
यद्ध्यानवैभवाल्लब्धं रूपमद्वैतमद्भुतम् ॥
3.10.m: Thus requested repeatedly by that Mahādeva, / that wondrous, peerless form obtained through the power of meditation—

3.10.s:
tadevānanyamanasā dhyātvā kiñcidvihasya saḥ /
tathāstviti tiro 'dhatta mahāyogeśvaro hariḥ //
3.10.d:
तदेवानन्यमनसा ध्यात्वा किञ्चिद्विहस्य सः ।
तथास्त्विति तिरो ऽधत्त महायोगेश्वरो हरिः ॥
3.10.m: meditating on that very [form] with a single-pointed mind, smiling slightly, / saying ‘So be it,’ Hari, the lord of great yoga, vanished.

3.10.s:
śarvo 'pi sarvataścakṣurmuhurvyāpārayankvacit /
adṛṣṭapūrvamārāmamabhirāmaṃ vyalokayat //
3.10.d:
शर्वो ऽपि सर्वतश्चक्षुर्मुहुर्व्यापारयन्क्वचित् ।
अदृष्टपूर्वमाराममभिरामं व्यलोकयत् ॥
3.10.m: Śarva too, casting his eyes all around repeatedly, / looked upon a delightful pleasure garden never seen before,

3.10.s:
vikasatkusumaśreṇīvinodimadhupālikam /
caṃpakastabakāmodasurabhīkṛtadiktaṭam //
3.10.d:
विकसत्कुसुमश्रेणीविनोदिमधुपालिकम् ।
चंपकस्तबकामोदसुरभीकृतदिक्तटम् ॥
3.10.m: delighting rows of honeybees with clusters of blossoming flowers, / its horizons perfumed with the fragrance of campaka bouquets,

3.10.s:
mākandavṛndamādhvīkamādyadullolakokilam /
aśokamaṇḍalīkāṇḍasatāṇḍavaśikhaṇḍikam //
3.10.d:
माकन्दवृन्दमाध्वीकमाद्यदुल्लोलकोकिलम् ।
अशोकमण्डलीकाण्डसताण्डवशिखण्डिकम् ॥
3.10.m: where excited cuckoos were intoxicated by the honey of mango groves, / where peacocks performed joyful tāṇḍava dances in bower-like clusters of aśoka trees,

3.10.s:
bhṛṅgālinavajhaṅkārajitavallakinisvanam /
pāṭalodārasaurabhyapāṭalīkusumojjvalam //
3.10.d:
भृङ्गालिनवझङ्कारजितवल्लकिनिस्वनम् ।
पाटलोदारसौरभ्यपाटलीकुसुमोज्ज्वलम् ॥
3.10.m: surpassing the sound of the lute with the fresh humming of swarms of bees, / radiant with trumpet-flower blossoms of noble pink fragrance,

3.10.s:
tamālatālahintālakṛtamālāvilāsitam /
paryantadīrghikādīrghapaṅkajaśrīpariṣkṛtam //
3.10.d:
तमालतालहिन्तालकृतमालाविलासितम् ।
पर्यन्तदीर्घिकादीर्घपङ्कजश्रीपरिष्कृतम् ॥
3.10.m: graced with tamāla, tāla, hintāla, and kṛtamāla trees, / adorned with the beauty of long lotuses in surrounding ponds.

3.10.s:
vātapātacalaccārupallavotphullapuṣpakam /
santānaprasavāmodasantānādhikavāsitam //
3.10.d:
वातपातचलच्चारुपल्लवोत्फुल्लपुष्पकम् ।
सन्तानप्रसवामोदसन्तानाधिकवासितम् ॥
3.10.m: with blossoming flowers and lovely sprouts moving in the wind's rush, / scented profusely with the fragrant flow of Santāna blossoms.

3.10.s:
tatra sarvatra puṣpāḍhye sarvalokamanohare /
pārijātatarormūle kāntā kācidadṛśyata //
3.10.d:
तत्र सर्वत्र पुष्पाढ्ये सर्वलोकमनोहरे ।
पारिजाततरोर्मूले कान्ता काचिददृश्यत ॥
3.10.m: There, rich in flowers everywhere and captivating to all worlds, / a certain lovely woman was seen at the foot of a pārijāta tree.

3.10.s:
bālārkapāṭalākārā navayauvanadarpitā /
ākṛṣṭapadmarāgābhā caraṇābjanakhacchadā //
3.10.d:
बालार्कपाटलाकारा नवयौवनदर्पिता ।
आकृष्टपद्मरागाभा चरणाब्जनखच्छदा ॥
3.10.m: Reddish like the morning sun, proud in her fresh youth, / having the luster of extracted rubies on the coverings of her lotus-feet's nails,

3.10.s:
yāvakaśrīvinikṣepapādalauhityavāhinī /
kalaniḥsvanamañjīrapadapadmamanoharā //
3.10.d:
यावकश्रीविनिक्षेपपादलौहित्यवाहिनी ।
कलनिःस्वनमञ्जीरपदपद्ममनोहरा ॥
3.10.m: bearing the redness of feet imbued with the beauty of red lac, / captivating with her lotus feet adorned with softly tinkling anklets,

3.10.s:
anaṅgavīratūṇīradarponmadanajaṅghikā /
kariśuṇḍākadalikākāntitulyoruśobhinī //
3.10.d:
अनङ्गवीरतूणीरदर्पोन्मदनजङ्घिका ।
करिशुण्डाकदलिकाकान्तितुल्योरुशोभिनी ॥
3.10.m: with shanks that maddened the pride of the quiver of the hero Love, / splendid with thighs matching the charm of an elephant's trunk and a banana tree,

3.10.s:
aruṇena dukūlena susparśena tanīyasā /
alaṅkṛtanitaṃbāḍhyā jaghanābhogabhāsurā //
3.10.d:
अरुणेन दुकूलेन सुस्पर्शेन तनीयसा ।
अलङ्कृतनितंबाढ्या जघनाभोगभासुरा ॥
3.10.m: rich in large hips adorned with an extremely fine red silk garment pleasing to the touch, / radiant with the broad expanse of her buttocks,

3.10.s:
navamāṇikyasannaddhahemakāñjīvirājitā /
natanābhimahāvarttatrivalyūrmiprabhājharā //
3.10.d:
नवमाणिक्यसन्नद्धहेमकाञ्जीविराजिता ।
नतनाभिमहावर्त्तत्रिवल्यूर्मिप्रभाझरा ॥
3.10.m: shining with a golden girdle fastened with fresh rubies, / with a flow of brilliance from the three folds [above] her deep, great whirlpool-like navel,

3.10.s:
stanakuḍmalahindolamuktādāmaśatāvṛtā /
atipīvaravakṣojabhārabhaṅguramadhyabhūḥ //
3.10.d:
स्तनकुड्मलहिन्दोलमुक्तादामशतावृता ।
अतिपीवरवक्षोजभारभङ्गुरमध्यभूः ॥
3.10.m: covered with hundreds of pearl strings swinging upon the buds of her breasts, / her middle region bending under the weight of her exceedingly plump breasts,

3.10.s:
śirīṣakomalabhujā kaṅkaṇāṅgadaśālinī /
sormikāṃ gulimanmṛṣṭaśaṅkhasundarakandharā //
3.10.d:
शिरीषकोमलभुजा कङ्कणाङ्गदशालिनी ।
सोर्मिकां गुलिमन्मृष्टशङ्खसुन्दरकन्धरा ॥
3.10.m: with arms tender as the śirīṣa flower, adorned with bracelets and armlets, / with rings on her fingers, and a neck lovely like a well-polished conch,

3.10.s:
mukhadarpaṇavṛttābhacubukāpāṭalāgharā /
śucibhiḥ paṅktibhiḥ śuddhairvidyārūpairvibhāsvaraiḥ //
3.10.d:
मुखदर्पणवृत्ताभचुबुकापाटलाघरा ।
शुचिभिः पङ्क्तिभिः शुद्धैर्विद्यारूपैर्विभास्वरैः ॥
3.10.m: with a chin resembling the roundness of a hand-mirror, with red lower lip, / and with gleaming, pure rows [of teeth] embodying luminous Vidyās,

3.10.s:
kundakuḍmalasacchāyairdantairdarśitacandrikā /
sthūlamauktikasannaddhanāsābharaṇabhāsurā //
3.10.d:
कुन्दकुड्मलसच्छायैर्दन्तैर्दर्शितचन्द्रिका ।
स्थूलमौक्तिकसन्नद्धनासाभरणभासुरा ॥
3.10.m: revealing moonlight by her teeth that shared the beauty of kunda buds, / radiant with a nose ornament set with a large pearl,

3.10.s:
ketakāntarddaladroṇidīrghadīrghavilocanā /
ardhendutulitāphāle samyakkḷptālakacchaṭā //
3.10.d:
केतकान्तर्द्दलद्रोणिदीर्घदीर्घविलोचना ।
अर्धेन्दुतुलिताफाले सम्यक्कॢप्तालकच्छटा ॥
3.10.m: with very long eyes resembling the inside of the spathe of a ketaka petal, / with neatly arranged curls of hair upon a forehead rivaling the half-moon,

3.10.s:
pālīvataṃsamāṇikyakuṇḍalāmaṇḍitaśrutiḥ /
navakarpūrakastūrīrasāmoditavīṭikā //
3.10.d:
पालीवतंसमाणिक्यकुण्डलामण्डितश्रुतिः ।
नवकर्पूरकस्तूरीरसामोदितवीटिका ॥
3.10.m: her ears adorned with ruby ear-ornaments resembling rings, / her betel roll perfumed with fresh camphor and musk essence,

3.10.s:
śaraccaruniśānāthamaṇḍalīmadhurānanā /
sphuratkastūritilakā nīlakuntalasaṃhatiḥ //
3.10.d:
शरच्चरुनिशानाथमण्डलीमधुरानना ।
स्फुरत्कस्तूरितिलका नीलकुन्तलसंहतिः ॥
3.10.m: her face sweet as the disc of the lovely autumn moon, / with a gleaming musk mark on her forehead, and a mass of black hair,

3.10.s: sīmantarekhāvinyastasiṃdūraśreṇibhāsurā //
3.10.d: सीमन्तरेखाविन्यस्तसिंदूरश्रेणिभासुरा ॥
3.10.m: radiant with the line of red vermilion applied along the parting of her hair,

3.10.s:
spharaccandrakalottaṃsamadalolavilocanā /
sarvaśṛṅgāraveṣāḍhyā sarvābharaṇamaṇḍitā //
3.10.d:
स्फरच्चन्द्रकलोत्तंसमदलोलविलोचना ।
सर्वशृङ्गारवेषाढ्या सर्वाभरणमण्डिता ॥
3.10.m: with eyes unsteady with passion and adorned with a gleaming crescent moon, / rich in every erotic adornment, embellished with every ornament.

3.10.s:
tāmimāṃ kandukakrīḍālolāmālolabhūṣaṇām /
dṛṣṭvā kṣipramumāṃ tyaktvā so 'nvadhāvadatheśvaraḥ //
3.10.d:
तामिमां कन्दुकक्रीडालोलामालोलभूषणाम् ।
दृष्ट्वा क्षिप्रमुमां त्यक्त्वा सो ऽन्वधावदथेश्वरः ॥
3.10.m: Seeing her engaged in playing with a ball, her ornaments trembling, / the Lord instantly abandoned Umā and ran after her.

3.10.s:
umāpi taṃ samovekṣya dhāvantaṃ cātmanaḥ priyam /
svātmānaṃ svātmarsondaryaṃ nindantī cātivismitā /
tasthāvavāṅmukhī tūṣṇīṃ lajjāsūyāsamanvitā //
3.10.d:
उमापि तं समोवेक्ष्य धावन्तं चात्मनः प्रियम् ।
स्वात्मानं स्वात्मर्सोन्दर्यं निन्दन्ती चातिविस्मिता ।
तस्थाववाङ्मुखी तूष्णीं लज्जासूयासमन्विता ॥
3.10.m: Umā too, seeing her husband running, / censured herself and her own beauty, exceedingly astonished; / she stood silent with face cast down, filled with shame and indignation.

3.10.s:
gṛhītvā kathamapyenāmāliliga muhurmuhuḥ /
uddhūyoddhūya sāpyevaṃ dhāvati sma sudūrataḥ //
3.10.d:
गृहीत्वा कथमप्येनामालिलिग मुहुर्मुहुः ।
उद्धूयोद्धूय साप्येवं धावति स्म सुदूरतः ॥
3.10.m: Catching her somehow, he embraced her again and again; / shaking him off repeatedly, she ran far away.

3.10.s:
punargṛhītvā tāmīśaḥ kāmaṃ kāmavaśīsṛtaḥ /
āśrliṣṭaṃ cātivegena tadvīryaṃ pracyutaṃ tadā //
3.10.d:
पुनर्गृहीत्वा तामीशः कामं कामवशीसृतः ।
आश्र्लिष्टं चातिवेगेन तद्वीर्यं प्रच्युतं तदा ॥
3.10.m: Subdued by passion, the Lord caught her again at will; / and as she was embraced with great force, his semen fell then.

3.10.s:
tataḥ samutthito devo mahāśāstā mahābalaḥ /
anekakoṭidaityendragarvanirvāpaṇakṣamaḥ //
3.10.d:
ततः समुत्थितो देवो महाशास्ता महाबलः ।
अनेककोटिदैत्येन्द्रगर्वनिर्वापणक्षमः ॥
3.10.m: From that arose the god Mahāśāstā, of great might, / capable of extinguishing the pride of many crores of demon chiefs.

3.10.s:
tadvīryabindusaṃsparśātsā bhūmistatratatra ca /
rajatasvarmavarṇābhūllakṣaṇādvindhyamardana //
3.10.d:
तद्वीर्यबिन्दुसंस्पर्शात्सा भूमिस्तत्रतत्र च ।
रजतस्वर्मवर्णाभूल्लक्षणाद्विन्ध्यमर्दन ॥
3.10.m: From the contact with drops of that semen, that ground here and there / became the color of silver and gold instantly, O crusher of the Vindhya!

3.10.s:
tathaivāntardadhe sāpi devatā viśvamohinī /
nivṛttaḥ sa girīśo 'pi giriṃ gaurīsakho yayau //
3.10.d:
तथैवान्तर्दधे सापि देवता विश्वमोहिनी ।
निवृत्तः स गिरीशो ऽपि गिरिं गौरीसखो ययौ ॥
3.10.m: Just then that goddess who enchants the universe disappeared; / and the Lord of the mountain, having turned back, went to the mountain along with Gaurī.

3.10.s:
athādbhutamidaṃ vakṣye lopāmudrāpate śṛṇu /
yanna kasyacidākhyātaṃ mamaiva tdṛdayesthitam //
3.10.d:
अथाद्भुतमिदं वक्ष्ये लोपामुद्रापते शृणु ।
यन्न कस्यचिदाख्यातं ममैव त्दृदयेस्थितम् ॥
3.10.m: Now I shall tell this wonder, listen, O husband of Lopāmudrā, / which has not been told to anyone, but remained in my very heart.

3.10.s:
purā bhaṇḍāsuro nāma sarvadaityaśikhāmaṇiḥ /
pūrvaṃ devānbahuvidhānyaḥ śāstā svecchayā paṭuḥ //
3.10.d:
पुरा भण्डासुरो नाम सर्वदैत्यशिखामणिः ।
पूर्वं देवान्बहुविधान्यः शास्ता स्वेच्छया पटुः ॥
3.10.m: Long ago, there was an Asura named Bhaṇḍa, the crest-jewel of all Daityas, / who previously ruled skillfully at will over the diverse gods.

3.10.s:
viśukraṃ nāma daiteyaṃ vargasaṃrakṣaṇakṣamam /
śukratulyaṃ vicārajñaṃ dakṣāṃsena sasarja saḥ //
3.10.d:
विशुक्रं नाम दैतेयं वर्गसंरक्षणक्षमम् ।
शुक्रतुल्यं विचारज्ञं दक्षांसेन ससर्ज सः ॥
3.10.m: From his right shoulder he created a Daitya named Viśukra, / capable of protecting his company, equal to Śukra and discerning in judgment.

3.10.s:
vāmāṃsena viṣāṅgaṃ ca sṛṣṭavānduṣṭaśekharam /
dhūminīnāmadheyāṃ ca bhaginīṃ bhaṇḍadānavaḥ //
3.10.d:
वामांसेन विषाङ्गं च सृष्टवान्दुष्टशेखरम् ।
धूमिनीनामधेयां च भगिनीं भण्डदानवः ॥
3.10.m: And from his left shoulder he created Viṣāṅga, the crown of the wicked, / and the Dānava Bhaṇḍa created a sister named Dhūminī.

3.10.s:
bhrātṛbhyāmugravīryābhyāṃ sahito nihatāhitaḥ /
brahmāṇḍaṃ khaṇḍayāmāsa śauryavīryasamucchritaḥ //
3.10.d:
भ्रातृभ्यामुग्रवीर्याभ्यां सहितो निहताहितः ।
ब्रह्माण्डं खण्डयामास शौर्यवीर्यसमुच्छ्रितः ॥
3.10.m: Together with his two brothers of fierce prowess, his enemies slain, / exalted by his heroism and valor, he shattered the cosmic egg.

3.10.s:
brahmaviṣṇumaheśāśca taṃ dṛṣṭvā dīptatejasam /
palāyanaparāḥ sadyaḥ sve sve dhāmni sadāvasan //
3.10.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाश्च तं दृष्ट्वा दीप्ततेजसम् ।
पलायनपराः सद्यः स्वे स्वे धाम्नि सदावसन् ॥
3.10.m: Seeing him blazing with splendor, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa / took to flight and lived constantly, each in his own abode.

3.10.s:
tadānīmeva tadbāhumaṃmarddana vimūrcchitāḥ /
śvasituṃ cāpi paṭavo nābhavannākināṃ gaṇāḥ //
3.10.d:
तदानीमेव तद्बाहुमंमर्द्दन विमूर्च्छिताः ।
श्वसितुं चापि पटवो नाभवन्नाकिनां गणाः ॥
3.10.m: Right then, crushed by his arms and fainting, / the hosts of heaven-dwellers were not even able to breathe.

3.10.s:
kecitpātālagarbheṣu kecidaṃbudhivāriṣu /
keciddigantakoṇeṣu kecitkuñjeṣu bhūbhṛtām //
3.10.d:
केचित्पातालगर्भेषु केचिदंबुधिवारिषु ।
केचिद्दिगन्तकोणेषु केचित्कुञ्जेषु भूभृताम् ॥
3.10.m: Some in the depths of Pātāla, some in the ocean's waters, / some in the corners of the directions, some in the bowers of mountains,

3.10.s:
vilīnā bhṛśavitrastāstyaktadārasutastriyaḥ /
bhraṣṭādhikārā ṛbhavo viceruśchannaveṣakāḥ //
3.10.d:
विलीना भृशवित्रस्तास्त्यक्तदारसुतस्त्रियः ।
भ्रष्टाधिकारा ऋभवो विचेरुश्छन्नवेषकाः ॥
3.10.m: vanished, exceedingly terrified, leaving their wives and sons; / their authorities lost, the gods wandered in disguised forms.

3.10.s:
yakṣānmahoragānsiddhānsādhyānsamaradurmadān /
brahmāṇaṃ padmanābhaṃ ca rudraṃ vajriṇameva ca /
matvā tṛṇāyitānsarvāṃllokānbhaṇḍaḥ śaśāsaha //
3.10.d:
यक्षान्महोरगान्सिद्धान्साध्यान्समरदुर्मदान् ।
ब्रह्माणं पद्मनाभं च रुद्रं वज्रिणमेव च ।
मत्वा तृणायितान्सर्वांल्लोकान्भण्डः शशासह ॥
3.10.m: Considering Yakṣas, great serpents, Siddhas, and Sādhyas arrogant in battle, / Brahmā, the lotus-navelled [Viṣṇu], Rudra, and the wielder of the thunderbolt all as mere blades of grass, Bhaṇḍa ruled the worlds.

3.10.s:
atha bhaṇḍāsuraṃ hantuṃ trailokyaṃ cāpi rakṣitum /
tṛtīyamudabhūdrūpaṃ mahāyāgānalānmune //
3.10.d:
अथ भण्डासुरं हन्तुं त्रैलोक्यं चापि रक्षितुम् ।
तृतीयमुदभूद्रूपं महायागानलान्मुने ॥
3.10.m: Then, O sage, to slay Bhaṇḍāsura and to protect the three worlds, / a third form arose from the fire of the great sacrifice,

3.10.s:
yadrūpaśālinīmāhurlalitā paradevatām /
pāśāṅkuśadhanurvāṇapariṣkṛtacaturbhujām //
3.10.d:
यद्रूपशालिनीमाहुर्ललिता परदेवताम् ।
पाशाङ्कुशधनुर्वाणपरिष्कृतचतुर्भुजाम् ॥
3.10.m: possessing which form they call the supreme deity Lalitā, / her four arms adorned with the noose, the goad, the bow, and arrows.

3.10.s:
sā devī parama śaktiḥ parabrahmasvarūpiṇī /
jaghāna bhaṇḍadaityendraṃ yuddhe yuddhaviśāradā //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne mohinīprādurbhāvamalakāsuravadho nāma daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ
samāptaścopoddhātakhaṇḍaḥ /
3.10.d:
सा देवी परम शक्तिः परब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी ।
जघान भण्डदैत्येन्द्रं युद्धे युद्धविशारदा ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने मोहिनीप्रादुर्भावमलकासुरवधो नाम दशमो ऽध्यायः
समाप्तश्चोपोद्धातखण्डः ।
3.10.m:
She, the goddess, the supreme power whose essence is the supreme Brahman, / skilled in warfare, slew the Daitya king Bhaṇḍa in battle.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled 'The Manifestation of Mohinī and the Slaying of Malakāsura', in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa; / and the Upoddhātakhaṇḍa is complete.

3.11.s:
agastya uvāca
kathaṃ bhaṇḍāsuro jātaḥ kathaṃ vā tripurāṃbikā /
kathaṃ babhañja taṃ saṃkhye tatsarvaṃ vada vistarāt //
3.11.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
कथं भण्डासुरो जातः कथं वा त्रिपुरांबिका ।
कथं बभञ्ज तं संख्ये तत्सर्वं वद विस्तरात् ॥
3.11.m: Agastya said: / How was Bhaṇḍāsura born, or how was the mother Tripurā [born]? / How did she crush him in battle? Tell all that in detail.

3.11.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
purā dākṣāyaṇīṃ tyaktvā pituryajñavināśanam //
3.11.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
पुरा दाक्षायणीं त्यक्त्वा पितुर्यज्ञविनाशनम् ॥
3.11.m: Hayagrīva said: / Long ago, having abandoned Dākṣāyaṇī, which destroyed her father's sacrifice,

3.11.s:
ātmānamātmanā paśyañjñānānandarasātmakaḥ /
upāsyamāno munibhiradvandvaguṇalakṣaṇaḥ //
3.11.d:
आत्मानमात्मना पश्यञ्ज्ञानानन्दरसात्मकः ।
उपास्यमानो मुनिभिरद्वन्द्वगुणलक्षणः ॥
3.11.m: beholding the Self through the Self, whose essence is the nectar of knowledge and bliss, / worshipped by sages, characterized by qualities free from dualities,

3.11.s:
gaṅgākūle himavataḥ paryante praviveśa ha /
sāpi śaṅkaramā rādhya cirakālaṃ manasvinī //
3.11.d:
गङ्गाकूले हिमवतः पर्यन्ते प्रविवेश ह ।
सापि शङ्करमा राध्य चिरकालं मनस्विनी ॥
3.11.m: he entered [the forest] on the bank of the Gaṅgā near the Himavat. / She too, having propitiated Śaṅkara for a long time, high-minded,

3.11.s: yogena svāṃ tanuṃ tyaktvā sutāsīddhimabhūbhṛtaḥ //
3.11.d: योगेन स्वां तनुं त्यक्त्वा सुतासीद्धिमभूभृतः ॥
3.11.m: abandoned her body through yoga and became the daughter of the King of Snows.

3.11.s:
sa śailo nāradācchrutvā rudrāṇīti svakanyākām /
tasya śuśrūṣaṇārthāya sthāpayāmāsa cāntike //
3.11.d:
स शैलो नारदाच्छ्रुत्वा रुद्राणीति स्वकन्याकाम् ।
तस्य शुश्रूषणार्थाय स्थापयामास चान्तिके ॥
3.11.m: Hearing from Nārada that his daughter was Rudrāṇī, / the mountain placed her near him to attend upon him.

3.11.s:
etasminnantare devāstārakeṇa hi pīḍitāḥ /
brahmaṇoktāḥ samāhūya madanaṃ cedamabruvan //
3.11.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवास्तारकेण हि पीडिताः ।
ब्रह्मणोक्ताः समाहूय मदनं चेदमब्रुवन् ॥
3.11.m: Meanwhile, the gods, oppressed indeed by Tāraka, / instructed by Brahmā, summoned Madana and said this:

3.11.s:
sargādau bhagavānbrahma sṛjamāno 'khilāḥ prajāḥ /
na nirvṛtirabhūttasya kadācidapi mānase /
tapaścacāra suciraṃ manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ //
3.11.d:
सर्गादौ भगवान्ब्रह्म सृजमानो ऽखिलाः प्रजाः ।
न निर्वृतिरभूत्तस्य कदाचिदपि मानसे ।
तपश्चचार सुचिरं मनोवाक्कायकर्मभिः ॥
3.11.m: "At the beginning of creation, when the lord Brahmā was creating all creatures, / he found no delight at all in his mind; / he performed severe penance for a very long time through deeds of mind, speech, and body.

3.11.s:
tataḥ prasanno bhagavānsalakṣmīko janārdanaḥ /
vareṇa cchandayāmāsa varadaḥ sarvadehinām //
3.11.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान्सलक्ष्मीको जनार्दनः ।
वरेण च्छन्दयामास वरदः सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥
3.11.m: Then the blessed Janārdana with Lakṣmī, the giver of boons to all embodied beings, / was pleased and offered him a boon according to his wish.

3.11.s:
brahmovāca /
yadi tuṣṭo 'si bhagavannanāyāsena vai jagat /
carācarayutaṃ caitatsṛjāmi tvatprasādataḥ //
3.11.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
यदि तुष्टो ऽसि भगवन्ननायासेन वै जगत् ।
चराचरयुतं चैतत्सृजामि त्वत्प्रसादतः ॥
3.11.m: Brahmā said: / 'If you are pleased, O Lord, by your grace I shall effortlessly create / this world with its moving and unmoving beings.'

3.11.s:
evamukto vidhātrā tu mahāla kṣmīmudaikṣata /
tadā prādurabhūstvaṃ hi jaganmohanarūpadhṛk //
3.11.d:
एवमुक्तो विधात्रा तु महाल क्ष्मीमुदैक्षत ।
तदा प्रादुरभूस्त्वं हि जगन्मोहनरूपधृक् ॥
3.11.m: Addressed thus by the Creator, he looked toward Mahālakṣmī; / then indeed you were manifested, bearing a form that enchants the world.

3.11.s:
tavāyudhārthaṃ dattaṃ ca puṣpabāṇekṣukārmukam /
vijayatvamajeyatvaṃ prādā tpramudito hariḥ //
3.11.d:
तवायुधार्थं दत्तं च पुष्पबाणेक्षुकार्मुकम् ।
विजयत्वमजेयत्वं प्रादा त्प्रमुदितो हरिः ॥
3.11.m: And for your weapons, the arrows of flowers and the sugarcane bow were given; / delighted, Hari bestowed victory and invincibility [upon you].

3.11.s:
asau sṛjati bhūtāni kāraṇena svakarmaṇā /
sākṣibhūtaḥ svajanato bhavānbhajatu nirvṛntim //
3.11.d:
असौ सृजति भूतानि कारणेन स्वकर्मणा ।
साक्षिभूतः स्वजनतो भवान्भजतु निर्वृन्तिम् ॥
3.11.m: "He creates beings through their own past action as the cause; / as a witness among your own people, may you enjoy contentment."

3.11.s:
eṣa dattavaro brahmā tvayi vinyasya tadbharam /
manaso nirvṛtiṃ prāpya vartate 'dyāpi manmatha //
3.11.d:
एष दत्तवरो ब्रह्मा त्वयि विन्यस्य तद्भरम् ।
मनसो निर्वृतिं प्राप्य वर्तते ऽद्यापि मन्मथ ॥
3.11.m: Brahmā, having granted this boon and placed that burden upon you, / has attained peace of mind and remains so even today, O Manmatha.

3.11.s: amoghaṃ balavīryaṃ te na te moghaḥ parākramaḥ //
3.11.d: अमोघं बलवीर्यं ते न ते मोघः पराक्रमः ॥
3.11.m: Unfailing is your strength and power; never in vain is your valor.

3.11.s:
sukumārāṇyamoghāni kusumāstrāṇi te sadā /
brahmadattavaro 'yaṃ hi tārako nāma dānavaḥ //
3.11.d:
सुकुमाराण्यमोघानि कुसुमास्त्राणि ते सदा ।
ब्रह्मदत्तवरो ऽयं हि तारको नाम दानवः ॥
3.11.m: Delicate yet always unfailing are your flower-arrows; / indeed, this Dānava named Tāraka has received a boon from Brahmā.

3.11.s:
bādhate sakalāṃllokānasmānapi viśeṣataḥ /
śivaputrādṛte 'nyatra na bhayaṃ tasya vidyate //
3.11.d:
बाधते सकलांल्लोकानस्मानपि विशेषतः ।
शिवपुत्रादृते ऽन्यत्र न भयं तस्य विद्यते ॥
3.11.m: He torments all the worlds, and us in particular; / except from a son of Śiva, he has no fear from anywhere else.

3.11.s:
tvāṃ vināsminmahākārye na kaścitpravadedapi /
svakarācca bhavetkāryaṃ bhavato nānyataḥ kvacit //
3.11.d:
त्वां विनास्मिन्महाकार्ये न कश्चित्प्रवदेदपि ।
स्वकराच्च भवेत्कार्यं भवतो नान्यतः क्वचित् ॥
3.11.m: Without you, no one could even speak of this great task; / the task must be accomplished by your own hand, not from anywhere else.

3.11.s:
ātmyaikyadhayānanirataḥ śivo gauryā samanvitaḥ /
himācalatale ramye vartate munibhirvṛtaḥ //
3.11.d:
आत्म्यैक्यधयाननिरतः शिवो गौर्या समन्वितः ।
हिमाचलतले रम्ये वर्तते मुनिभिर्वृतः ॥
3.11.m: Intent on meditation on the oneness of the Self, Śiva, accompanied by Gaurī, / stays at the lovely foot of the Himālaya, surrounded by sages.

3.11.s:
taṃ niyojaya gauryāṃ tu janiṣyati ca tatsutaḥ /
īṣatkāryamidaṃ kṛtvā trāyasvāsmānmahābala //
3.11.d:
तं नियोजय गौर्यां तु जनिष्यति च तत्सुतः ।
ईषत्कार्यमिदं कृत्वा त्रायस्वास्मान्महाबल ॥
3.11.m: Direct him toward Gaurī, and his son will be born; / having accomplished this small task, protect us, O one of great strength!

3.11.s:
evamabhyarthito devaiḥ stūyamāno muhurmuhuḥ /
jagāmātmavināśāya yato himavatastaṭam //
3.11.d:
एवमभ्यर्थितो देवैः स्तूयमानो मुहुर्मुहुः ।
जगामात्मविनाशाय यतो हिमवतस्तटम् ॥
3.11.m: Thus entreated by the gods and praised repeatedly, / he went toward the slope of the Himavat for his own destruction.

3.11.s:
kimapyārādhayāntaṃ tu dhyānasaṃmīlitekṣaṇam /
dadarśeśānamāsīnaṃ kusumaṣurudāyudhaḥ //
3.11.d:
किमप्याराधयान्तं तु ध्यानसंमीलितेक्षणम् ।
ददर्शेशानमासीनं कुसुमषुरुदायुधः ॥
3.11.m: He who has flowers as arrows, raising his weapon, saw the Lord seated, / worshipping something indefinable, his eyes closed in meditation.

3.11.s:
etasminnantare tatra himavattanayā śivam /
ārirādhayiṣuścā gādbibhrāṇā rūpamadbhutam //
3.11.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र हिमवत्तनया शिवम् ।
आरिराधयिषुश्चा गाद्बिभ्राणा रूपमद्भुतम् ॥
3.11.m: Meanwhile, the daughter of Himavat came there, / wishing to attend upon Śiva, bearing a wondrous form.

3.11.s:
sametya śambhuṃ girijāṃ gandhapuṣpopahārakaiḥ /
śuśrūṣaṇaparāṃ tatra dadarśātibalaḥ smaraḥ //
3.11.d:
समेत्य शम्भुं गिरिजां गन्धपुष्पोपहारकैः ।
शुश्रूषणपरां तत्र ददर्शातिबलः स्मरः ॥
3.11.m: Smara, possessing immense power, saw Girijā approaching Śambhu, / intent on serving him there with offerings of perfumes and flowers.

3.11.s:
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānānnātidūre 'sya saṃsthitaḥ /
sumanomārgaṇairagryaissa vivyādha maheśvaram //
3.11.d:
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानान्नातिदूरे ऽस्य संस्थितः ।
सुमनोमार्गणैरग्र्यैस्स विव्याध महेश्वरम् ॥
3.11.m: Invisible to all beings, standing not very far from him, / he pierced Maheśvara with excellent flower-arrows.

3.11.s:
vismṛtya sa hi kāryāṇi bāṇaviddho 'ntike sthitām /
gaurīṃ vilokayāmāsa manmathāviṣṭacetanaḥ //
3.11.d:
विस्मृत्य स हि कार्याणि बाणविद्धो ऽन्तिके स्थिताम् ।
गौरीं विलोकयामास मन्मथाविष्टचेतनः ॥
3.11.m: Forgetting his undertakings, pierced by the arrows, his mind overcome by Manmatha, / he looked upon Gaurī standing nearby.

3.11.s:
dhṛtimālaṃbya tu punaḥ kimetaditi cintayan /
dadarśāgre tu sannaddhaṃ manmathaṃ kusumāyudham //
3.11.d:
धृतिमालंब्य तु पुनः किमेतदिति चिन्तयन् ।
ददर्शाग्रे तु सन्नद्धं मन्मथं कुसुमायुधम् ॥
3.11.m: Recovering his composure, however, wondering, "What is this?", / he saw Manmatha in front of him, armed with flower-weapons, ready [for action].

3.11.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā kupitaḥ śūlī trailokyadahanakṣamaḥ /
tārtīyaṃ cakṣurunmīlya dadāha makaradhvajam //
3.11.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा कुपितः शूली त्रैलोक्यदहनक्षमः ।
तार्तीयं चक्षुरुन्मील्य ददाह मकरध्वजम् ॥
3.11.m: Seeing him, the trident-bearer, capable of burning up the three worlds, became enraged; / opening his third eye, he burned Makaradhvaja to ashes.

3.11.s:
śivenaivamavajñātā duḥkhitā śailakanyakā /
anujñayā tataḥ pitrostapaḥ kartumagādvanam //
3.11.d:
शिवेनैवमवज्ञाता दुःखिता शैलकन्यका ।
अनुज्ञया ततः पित्रोस्तपः कर्तुमगाद्वनम् ॥
3.11.m: Slighted thus by Śiva, the grief-stricken daughter of the mountain, / with the permission of her parents, then went to the forest to perform austerities.

3.11.s:
atha tadbhasma saṃvīkṣya citrakarmā gaṇeśvaraḥ /
tadbhasmanā tu puruṣaṃ citrākāraṃ cakāra saḥ //
3.11.d:
अथ तद्भस्म संवीक्ष्य चित्रकर्मा गणेश्वरः ।
तद्भस्मना तु पुरुषं चित्राकारं चकार सः ॥
3.11.m: Then Citrakarmā, a leader of the Gaṇas, seeing those ashes, / fashioned with those ashes a man of wondrous form.

3.11.s:
taṃ vicitratanuṃ rudro dadarśāgre tu pūruṣam /
tatkṣaṇājjāta jīvo 'bhūnmūrtimāniva manmathaḥ /
mahābalo 'titejasvī madhyāhnārkasamaprabhaḥ //
3.11.d:
तं विचित्रतनुं रुद्रो ददर्शाग्रे तु पूरुषम् ।
तत्क्षणाज्जात जीवो ऽभून्मूर्तिमानिव मन्मथः ।
महाबलो ऽतितेजस्वी मध्याह्नार्कसमप्रभः ॥
3.11.m: Rudra saw before him that man of wondrous form; / that very moment he came to life, like Manmatha incarnate, / of great strength, exceedingly radiant, shining like the midday sun.

3.11.s:
taṃ citrakarmā bāhubhyāṃ samāliṅgya mudānvitaḥ /
stuhi vāla mahādevaṃ sa tu sarvārthasiddhidaḥ //
3.11.d:
तं चित्रकर्मा बाहुभ्यां समालिङ्ग्य मुदान्वितः ।
स्तुहि वाल महादेवं स तु सर्वार्थसिद्धिदः ॥
3.11.m: Embracing him with both arms, Citrakarmā, filled with joy, [said:] / "Praise Mahādeva, O boy; he grants the accomplishment of all aims!"

3.11.s:
ityuktvā śatarudrīyamupādiśadameyadhīḥ /
nanāma śataśo rudraṃ śatarudriyamājapan //
3.11.d:
इत्युक्त्वा शतरुद्रीयमुपादिशदमेयधीः ।
ननाम शतशो रुद्रं शतरुद्रियमाजपन् ॥
3.11.m: Having said this, [the leader] of boundless intellect instructed him in the Śatarudrīya; / repeatedly muttering the Śatarudrīya, he bowed hundreds of times to Rudra.

3.11.s:
tataḥ prasanno bhagavānmahādevo vṛṣadhvajaḥ /
vareṇa cchandayāmāsa varaṃ vavre sa bālakaḥ //
3.11.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान्महादेवो वृषध्वजः ।
वरेण च्छन्दयामास वरं वव्रे स बालकः ॥
3.11.m: Then the blessed lord Mahādeva, who has the bull on his banner, became pleased / and offered him a boon; the boy chose a boon:

3.11.s:
pratidvandvibalārthaṃ tu madbalenopayokṣyati /
tadastraśastramukhyāni vṛthā kurvantu no mama //
3.11.d:
प्रतिद्वन्द्विबलार्थं तु मद्बलेनोपयोक्ष्यति ।
तदस्त्रशस्त्रमुख्यानि वृथा कुर्वन्तु नो मम ॥
3.11.m: "Whatever power my opponent employs against my power, / let half of his power, [together with] weapons and missiles, become futile against me!"

3.11.s:
tatheti tatpratiśrutya vicārya kimapi prabhuḥ /
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi rājyamasmai dadau punaḥ //
3.11.d:
तथेति तत्प्रतिश्रुत्य विचार्य किमपि प्रभुः ।
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि राज्यमस्मै ददौ पुनः ॥
3.11.m: "So be it," promised the Lord, and reflecting a moment, / gave him rule over the kingdom for sixty thousand years.

3.11.s:
etaddṛṣṭvā tu caritaṃ dhātā bhaṇḍiti bhaṇḍiti /
yaduvāca tato nāmnā bhaṇḍo lokeṣu kathyate //
3.11.d:
एतद्दृष्ट्वा तु चरितं धाता भण्डिति भण्डिति ।
यदुवाच ततो नाम्ना भण्डो लोकेषु कथ्यते ॥
3.11.m: Seeing this conduct, the Creator exclaimed, "Bhaṇḍ! Bhaṇḍ!"; / therefore, he is called Bhaṇḍa by name among the worlds.

3.11.s:
iti dattvā varaṃ tasmai sarvairmunigaṇairvṛtaḥ /
dattvāstrāṇi ca śastrāṇi tatraivāntaradhācca saḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne bhaṇḍāsuraprādurbhāvo nāmaikādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.11.d:
इति दत्त्वा वरं तस्मै सर्वैर्मुनिगणैर्वृतः ।
दत्त्वास्त्राणि च शस्त्राणि तत्रैवान्तरधाच्च सः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने भण्डासुरप्रादुर्भावो नामैकादशो ऽध्यायः
3.11.m:
Having thus granted him the boon, surrounded by all the hosts of sages, / and having given him divine missiles and weapons, he vanished right there.

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Manifestation of the Asura Bhaṇḍa," in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the venerable Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

3.12.s:
rudrakopānalājjāto yato bhaṇḍo mahābalaḥ /
tasmādraudrasvabhāvo hi dānavaścābhavattataḥ //
3.12.d:
रुद्रकोपानलाज्जातो यतो भण्डो महाबलः ।
तस्माद्रौद्रस्वभावो हि दानवश्चाभवत्ततः ॥
3.12.m: Since the mighty Bhaṇḍa was born from the fire of Rudra's wrath, / he became a Dānava of a fierce nature because of that.

3.12.s:
athāgacchanmahātejāḥ śukro daityapurohitaḥ /
samāyātāśca śataśo daiteyāḥ sumahābalāḥ //
3.12.d:
अथागच्छन्महातेजाः शुक्रो दैत्यपुरोहितः ।
समायाताश्च शतशो दैतेयाः सुमहाबलाः ॥
3.12.m: Then Śukra of great splendor, the priest of the Daityas, arrived, / and hundreds of Daityas of immense strength gathered.

3.12.s:
athāhūya mayaṃ bhaṇḍo daityavaṃśyādiśilpinam /
niyukto bhṛguputreṇa nijagādārthavadvacaḥ //
3.12.d:
अथाहूय मयं भण्डो दैत्यवंश्यादिशिल्पिनम् ।
नियुक्तो भृगुपुत्रेण निजगादार्थवद्वचः ॥
3.12.m: Then, having summoned Maya, the prime architect of the Daitya lineage, / Bhaṇḍa, directed by the son of Bhṛgu, spoke meaningful words:

3.12.s:
yatra sthitvā tu daityendraistrailokyaṃ śāsitaṃ purā /
tadgatvā śoṇitapuraṃ kuruṣva tvaṃ yathāpuram //
3.12.d:
यत्र स्थित्वा तु दैत्येन्द्रैस्त्रैलोक्यं शासितं पुरा ।
तद्गत्वा शोणितपुरं कुरुष्व त्वं यथापुरम् ॥
3.12.m: "Go to Śoṇitapura, where the lords of Daityas ruled the three worlds of old, / and reconstruct it as it was before."

3.12.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ śilpī sa gatvātha puraṃ mahat /
cakre 'marapuraprakhyaṃ manasaivekṣaṇena tu //
3.12.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं शिल्पी स गत्वाथ पुरं महत् ।
चक्रे ऽमरपुरप्रख्यं मनसैवेक्षणेन तु ॥
3.12.m: Hearing that command, the architect went to that great city / and transformed it, like the city of the immortals, merely by the gaze of his mind.

3.12.s:
athābhiṣiktaḥ śukreṇa daiteyaiśca mahābalaiḥ /
śuśabhe parayā lakṣmyā tejasā ca samanvitaḥ //
3.12.d:
अथाभिषिक्तः शुक्रेण दैतेयैश्च महाबलैः ।
शुशभे परया लक्ष्म्या तेजसा च समन्वितः ॥
3.12.m: Then, consecrated by Śukra and the Daiteyas of immense strength, / he shone endowed with supreme splendor and glory.

3.12.s:
hiraṇyāya tu yaddattaṃ kirīṭaṃ brahmaṇā purā /
sajīvamavināśyaṃ ca daityendrairapi bhūṣitam /
dadhau bhṛgusutotsṛṣṭaṃ bhaṇḍo bālārkasannibham //
3.12.d:
हिरण्याय तु यद्दत्तं किरीटं ब्रह्मणा पुरा ।
सजीवमविनाश्यं च दैत्येन्द्रैरपि भूषितम् ।
दधौ भृगुसुतोत्सृष्टं भण्डो बालार्कसन्निभम् ॥
3.12.m: The crown given of old to Hiraṇya[kaśipu] by Brahmā, / living, indestructible, and adorned by the lords of Daityas, / resembling the rising sun, presented by the son of Bhṛgu, Bhaṇḍa put on.

3.12.s:
cāmare candrasaṃkāśe sajīve brahma nirmite /
na rogo na ca duḥkhāni saṃdadhau yanniṣevaṇāt //
3.12.d:
चामरे चन्द्रसंकाशे सजीवे ब्रह्म निर्मिते ।
न रोगो न च दुःखानि संदधौ यन्निषेवणात् ॥
3.12.m: Two chowries resembling the moon, alive, fashioned by Brahmā, / from the fanning of which neither disease nor sorrows arose, he took up.

3.12.s:
tasyātapatraṃ pradadau brahmaṇaiva purā kṛtam /
yasya cchāyāniṣaṇṇāstu bādhyante nāstrakoṭibhiḥ //
3.12.d:
तस्यातपत्रं प्रददौ ब्रह्मणैव पुरा कृतम् ।
यस्य च्छायानिषण्णास्तु बाध्यन्ते नास्त्रकोटिभिः ॥
3.12.m: He gave him a parasol crafted of old by Brahmā himself, / seated under whose shadow one is not afflicted even by tens of millions of weapons.

3.12.s:
dhanuśca vijayaṃ nāma śaṅkhaṃ ca ripughātinam /
anyānyapi mahārhāṇi bhūṣaṇāni pradattavān //
3.12.d:
धनुश्च विजयं नाम शङ्खं च रिपुघातिनम् ।
अन्यान्यपि महार्हाणि भूषणानि प्रदत्तवान् ॥
3.12.m: He gave the bow named Vijaya and the enemy-slaying conch, / and other exceedingly costly ornaments as well.

3.12.s:
tasya siṃhāsanaṃ prādādakṣayyaṃ sūryasannibham /
tataḥ siṃhāsanāsīnaḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ /
babhūvātīva tejasvī ratnamuttejitaṃ yathā //
3.12.d:
तस्य सिंहासनं प्रादादक्षय्यं सूर्यसन्निभम् ।
ततः सिंहासनासीनः सर्वाभरणभूषितः ।
बभूवातीव तेजस्वी रत्नमुत्तेजितं यथा ॥
3.12.m: He gave him an imperishable throne resembling the sun; / then, seated on the throne and adorned with all ornaments, / he became exceedingly radiant, like a polished gem.

3.12.s:
babhūvuratha daiteyāstayāṣṭau tu mahābalāḥ /
indraśatruramitraghno vidyunmālī vibhīṣaṇaḥ /
ugrakarmogradhanvā ca vijayaśruti pāragaḥ //
3.12.d:
बभूवुरथ दैतेयास्तयाष्टौ तु महाबलाः ।
इन्द्रशत्रुरमित्रघ्नो विद्युन्माली विभीषणः ।
उग्रकर्मोग्रधन्वा च विजयश्रुति पारगः ॥
3.12.m: Then there were eight Daiteyas of immense strength born of him: / Indraśatru, Amitraghna, Vidyunmālī, Vibhīṣaṇa, / Ugrakarman, Ugradhanvan, Vijaya, and Śrutipāraga.

3.12.s:
sumohinī kumudinī citrāṅgī suṃdarī tathā /
catasro vanitāstasya babhūvuḥ priyadarśanāḥ //
3.12.d:
सुमोहिनी कुमुदिनी चित्राङ्गी सुंदरी तथा ।
चतस्रो वनितास्तस्य बभूवुः प्रियदर्शनाः ॥
3.12.m: Sumohinī, Kumudinī, Citrāṅgī, and Sundarī— / four lovely women became his wives.

3.12.s:
tamasevanta kālajñā devāḥ sarve savāsavāḥ /
syandanāsturagā nāgāḥ pādātāśca sahasraśaḥ //
3.12.d:
तमसेवन्त कालज्ञा देवाः सर्वे सवासवाः ।
स्यन्दनास्तुरगा नागाः पादाताश्च सहस्रशः ॥
3.12.m: All the gods, along with Vāsava, served him, knowing the right time; / chariots, horses, elephants, and foot-soldiers by the thousands

3.12.s:
saṃbabhūvurmahākāyā mahānto jitakāśinaḥ /
babhūvurdānavāḥ sarve bhṛguputramatānugāḥ //
3.12.d:
संबभूवुर्महाकाया महान्तो जितकाशिनः ।
बभूवुर्दानवाः सर्वे भृगुपुत्रमतानुगाः ॥
3.12.m: appeared, huge of body, formidable, appearing victorious; / all the Dānavas followed the teachings of the son of Bhṛgu.

3.12.s:
arcayanto mahādevamāsthitāḥ śivaśāsane /
babhūvurdānavāstatra putrapautradhanānvitāḥ /
gṛhegṛhe ca yajñāśca saṃbabhūvuḥ samantataḥ //
3.12.d:
अर्चयन्तो महादेवमास्थिताः शिवशासने ।
बभूवुर्दानवास्तत्र पुत्रपौत्रधनान्विताः ।
गृहेगृहे च यज्ञाश्च संबभूवुः समन्ततः ॥
3.12.m: Worshipping Mahādeva, abiding by the command of Śiva, / the Dānavas dwelt there endowed with sons, grandsons, and wealth, / and in house after house sacrifices took place on all sides.

3.12.s:
ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni mīmāṃsānyāyakādayaḥ /
pravartante sma daityānāṃ bhūyaḥ pratigṛhaṃ tadā //
3.12.d:
ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि मीमांसान्यायकादयः ।
प्रवर्तन्ते स्म दैत्यानां भूयः प्रतिगृहं तदा ॥
3.12.m: The Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma verses, as well as Mīmāṃsā, Nyāya, and other [sciences], / flourished repeatedly in every Daitya house at that time.

3.12.s:
yathāśrameṣu mukhyeṣu munīnāṃ ca dvijanmanām /
tathā yajñeṣu daityānāṃ bubhujurhavyabhojinaḥ //
3.12.d:
यथाश्रमेषु मुख्येषु मुनीनां च द्विजन्मनाम् ।
तथा यज्ञेषु दैत्यानां बुभुजुर्हव्यभोजिनः ॥
3.12.m: Just as in the foremost hermitages of sages and twice-born men, / so at the sacrifices of the Daityas the consumers of oblations ate.

3.12.s:
evaṃ kṛtavato 'pyasya bhaṇḍasya jitakāśinaḥ /
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi vyatītāni kṣaṇārdhavat //
3.12.d:
एवं कृतवतो ऽप्यस्य भण्डस्य जितकाशिनः ।
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि व्यतीतानि क्षणार्धवत् ॥
3.12.m: Even as he acted thus, sixty thousand years passed by / for this victorious Bhaṇḍa as if half a moment.

3.12.s:
vardhamānamatho daityaṃ tapasā ca balena ca /
hīyamānabalaṃ cendraṃ saṃprekṣya kamalāpatiḥ //
3.12.d:
वर्धमानमथो दैत्यं तपसा च बलेन च ।
हीयमानबलं चेन्द्रं संप्रेक्ष्य कमलापतिः ॥
3.12.m: Seeing then the Daitya growing through austerity and through strength, / and Indra with dwindling strength, the consort of Kamalā

3.12.s:
sasarja sahasā kāñcinmāyāṃ lokavimohinīm /
tāmuvāca tato māyāṃ devadevo janārdanaḥ //
3.12.d:
ससर्ज सहसा काञ्चिन्मायां लोकविमोहिनीम् ।
तामुवाच ततो मायां देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
3.12.m: suddenly produced a certain Māyā that deludes the worlds. / Then the god of gods, Janārdana, spoke to that Māyā:

3.12.s:
tvaṃ hi sarvāṇi bhūtāni mohayantī nijaujasā /
vicarasva yathākāmaṃ tvāṃ na jñāsyati kaścana //
3.12.d:
त्वं हि सर्वाणि भूतानि मोहयन्ती निजौजसा ।
विचरस्व यथाकामं त्वां न ज्ञास्यति कश्चन ॥
3.12.m: “Deluding all beings with your own splendor, / roam about as you desire; no one will know you.

3.12.s:
tvaṃ tu śīghramito gatvā bhaṇḍaṃ daiteyanāyakam /
mohayitvācireṇaiva viṣayānupabhokṣyase //
3.12.d:
त्वं तु शीघ्रमितो गत्वा भण्डं दैतेयनायकम् ।
मोहयित्वाचिरेणैव विषयानुपभोक्ष्यसे ॥
3.12.m: Go quickly from here to Bhaṇḍa, the leader of the Daiteyas; / having deluded him before long, you shall enjoy worldly pleasures.”

3.12.s:
evaṃ labdhvā varaṃ māyā taṃ praṇamya janārdanam /
yayāce 'psaraso mukhyāḥ sahāyārthaṃ tu kāścana //
3.12.d:
एवं लब्ध्वा वरं माया तं प्रणम्य जनार्दनम् ।
ययाचे ऽप्सरसो मुख्याः सहायार्थं तु काश्चन ॥
3.12.m: Having received this boon and bowed to that Janārdana, / Māyā requested some of the foremost Apsarases for assistance.

3.12.s:
tayā saṃprārthito bhūyaḥ preṣayāmāsa kāścana /
tābhirviśvācimukhyābhiḥ sahitā sā mṛgekṣaṇā /
prayayau mānasasyāgyaṃ taṭamujjvalabhūruham //
3.12.d:
तया संप्रार्थितो भूयः प्रेषयामास काश्चन ।
ताभिर्विश्वाचिमुख्याभिः सहिता सा मृगेक्षणा ।
प्रययौ मानसस्याग्यं तटमुज्ज्वलभूरुहम् ॥
3.12.m: Requested by her, he again sent some. / Accompanied by them, chief among whom was Viśvācī, that doe-eyed one / went to the excellent bank of Mānasa, adorned with brilliant trees.

3.12.s:
yatra krīḍati daityendro nijanārībhiranvitaḥ /
tatra sā mṛgaśāvākṣī mūle caṃpakaśākhinaḥ /
nivāsamakarodramyaṃ gāyantī madhurasvaram //
3.12.d:
यत्र क्रीडति दैत्येन्द्रो निजनारीभिरन्वितः ।
तत्र सा मृगशावाक्षी मूले चंपकशाखिनः ।
निवासमकरोद्रम्यं गायन्ती मधुरस्वरम् ॥
3.12.m: Where the lord of Daityas sports, accompanied by his women, / there that doe-eyed one made a delightful dwelling at the foot of a campaka tree, / singing in a sweet voice.

3.12.s:
athāgatastu daityendro balibhirbhantribhirvṛtaḥ /
śrutvā tu vīṇāninadaṃ dadarśa ca varāṅganām //
3.12.d:
अथागतस्तु दैत्येन्द्रो बलिभिर्भन्त्रिभिर्वृतः ।
श्रुत्वा तु वीणानिनदं ददर्श च वराङ्गनाम् ॥
3.12.m: Then the lord of Daityas arrived, surrounded by strong ministers; / hearing the sound of the vīṇā, he saw the excellent woman.

3.12.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cārusarvāṅgīṃ vidyullekhāmivāparām /
māyāmaye mahāgarte patito madanābhidhe //
3.12.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वाङ्गीं विद्युल्लेखामिवापराम् ।
मायामये महागर्ते पतितो मदनाभिधे ॥
3.12.m: Seeing her, lovely in every limb like a second streak of lightning, / he fell into the great illusion-filled pit named Passion.

3.12.s: athāsya mantriṇo 'bhūvantdṛdaye smaratāpi tāḥ //
3.12.d: अथास्य मन्त्रिणो ऽभूवन्त्दृदये स्मरतापि ताः ॥
3.12.m: Then his ministers also were tormented by love in their hearts.

3.12.s:
tena daiteyanāthena ciraṃ saṃprarthitā satī /
taiśca saṃprarthitāstāśca pratiśūśruvurañjasā //
3.12.d:
तेन दैतेयनाथेन चिरं संप्रर्थिता सती ।
तैश्च संप्रर्थितास्ताश्च प्रतिशूश्रुवुरञ्जसा ॥
3.12.m: Solicited for a long time by that lord of Daiteyas, she, / and those [other women] solicited by those [ministers], quickly consented.

3.12.s:
yāstvalabhyā mahāyajñairaśvamedhādikairapi /
tā labdhvā mohinīmukhyā nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ yayuḥ //
3.12.d:
यास्त्वलभ्या महायज्ञैरश्वमेधादिकैरपि ।
ता लब्ध्वा मोहिनीमुख्या निर्वृतिं परमां ययुः ॥
3.12.m: Having obtained those [women] who were unattainable even through great sacrifices such as the Aśvamedha, / chief among whom was Mohinī, they experienced supreme delight.

3.12.s:
visasmarustadā vedāṃstathā devamumāpatim /
vijahuste tathā yajñakriyāścānyāḥ śubhāvahāḥ //
3.12.d:
विसस्मरुस्तदा वेदांस्तथा देवमुमापतिम् ।
विजहुस्ते तथा यज्ञक्रियाश्चान्याः शुभावहाः ॥
3.12.m: Then they forgot the Vedas, and likewise the god, Umā's consort; / they abandoned sacrificial rites and other auspicious deeds.

3.12.s:
avamānahataścāsītteṣāmapi purohitaḥ /
muhūrttamiva teṣāṃ tu yayāvabdāyutaṃ tadā //
3.12.d:
अवमानहतश्चासीत्तेषामपि पुरोहितः ।
मुहूर्त्तमिव तेषां तु ययावब्दायुतं तदा ॥
3.12.m: Their domestic priest also was struck with disrespect. / To them ten thousand years passed like a single muhūrta.

3.12.s:
mohiteṣvatha daityeṣu sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ /
vimuktopadravā brahmannāmodaṃ paramaṃ yayuḥ //
3.12.d:
मोहितेष्वथ दैत्येषु सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ।
विमुक्तोपद्रवा ब्रह्मन्नामोदं परमं ययुः ॥
3.12.m: When the Daityas were thus deluded, O Brahman, all the gods with Indra, / freed from trouble, experienced supreme joy.

3.12.s:
kadācidatha devendraṃ vīkṣya siṃhāsane sthitam /
sarvadevaiḥ parivṛtaṃ nārado munirāyayau //
3.12.d:
कदाचिदथ देवेन्द्रं वीक्ष्य सिंहासने स्थितम् ।
सर्वदेवैः परिवृतं नारदो मुनिराययौ ॥
3.12.m: Once, seeing the king of the gods seated upon his throne, / surrounded by all the gods, the sage Nārada arrived.

3.12.s:
praṇamya muniśārdūlaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam /
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā deveśo vākyamabravīt //
3.12.d:
प्रणम्य मुनिशार्दूलं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा देवेशो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
3.12.m: Bowing to the tiger among sages, who blazed like fire, / the lord of the gods folded his hands and spoke these words:

3.12.s:
bhagavansarvadharmajña parāparavidāṃ vara /
tatraiva gamanaṃ te syādyaṃ dhanyaṃ kartumicchasi //
3.12.d:
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ परापरविदां वर ।
तत्रैव गमनं ते स्याद्यं धन्यं कर्तुमिच्छसि ॥
3.12.m: “O Blessed One, knower of all duties, best among knowers of the higher and the lower! / Your going can only be to someone whom you wish to make blessed.

3.12.s:
bhaviṣyacchobhanākāraṃ tavāgamanakāraṇam /
tvadvākyāmṛtamākarṇya śravaṇānandanirbharam /
aśeṣaduḥkhānyuttīrya kṛtārthaḥ syāṃ munīśvara //
3.12.d:
भविष्यच्छोभनाकारं तवागमनकारणम् ।
त्वद्वाक्यामृतमाकर्ण्य श्रवणानन्दनिर्भरम् ।
अशेषदुःखान्युत्तीर्य कृतार्थः स्यां मुनीश्वर ॥
3.12.m: The purpose of your arrival must have an auspicious form in the future. / Having heard the nectar of your speech, completely full of joy to the ears, / having crossed over all sorrows, I would be one who has accomplished his goal, O lord of sages!”

3.12.s:
nārada uvāca
atha saṃmohito bhaṇḍo daityendro viṣṇumāyayā /
tayā vimukto lokāṃstrīndahetāgnirivāparaḥ //
3.12.d:
नारद उवाच
अथ संमोहितो भण्डो दैत्येन्द्रो विष्णुमायया ।
तया विमुक्तो लोकांस्त्रीन्दहेताग्निरिवापरः ॥
3.12.m: Nārada said: / “Now Bhaṇḍa, the lord of Daityas, is deluded by Viṣṇu's māyā; / released from it, he would burn the three worlds like a second fire.

3.12.s:
adhikastava tejobhirastrairmāyābalena ca /
tasya tejo 'pahārastu kartavyo 'tibalasya tu //
3.12.d:
अधिकस्तव तेजोभिरस्त्रैर्मायाबलेन च ।
तस्य तेजो ऽपहारस्तु कर्तव्यो ऽतिबलस्य तु ॥
3.12.m: He is superior to you in splendors, weapons, and strength of māyā. / But his splendor must be taken away, exceedingly strong though he is.

3.12.s:
vinārādhanato devyāḥ parāśaktestu vāsava /
aśakyo 'nyena tapasā kalpakoṭiśatairapi //
3.12.d:
विनाराधनतो देव्याः पराशक्तेस्तु वासव ।
अशक्यो ऽन्येन तपसा कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ॥
3.12.m: Without propitiating the Goddess, the Supreme Śakti, O Vāsava, / he cannot be overcome by other austerity, even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.

3.12.s:
puraivodayataḥ śatrorārādhayata bāliśāḥ /
ārādhitā bhagavatī sā vaḥ śreyo vidhāsyati //
3.12.d:
पुरैवोदयतः शत्रोराराधयत बालिशाः ।
आराधिता भगवती सा वः श्रेयो विधास्यति ॥
3.12.m: Even before the enemy rises again, propitiate [her], O foolish ones! / When propitiated, the Goddess will bring about your welfare.”

3.12.s:
evaṃ saṃbodhitastena śakro devagaṇeśvaraḥ /
taṃ muniṃ pūjayāmāsa sarvadevaiḥ samanvitaḥ /
tapase kṛtasannāho yayau haimavataṃ taṭam //
3.12.d:
एवं संबोधितस्तेन शक्रो देवगणेश्वरः ।
तं मुनिं पूजयामास सर्वदेवैः समन्वितः ।
तपसे कृतसन्नाहो ययौ हैमवतं तटम् ॥
3.12.m: Thus addressed by him, Śakra, the lord of the hosts of gods, / worshipped that sage together with all the gods. / Having made preparation for austerity, he went to the slope of the Himālaya.

3.12.s:
tatra bhāgīrathītīre sarvartukusumojjvale /
parāśaktermahāpūjāṃ cakre 'khilasuraiḥ samam /
indraprasthamabhūnnāmrā tadādyakhilasiddhidam //
3.12.d:
तत्र भागीरथीतीरे सर्वर्तुकुसुमोज्ज्वले ।
पराशक्तेर्महापूजां चक्रे ऽखिलसुरैः समम् ।
इन्द्रप्रस्थमभून्नाम्रा तदाद्यखिलसिद्धिदम् ॥
3.12.m: There, on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, radiant with flowers of all seasons, / he performed a great worship of the Supreme Śakti together with all the deities. / Indraprastha was the name [of the place], bestowing all siddhis from that day onward.

3.12.s:
brahmātmajopadiṣṭena kurvatāṃ vidhinā parām /
devyāstu mahatīṃ pūjāṃ japadhyānaratātmanām //
3.12.d:
ब्रह्मात्मजोपदिष्टेन कुर्वतां विधिना पराम् ।
देव्यास्तु महतीं पूजां जपध्यानरतात्मनाम् ॥
3.12.m: As they performed the supreme, great worship of the Goddess / according to the procedure taught by Brahmā's son, their minds devoted to recitation and meditation,

3.12.s:
ugre tapasi saṃsthānāmananyā rpitacetasām /
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśāhāni ca saṃyayuḥ //
3.12.d:
उग्रे तपसि संस्थानामनन्या र्पितचेतसाम् ।
दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशाहानि च संययुः ॥
3.12.m: abiding in severe austerity, their minds fixed on nothing else, / ten thousand years and ten days passed by.

3.12.s:
mohitānatha tāndṛṣṭvā bhṛguputro mahāmatiḥ /
bhaṇḍāsuraṃ samabhyetya nijagāda purohitaḥ //
3.12.d:
मोहितानथ तान्दृष्ट्वा भृगुपुत्रो महामतिः ।
भण्डासुरं समभ्येत्य निजगाद पुरोहितः ॥
3.12.m: Then, seeing them deluded, the wise son of Bhṛgu, / their domestic priest, approached Bhaṇḍāsura and said:

3.12.s:
tvāmevāśritya rācaindra sadā dānavasattamāḥ /
nirbhayāstriṣu lokeṣu carantīcchavihāriṇaḥ //
3.12.d:
त्वामेवाश्रित्य राचैन्द्र सदा दानवसत्तमाः ।
निर्भयास्त्रिषु लोकेषु चरन्तीच्छविहारिणः ॥
3.12.m: “Depending solely on you, O king of kings, the best of Dānavas / always roam fearlessly in the three worlds, sporting as they wish.

3.12.s:
jātimātraṃ hi bhavato hanti sarvānsadā hariḥ /
tenaiva nirmitā māyā yayā saṃmohito bhavān //
3.12.d:
जातिमात्रं हि भवतो हन्ति सर्वान्सदा हरिः ।
तेनैव निर्मिता माया यया संमोहितो भवान् ॥
3.12.m: For Hari is ever the slayer of all who merely belong to your class; / by him alone has been created the māyā by which you have been deluded.

3.12.s:
bhavantaṃ mohitaṃ dṛṣṭvā randhrānveṣaṇa tatparaḥ /
bhavatāṃ vijayārthāya karotīndro mahattapaḥ //
3.12.d:
भवन्तं मोहितं दृष्ट्वा रन्ध्रान्वेषण तत्परः ।
भवतां विजयार्थाय करोतीन्द्रो महत्तपः ॥
3.12.m: Seeing you deluded, Indra, intent on seeking a vulnerability, / is performing great austerity for your defeat.

3.12.s:
yadi tuṣṭā jagaddhātrī tasyaiva vijayo bhavet /
imāṃ māyāmayīṃ tyaktvā mantribhiḥ sahito bhavān /
gatvā haimavataṃ śailaṃ pareṣāṃ vighnamācara //
3.12.d:
यदि तुष्टा जगद्धात्री तस्यैव विजयो भवेत् ।
इमां मायामयीं त्यक्त्वा मन्त्रिभिः सहितो भवान् ।
गत्वा हैमवतं शैलं परेषां विघ्नमाचर ॥
3.12.m: If the supporter of the world is pleased, the victory will be his alone. / Leaving this woman of māyā, together with your ministers / go to the snowy mountain and cause an obstacle to your enemies!”

3.12.s:
evamuktastu guruṇā hitvā paryaṅkamuttamam /
mantrivṛddhānu pāhūya yathāvṛttāntamāha saḥ //
3.12.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु गुरुणा हित्वा पर्यङ्कमुत्तमम् ।
मन्त्रिवृद्धानु पाहूय यथावृत्तान्तमाह सः ॥
3.12.m: Thus addressed by his guru, leaving the excellent couch, / he summoned the elder ministers and related the situation as it had occurred.

3.12.s:
tacchrutvā nṛpatiṃ prāha śrutavarmā vimṛśya ca /
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇāṃ rājyaṃ tava śivārpitam //
3.12.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा नृपतिं प्राह श्रुतवर्मा विमृश्य च ।
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणां राज्यं तव शिवार्पितम् ॥
3.12.m: Hearing that and reflecting, Śrutavarmā spoke to the king: / “Sovereignty for sixty thousand years was granted to you by Śiva.

3.12.s:
tasmādapyadhikaṃ vīra gatamāsīdanekaśaḥ /
aśakyapratikāryo 'yaṃ yaḥ kālaśivacoditaḥ //
3.12.d:
तस्मादप्यधिकं वीर गतमासीदनेकशः ।
अशक्यप्रतिकार्यो ऽयं यः कालशिवचोदितः ॥
3.12.m:
Even more than that has passed many times over, O hero! / This [course of time] set in motion by Śiva is impossible to counteract.

This is impossible to counteract except by worshipping him; / in due time one must experience sorrow or happiness.”

3.12.s:
aśakyapratikāryo 'yaṃ tadabhyarcanato vinā /
kāle tu bhogaḥ karttavyo duḥkhasya ca sukhasya vā //
3.12.d:
अशक्यप्रतिकार्यो ऽयं तदभ्यर्चनतो विना ।
काले तु भोगः कर्त्तव्यो दुःखस्य च सुखस्य वा ॥

3.12.s:
athāha bhīmakarmākhyo nopekṣyo 'riryathābalam /
kriyāvighne kṛte 'smābhirvijayaste bhaviṣyati //
3.12.d:
अथाह भीमकर्माख्यो नोपेक्ष्यो ऽरिर्यथाबलम् ।
क्रियाविघ्ने कृते ऽस्माभिर्विजयस्ते भविष्यति ॥
3.12.m: Then he who was named Bhīmakarmā said: “An enemy must not be disregarded according to one's strength. / When an obstacle to their ritual is caused by us, victory will be yours.

3.12.s:
tava yuddhe mahārāja parārthaṃ balahāriṇī /
dattā vidyā śivenaiva tasmātte vijayaḥ sadā //
3.12.d:
तव युद्धे महाराज परार्थं बलहारिणी ।
दत्ता विद्या शिवेनैव तस्मात्ते विजयः सदा ॥
3.12.m: In battle, O great king, Śiva himself gave you / the spell that takes away the opponent's strength; therefore victory is always yours.”

3.12.s:
anumene ca tadvākyaṃ bhaṇḍo dānavanāyakaḥ /
nirgatya sahasenābhiryayau haimavataṃ taṭam //
3.12.d:
अनुमेने च तद्वाक्यं भण्डो दानवनायकः ।
निर्गत्य सहसेनाभिर्ययौ हैमवतं तटम् ॥
3.12.m: And Bhaṇḍa, the leader of the Dānavas, agreed to his statement. / Setting forth with his armies, he went to the slope of the Himālaya.

3.12.s:
tapovighnakarāndṛṣṭvā dānavāñjagadaṃbikā /
alaṅghyamakarodagre mahāprākāramujjvalam //
3.12.d:
तपोविघ्नकरान्दृष्ट्वा दानवाञ्जगदंबिका ।
अलङ्घ्यमकरोदग्रे महाप्राकारमुज्ज्वलम् ॥
3.12.m: Seeing the Dānavas causing an obstacle to the austerity, the mother of the world / erected in front an insurmountable, brilliant great rampart.

3.12.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavendro 'pi kimetaditi vismitaḥ /
saṃkruddho dānavāstreṇa babhañjātibalena tu //
3.12.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा दानवेन्द्रो ऽपि किमेतदिति विस्मितः ।
संक्रुद्धो दानवास्त्रेण बभञ्जातिबलेन तु ॥
3.12.m: Seeing it, the lord of Dānavas also wondered, “What is this?” / Filled with wrath, he shattered it with a Dānava weapon of immense power.

3.12.s:
punareva tadagre 'bhūdalaṅghyaḥ sarvadānavaiḥ /
vāyavyāstreṇa taṃ dhīro babhañja ca nanāda ca //
3.12.d:
पुनरेव तदग्रे ऽभूदलङ्घ्यः सर्वदानवैः ।
वायव्यास्त्रेण तं धीरो बभञ्ज च ननाद च ॥
3.12.m: Immediately it arose again in front, insurmountable to all Dānavas; / the steadfast one shattered it with the Vāyavya weapon and roared.

3.12.s:
paunaḥ punyena tadbhasma prābhūtpunarupasthitam /
etaddṛṣṭvā tu daityendro viṣaṇmaḥ svapuraṃ yayau //
3.12.d:
पौनः पुन्येन तद्भस्म प्राभूत्पुनरुपस्थितम् ।
एतद्दृष्ट्वा तु दैत्येन्द्रो विषण्मः स्वपुरं ययौ ॥
3.12.m: Repeatedly from that ash it arose and stood again. / Seeing this, the lord of Daityas became dejected and went to his city.

3.12.s:
tāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā jagaddhātrīṃ dṛṣṭvā prākāramujjvalam /
bhayādvivyathire devā vimuktasakalakriyāḥ //
3.12.d:
तां च दृष्ट्वा जगद्धात्रीं दृष्ट्वा प्राकारमुज्ज्वलम् ।
भयाद्विव्यथिरे देवा विमुक्तसकलक्रियाः ॥
3.12.m: And having seen that supporter of the world and seen that brilliant rampart, / the gods were agitated with fear, abandoning all their rituals.

3.12.s:
tānuvāca tataḥ śakro daityendro 'yamihāgataḥ /
aśakyaḥ samare yoddhumasmābhirakhilairapi //
3.12.d:
तानुवाच ततः शक्रो दैत्येन्द्रो ऽयमिहागतः ।
अशक्यः समरे योद्धुमस्माभिरखिलैरपि ॥
3.12.m: Then Śakra said to them: “This lord of Daityas has arrived here; / it is impossible for all of us together to fight him in battle.

3.12.s:
palāyitānāmapi no gatiranyā na kutracit /
kuṇḍaṃ yojanavistāraṃ samyakkṛtvā tu śobhanam //
3.12.d:
पलायितानामपि नो गतिरन्या न कुत्रचित् ।
कुण्डं योजनविस्तारं सम्यक्कृत्वा तु शोभनम् ॥
3.12.m: Even if we flee, there is no other recourse for us anywhere. / Having properly made a splendid sacrificial pit a yojana in extent,”

3.12.s:
mahāyāgavidhānena praṇidhāya hutāśanam /
yajāmaḥ paramāṃ śāktiṃ mahāmāsairvayaṃ surāḥ //
3.12.d:
महायागविधानेन प्रणिधाय हुताशनम् ।
यजामः परमां शाक्तिं महामासैर्वयं सुराः ॥
3.12.m: Establishing the sacrificial fire according to the ordinances of the great sacrifice, / gods, let us worship the supreme Śakti with our great flesh!

3.12.s:
brahmabhūtā bhaviṣyāmo bhokṣyāmo vā triviṣṭapam /
evamuktāstu te sarvedevāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ //
3.12.d:
ब्रह्मभूता भविष्यामो भोक्ष्यामो वा त्रिविष्टपम् ।
एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वेदेवाः सेन्द्रपुरोगमाः ॥
3.12.m: We shall become one with Brahman, or we shall enjoy heaven!' / Thus spoken to, all those gods, led by Indra,

3.12.s:
vidhivajjuhuvurmāṃsānyutkṛtyotkṛtya mantrataḥ /
huteṣu sarvamāṃseṣu pādeṣu ca kareṣu ca //
3.12.d:
विधिवज्जुहुवुर्मांसान्युत्कृत्योत्कृत्य मन्त्रतः ।
हुतेषु सर्वमांसेषु पादेषु च करेषु च ॥
3.12.m: severed and severed their flesh according to the rules and offered it with mantras. / When all the flesh from their feet and their hands had been offered,

3.12.s:
hotumicchatsu deveṣu kalevaramaśeṣataḥ /
prādurbabhūva paramantejaḥ puñjo hyanuttamaḥ //
3.12.d:
होतुमिच्छत्सु देवेषु कलेवरमशेषतः ।
प्रादुर्बभूव परमन्तेजः पुञ्जो ह्यनुत्तमः ॥
3.12.m: and the gods wished to sacrifice their bodies entirely, / there appeared a supreme, unexcelled mass of splendor.

3.12.s:
tanmadhyataḥ samudabhūccakrākāramanuttamam /
tanmadhye tu mahādevīmudayārkasamaprabhām //
3.12.d:
तन्मध्यतः समुदभूच्चक्राकारमनुत्तमम् ।
तन्मध्ये तु महादेवीमुदयार्कसमप्रभाम् ॥
3.12.m: From the midst of it arose an unexcelled [form] shaped like a wheel; / and in the midst of it, [they saw] the Great Goddess, radiant as the rising sun,

3.12.s:
jagadujjīvanakarīṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivātmikām /
saundaryasārasīmāṃ tāmānandarasasāgarām //
3.12.d:
जगदुज्जीवनकरीं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवात्मिकाम् ।
सौन्दर्यसारसीमां तामानन्दरससागराम् ॥
3.12.m: giving life to the world, embodied as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, / the utmost limit of the essence of beauty, an ocean of the nectar of bliss,

3.12.s:
japākusumasaṃkāśāṃ dāḍimīkusumāṃbarām /
sarvābharaṇasaṃyuktāṃ śṛṅgāraikarasālayām //
3.12.d:
जपाकुसुमसंकाशां दाडिमीकुसुमांबराम् ।
सर्वाभरणसंयुक्तां शृङ्गारैकरसालयाम् ॥
3.12.m: resembling a hibiscus flower, robed in pomegranate blossoms, / adorned with all ornaments, the sole abode of the aesthetic sentiment of love,

3.12.s:
kṛpātaraṅgitāpāṅganayanālokakaumudīm /
pāśāṅkuśekṣukodaṇḍapañcabāṇalasatkarām //
3.12.d:
कृपातरङ्गितापाङ्गनयनालोककौमुदीम् ।
पाशाङ्कुशेक्षुकोदण्डपञ्चबाणलसत्कराम् ॥
3.12.m: her gaze like moonlight from eyes whose sidelong glances waved with compassion, / her hands gleaming with a noose, a goad, a sugarcane bow, and five arrows.

3.12.s:
tāṃ vilokya mahādevīṃ devāḥ sarve savāsavāḥ /
praṇemurmuditātmāno bhūyobhūyo 'khilātmikam //
3.12.d:
तां विलोक्य महादेवीं देवाः सर्वे सवासवाः ।
प्रणेमुर्मुदितात्मानो भूयोभूयो ऽखिलात्मिकम् ॥
3.12.m: Beholding that Great Goddess, all the gods along with Indra, / joyful in mind, bowed down again and again to her who is the self of all.

3.12.s:
tayā vilokitāḥ sadyaste sarve vigatajvarāḥ /
saṃpūrṇāṅgā dṛḍhatarā vajradehā mahābalāḥ /
tuṣṭuvuśca mahādevīmaṃbikāmakhilārthadām //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne lalitāprādurbhāvo nāma dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.12.d:
तया विलोकिताः सद्यस्ते सर्वे विगतज्वराः ।
संपूर्णाङ्गा दृढतरा वज्रदेहा महाबलाः ।
तुष्टुवुश्च महादेवीमंबिकामखिलार्थदाम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने ललिताप्रादुर्भावो नाम द्वादशो ऽध्यायः
3.12.m:
Looked upon by her, they all at once became free of distress, / their limbs restored, exceedingly firm, with adamantine bodies and great strength; / and they praised the Great Goddess, the Mother who grants all aims.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, named 'The Manifestation of Lalitā', in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the final part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

3.13.s:
devā ūcuḥ
jaya devi jaganmātarjaya devi parātpare /
jaya kalyāṇanilaye jaya kāmakalātmike //
3.13.d:
देवा ऊचुः
जय देवि जगन्मातर्जय देवि परात्परे ।
जय कल्याणनिलये जय कामकलात्मिके ॥
3.13.m: The gods said: / 'Victory, O Goddess, Mother of the universe! Victory, O Goddess beyond the highest! / Victory, O Abode of Auspiciousness! Victory, O Essence of Kāmakalā!

3.13.s:
jayakāri ca vāmākṣi jaya kāmākṣi sundari /
jayākhilasurārādhye jaya kāmeśi mānade //
3.13.d:
जयकारि च वामाक्षि जय कामाक्षि सुन्दरि ।
जयाखिलसुराराध्ये जय कामेशि मानदे ॥
3.13.m: O bringer of victory, O fair-eyed one! Victory, O Kāmākṣī, O beautiful one! / Victory, O One adored by all gods! Victory, O Kāmeśī, granter of honor!

3.13.s:
jaya brahmamaye devi brahmātmakarasātmike /
jaya nārāyaṇi pare nanditāśeṣaviṣṭape //
3.13.d:
जय ब्रह्ममये देवि ब्रह्मात्मकरसात्मिके ।
जय नारायणि परे नन्दिताशेषविष्टपे ॥
3.13.m: Victory, O Goddess consisting of Brahman, whose nature is the nectar of the self of Brahman! / Victory, O Nārāyaṇī, supreme one, who delight the entire world!

3.13.s:
jaya śrīkaṇṭhadayite jaya śrīlaliteṃbike /
jaya śrīvijaye devi vijaya śrīsamṛddhide //
3.13.d:
जय श्रीकण्ठदयिते जय श्रीललितेंबिके ।
जय श्रीविजये देवि विजय श्रीसमृद्धिदे ॥
3.13.m: Victory, O beloved of Śrīkaṇṭha! Victory, O Śrīlalitā, O Mother! / Victory, O Goddess Śrīvijayā! Triumph, O granter of the prosperity of fortune!

3.13.s:
jātasya jāyamānasya iṣṭāpūrtasya hetave /
namastasyai trijagatāṃ pālayitryai parātpare //
3.13.d:
जातस्य जायमानस्य इष्टापूर्तस्य हेतवे ।
नमस्तस्यै त्रिजगतां पालयित्र्यै परात्परे ॥
3.13.m: To the cause of what has come to be and what is yet to come, of sacrifices and pious deeds, / homage to her, the protectress of the three worlds, higher than the highest!

3.13.s:
kalāmuhūrtakāṣṭhāhar māsartuśaradātmane /
namaḥ sahasraśīrṣāyai sahasramukhalocane //
3.13.d:
कलामुहूर्तकाष्ठाहर् मासर्तुशरदात्मने ।
नमः सहस्रशीर्षायै सहस्रमुखलोचने ॥
3.13.m: To the soul of kalās, muhūrtas, kāṣṭhās, days, months, seasons, and years; / homage to the thousand-headed one, who has a thousand faces and eyes!

3.13.s:
namaḥ sahasrahastābjapādapaṅkajaśobhite /
aṇoraṇutare devi mahato 'pi mahīyasi //
3.13.d:
नमः सहस्रहस्ताब्जपादपङ्कजशोभिते ।
अणोरणुतरे देवि महतो ऽपि महीयसि ॥
3.13.m: Homage to you who are adorned with a thousand lotus hands and lotus feet! / O Goddess subtler than the subtle, and greater even than the great!

3.13.s:
parātparatare mātastejastejīyasāmapi /
atalaṃ tu bhavetpādau vitalaṃ jānunī tava //
3.13.d:
परात्परतरे मातस्तेजस्तेजीयसामपि ।
अतलं तु भवेत्पादौ वितलं जानुनी तव ॥
3.13.m: Higher than the highest, O Mother, light even of the luminous! / Atala would be your feet, and Vitala your knees;

3.13.s:
rasātalaṃ kaṭīdeśaḥ kukṣiste dharaṇī bhavet /
hṛdayaṃ tu bhuvarlokaḥ svaste mukhamudāhṛtam //
3.13.d:
रसातलं कटीदेशः कुक्षिस्ते धरणी भवेत् ।
हृदयं तु भुवर्लोकः स्वस्ते मुखमुदाहृतम् ॥
3.13.m: Rasātala your waist, and the earth your belly; / Bhuvarloka your heart, and heaven is declared your face.

3.13.s:
dṛśaścandrārkadahanā diśaste bāhavoṃbike /
marutastu tavocchvāsā vācaste śrutayo 'khilāḥ //
3.13.d:
दृशश्चन्द्रार्कदहना दिशस्ते बाहवोंबिके ।
मरुतस्तु तवोच्छ्वासा वाचस्ते श्रुतयो ऽखिलाः ॥
3.13.m: The moon, sun, and fire are your eyes; the directions are your arms, O Mother; / the winds are your breaths, and all the Vedas your words.

3.13.s:
krīḍā te lokaracanā sakhā te cinmayaḥ śivaḥ /
āhāraste sadānando vāsaste hṛdaye satām //
3.13.d:
क्रीडा ते लोकरचना सखा ते चिन्मयः शिवः ।
आहारस्ते सदानन्दो वासस्ते हृदये सताम् ॥
3.13.m: The creation of worlds is your play; consciousness itself, Śiva, is your friend; / eternal bliss is your food, and your dwelling is in the hearts of the virtuous.

3.13.s:
dṛśyādṛśya svarūpāṇi rūpāṇi bhuvanāni te /
śiroruhā ghanāste tu tārakāḥ kusumāni te //
3.13.d:
दृश्यादृश्य स्वरूपाणि रूपाणि भुवनानि ते ।
शिरोरुहा घनास्ते तु तारकाः कुसुमानि ते ॥
3.13.m: Visible and invisible in nature, the worlds are your forms; / the clouds are your hair, and the stars are your flowers.

3.13.s:
dharmādyā bāhavaste syuradharmādyāyudhāni te /
yamāśca niyamāścaiva karapādaruhāstathā //
3.13.d:
धर्माद्या बाहवस्ते स्युरधर्माद्यायुधानि ते ।
यमाश्च नियमाश्चैव करपादरुहास्तथा ॥
3.13.m: Dharma and the rest are your arms, and adharma and the rest are your weapons; / and the restraints and observances are the nails of your hands and feet.

3.13.s:
stanau svāhāsvadhākarau lokojjīvanakārakau /
prāṇāyāmastu te nāsā rasanā te sarasvatī //
3.13.d:
स्तनौ स्वाहास्वधाकरौ लोकोज्जीवनकारकौ ।
प्राणायामस्तु ते नासा रसना ते सरस्वती ॥
3.13.m: Your breasts, producing svāhā and svadhā, grant life to the worlds; / breath-control is your nose, and Sarasvatī is your tongue.

3.13.s:
pratyāhārastvidriṃyāṇi dhyānaṃ te dhīstu sattamā /
manaste dhāraṇāśaktirhṛdayaṃ te samādhikaḥ //
3.13.d:
प्रत्याहारस्त्विद्रिंयाणि ध्यानं ते धीस्तु सत्तमा ।
मनस्ते धारणाशक्तिर्हृदयं ते समाधिकः ॥
3.13.m: Sensory withdrawal is your senses; meditation is your intellect, most excellent of states; / the mind is your power of retention, and your heart is deep absorption.

3.13.s:
mahīruhāsteṅgaruhāḥ prabhātaṃ vasanaṃ tava /
bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyacca nityaṃ ca tava vigrahaḥ //
3.13.d:
महीरुहास्तेङ्गरुहाः प्रभातं वसनं तव ।
भूतं भव्यं भविष्यच्च नित्यं च तव विग्रहः ॥
3.13.m: The trees are the hairs of your body; the dawn is your garment; / the past, the present, and the future, as well as the eternal, are your body.

3.13.s:
yajñarūpā jagaddhātrī viśvarūpā ca pāvanī /
ādau yā tu dayābhūtā sasarja nikhilāḥ prajāḥ //
3.13.d:
यज्ञरूपा जगद्धात्री विश्वरूपा च पावनी ।
आदौ या तु दयाभूता ससर्ज निखिलाः प्रजाः ॥
3.13.m: Having the form of sacrifice, the maintainer of the world, all-formed and purifying; / she who in the beginning became compassion and brought forth all creatures;

3.13.s: hṛdayasthāpi lokānāmadṛśyā mohanātmikā //
3.13.d: हृदयस्थापि लोकानामदृश्या मोहनात्मिका ॥
3.13.m: and who, though dwelling in the hearts of creatures, is invisible, consisting of delusion;

3.13.s:
nāmarūpavibhāgaṃ ca yā karoti svalīlayā /
tānyadhiṣṭhāya tiṣṭhantī teṣvasaktārthakāmadā /
namastasyai mahādevyai sarvaśaktyai namonamaḥ //
3.13.d:
नामरूपविभागं च या करोति स्वलीलया ।
तान्यधिष्ठाय तिष्ठन्ती तेष्वसक्तार्थकामदा ।
नमस्तस्यै महादेव्यै सर्वशक्त्यै नमोनमः ॥
3.13.m: she who makes the division of names and forms by her own sport, / presiding over them while remaining unattached to them, granter of desire and wealth— / homage to that Great Goddess, all-powerful, homage, homage!

3.13.s:
yadājñayā pravartante vahnisūryaidumārutāḥ /
pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni tasyai devyai namonamaḥ //
3.13.d:
यदाज्ञया प्रवर्तन्ते वह्निसूर्यैदुमारुताः ।
पृथिव्यादीनि भूतानि तस्यै देव्यै नमोनमः ॥
3.13.m: By whose command fire, sun, moon, and winds go forth, / as well as earth and the other elements—homage, homage to that Goddess!

3.13.s:
yā sasarjādidhātāraṃ sargādāvādibhūridam /
dadhāra svayamevaikā tasyai devyai namonamaḥ //
3.13.d:
या ससर्जादिधातारं सर्गादावादिभूरिदम् ।
दधार स्वयमेवैका तस्यै देव्यै नमोनमः ॥
3.13.m: She who brought forth the primal creator at the beginning of creation, and alone by herself / upheld this vast primal [creation]—homage, homage to that Goddess!

3.13.s:
yathā dhṛtā tu dhariṇī yayākāśamameyayā /
yasyāmudeti savitā tasyai devyai namonamaḥ //
3.13.d:
यथा धृता तु धरिणी ययाकाशममेयया ।
यस्यामुदेति सविता तस्यै देव्यै नमोनमः ॥
3.13.m: By whom, immeasurable, the earth is borne, as well as space, / and in whom the sun rises—homage, homage to that Goddess!

3.13.s:
yatrodeti jagatkṛtsnaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati nirbharam /
yatrāntameti kāle tu tasyai devyai namonamaḥ //
3.13.d:
यत्रोदेति जगत्कृत्स्नं यत्र तिष्ठति निर्भरम् ।
यत्रान्तमेति काले तु तस्यै देव्यै नमोनमः ॥
3.13.m: In whom the whole world arises, in whom it rests completely, / and in whom it comes to an end in time—homage, homage to that Goddess!

3.13.s:
namonamaste rajase bhavāyai namonamaḥ sāttvikasaṃsthitāyai /
namonamaste tamase harāyai namonamo nirguṇataḥ śivāyai //
3.13.d:
नमोनमस्ते रजसे भवायै नमोनमः सात्त्विकसंस्थितायै ।
नमोनमस्ते तमसे हरायै नमोनमो निर्गुणतः शिवायै ॥
3.13.m: Homage, homage to you as rajas, as Bhavā; homage, homage to you abiding as sattva; / homage, homage to you as tamas, as Harā; homage, homage to you as Śivā beyond the guṇas!

3.13.s:
namonamaste jagadekamātre namonamaste jagadekapitre /
namonamaste 'khilarūpatantre namonamaste 'khilayantrarūpe //
3.13.d:
नमोनमस्ते जगदेकमात्रे नमोनमस्ते जगदेकपित्रे ।
नमोनमस्ते ऽखिलरूपतन्त्रे नमोनमस्ते ऽखिलयन्त्ररूपे ॥
3.13.m: Homage, homage to you, the sole mother of the world! Homage, homage to you, the sole father of the world! / Homage, homage to you whose doctrine is all forms! Homage, homage to you whose form is every yantra!

3.13.s:
namonamo lokagurupradhāne namonamaste 'khilavāgvibhūtyai /
namo 'stu lakṣmyai jagadekatuṣṭyai namonamaḥ śāṃbhavi sarvaśaktyai //
3.13.d:
नमोनमो लोकगुरुप्रधाने नमोनमस्ते ऽखिलवाग्विभूत्यै ।
नमो ऽस्तु लक्ष्म्यै जगदेकतुष्ट्यै नमोनमः शांभवि सर्वशक्त्यै ॥
3.13.m: Homage, homage to you, foremost teacher of the world! Homage, homage to you, the splendor of all speech! / Homage be to Lakṣmī, the sole contentment of the world! Homage, homage, O Śāmbhavī, all-powerful one!

3.13.s:
anādimadhyāntamapāñcabhautikaṃ hyavāṅmanogamyamatarkyavaibhavam /
arūpamadvandvamadṛṣṭagocaraṃ prabhāvamagryaṃ kathamaṃba varṇaye //
3.13.d:
अनादिमध्यान्तमपाञ्चभौतिकं ह्यवाङ्मनोगम्यमतर्क्यवैभवम् ।
अरूपमद्वन्द्वमदृष्टगोचरं प्रभावमग्र्यं कथमंब वर्णये ॥
3.13.m: Without beginning, middle, or end, not made of the five elements, / unreachable by speech and mind, of inconceivable majesty, / formless, beyond duality, outside the scope of sight—how, O Mother, can I describe your foremost majesty?

3.13.s:
prasīda viśveśvari viśvavandite prasīda vidyeśvari vedarūpiṇi /
prasīda māyāmayi mantrāvigrahe prasīda sarveśvari sarvarūpiṇi //
3.13.d:
प्रसीद विश्वेश्वरि विश्ववन्दिते प्रसीद विद्येश्वरि वेदरूपिणि ।
प्रसीद मायामयि मन्त्राविग्रहे प्रसीद सर्वेश्वरि सर्वरूपिणि ॥
3.13.m: Be gracious, O Ruler of the Universe, adored by the universe! Be gracious, O Ruler of Wisdom, embodied as the Veda! / Be gracious, O Full of Illusion, whose body is mantra! Be gracious, O Ruler of All, whose form is all!

3.13.s:
iti statvā mahādevīṃ devāḥ sarve savāsavāḥ /
bhūyobhūyo namaskṛtya śaraṇaṃ jagamurañjasā //
3.13.d:
इति स्तत्वा महादेवीं देवाः सर्वे सवासवाः ।
भूयोभूयो नमस्कृत्य शरणं जगमुरञ्जसा ॥
3.13.m: Having thus praised the Great Goddess, all the gods along with Indra, / bowing down again and again, quickly took refuge [in her].

3.13.s:
tataḥ prasannā sā devī praṇataṃ vīkṣya vāsavam /
vareṇa cchandayāmāsa varadākhiladehinām //
3.13.d:
ततः प्रसन्ना सा देवी प्रणतं वीक्ष्य वासवम् ।
वरेण च्छन्दयामास वरदाखिलदेहिनाम् ॥
3.13.m: Then that Goddess, pleased, beholding Indra bowed low, / offered him a boon, she who grants boons to all embodied beings.

3.13.s:
indra uvāca
yadi tuṣṭāsi karyāṇi varaṃ daityendra pīḍitaḥ /
durdharaṃ jīvitaṃ dehi tvāṃ gatāḥ śaraṇārthinaḥ //
3.13.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
यदि तुष्टासि कर्याणि वरं दैत्येन्द्र पीडितः ।
दुर्धरं जीवितं देहि त्वां गताः शरणार्थिनः ॥
3.13.m: Indra said: / 'If you are pleased, grant a boon for our tasks; afflicted by the king of Daityas, / grant us life, which is hard to preserve; we have come seeking refuge in you.'

3.13.s:
śrīdevyuvāca
ahameva vinirjitya bhaṇḍaṃ daityakulodbhavam /
acirāttava dāsyāmi trailokyaṃ sacarācaram //
3.13.d:
श्रीदेव्युवाच
अहमेव विनिर्जित्य भण्डं दैत्यकुलोद्भवम् ।
अचिरात्तव दास्यामि त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
3.13.m: The holy Goddess said: / 'Having myself vanquished Bhaṇḍa, who was born in the Daitya family, / I shall before long give you the three worlds with all that moves and is still.

3.13.s:
nirbhayā muditāḥ santu sarve devagaṇāstathā /
ye stoṣyanti ca māṃ bhaktyā stavenānena mānavāḥ //
3.13.d:
निर्भया मुदिताः सन्तु सर्वे देवगणास्तथा ।
ये स्तोष्यन्ति च मां भक्त्या स्तवेनानेन मानवाः ॥
3.13.m: Let all the hosts of gods be fearless and joyful; / and those men who shall praise me with devotion by this hymn

3.13.s:
bhājanaṃ te bhaviṣyanti dharmaśrīyaśasāṃ sadā /
vidyāvinayasaṃpannā nīrogā dīrghajīvinaḥ //
3.13.d:
भाजनं ते भविष्यन्ति धर्मश्रीयशसां सदा ।
विद्याविनयसंपन्ना नीरोगा दीर्घजीविनः ॥
3.13.m: shall ever become vessels of righteousness, fortune, and renown; / endowed with learning and modesty, free from disease, and long-lived,

3.13.s:
putramitrakala trāḍhyā bhavantu madanugrahāt /
iti labdhavarā devā devendro 'pi mahābalaḥ //
3.13.d:
पुत्रमित्रकल त्राढ्या भवन्तु मदनुग्रहात् ।
इति लब्धवरा देवा देवेन्द्रो ऽपि महाबलः ॥
3.13.m: may they abound in sons, friends, and wives by my grace.' / Having thus obtained their boons, the gods and the mighty Indra [rejoiced].

3.13.s:
āmodaṃ paramaṃ jagmustāṃ vilokya muhurmuhuḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne lalitāstavarājo nāma trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.13.d:
आमोदं परमं जग्मुस्तां विलोक्य मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने ललितास्तवराजो नाम त्रयोदशो ऽध्यायः
3.13.m:
Attained supreme joy, beholding her again and again.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, named 'The King of Hymns to Lalitā', in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the final part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

3.14.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
etasminneva kāle tu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ /
ājagāmātha deveśīṃ draṣṭukāmo maharṣibhiḥ //
3.14.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
आजगामाथ देवेशीं द्रष्टुकामो महर्षिभिः ॥
3.14.m: Hayagrīva said: / At that very time, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / wishing to see the ruler of gods, arrived together with the great sages.

3.14.s:
ājagāma tato viṣṇurārūḍho vinatāsutam /
śivo 'pi vṛṣamārūḍhaḥ samāyāto 'khileśvarīm //
3.14.d:
आजगाम ततो विष्णुरारूढो विनतासुतम् ।
शिवो ऽपि वृषमारूढः समायातो ऽखिलेश्वरीम् ॥
3.14.m: Then Viṣṇu came, mounted upon the son of Vinatā; / Śiva too, mounted upon his bull, approached the sovereign goddess of all.

3.14.s:
devarṣayo nāradādyāḥ samājagmurmaheśvarīm /
āyayustāṃ mahādevīṃ sarve cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ //
3.14.d:
देवर्षयो नारदाद्याः समाजग्मुर्महेश्वरीम् ।
आययुस्तां महादेवीं सर्वे चाप्सरसां गणाः ॥
3.14.m: The divine sages headed by Nārada approached the great goddess; / all the hosts of apsarases came to the great goddess.

3.14.s:
viśvāvasuprabhṛtayo gandharvāścaiva yakṣakāḥ /
brahmaṇātha samādiṣṭo viśvakarmā viśāṃpatiḥ //
3.14.d:
विश्वावसुप्रभृतयो गन्धर्वाश्चैव यक्षकाः ।
ब्रह्मणाथ समादिष्टो विश्वकर्मा विशांपतिः ॥
3.14.m: The gandharvas headed by Viśvavasu, and the yakṣas [came as well]. / Then Viśvakarman, lord of the people, was commanded by Brahmā,

3.14.s:
cakāra nagaraṃ divyaṃ yathāmarapuraṃ tathā /
tato bhagavatī durgā sarvamantrādhidevatā //
3.14.d:
चकार नगरं दिव्यं यथामरपुरं तथा ।
ततो भगवती दुर्गा सर्वमन्त्राधिदेवता ॥
3.14.m: And he made a heavenly city, just like the city of the immortals. / Then the goddess Durgā, presiding deity of all mantras,

3.14.s:
vidyādhidevatā śyāmā samājagmaturaṃbikām /
brāhayādyā mātaraścaiva svasvabhūtagaṇāvṛtāḥ //
3.14.d:
विद्याधिदेवता श्यामा समाजग्मतुरंबिकाम् ।
ब्राहयाद्या मातरश्चैव स्वस्वभूतगणावृताः ॥
3.14.m: And Śyāmā, presiding deity of sacred lore, approached Ambikā, / as well as the mothers headed by Brāhmī, surrounded by their respective hosts of spirits,

3.14.s:
siddhayo hyaṇimādyāśca yoginyaścaiva koṭiśaḥ /
bhairavāḥ kṣetrapālāśca mahāśāstā gaṇāgraṇīḥ //
3.14.d:
सिद्धयो ह्यणिमाद्याश्च योगिन्यश्चैव कोटिशः ।
भैरवाः क्षेत्रपालाश्च महाशास्ता गणाग्रणीः ॥
3.14.m: And the supernatural powers headed by aṇimā, and yoginīs by the millions, / the bhairavas, the protectors of sacred sites, and the great Śāstṛ, leader of the hosts,

3.14.s:
mahāgaṇeśvaraḥ skando baṭuko vīrabhadrakaḥ /
āgatya te mahādevīṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ praṇatāstadā //
3.14.d:
महागणेश्वरः स्कन्दो बटुको वीरभद्रकः ।
आगत्य ते महादेवीं तुष्टुवुः प्रणतास्तदा ॥
3.14.m: Mahāgaṇeśvara, Skanda, Baṭuka, and Vīrabhadra; / having arrived, they bowed low and praised the great goddess.

3.14.s:
tatrātha nagarīṃ ramyāṃ sāṭṭaprākāratoraṇām /
gajāśvarathaśālāḍhyāṃ rājavīthivirājitām //
3.14.d:
तत्राथ नगरीं रम्यां साट्टप्राकारतोरणाम् ।
गजाश्वरथशालाढ्यां राजवीथिविराजिताम् ॥
3.14.m: Then, [beholding] there the lovely city endowed with turrets, ramparts, and arched gateways, / rich in stables for elephants, horses, and chariots, adorned with royal avenues,

3.14.s:
sāmantānāmamātyānāṃ sainikānāṃ dvijanma nām /
vetāladāsadāsīnāṃ gṛhāṇi rucirāṇi ca //
3.14.d:
सामन्तानाममात्यानां सैनिकानां द्विजन्म नाम् ।
वेतालदासदासीनां गृहाणि रुचिराणि च ॥
3.14.m: With charming houses of feudatories, ministers, / soldiers, the twice-born, vetālas, and male and female servants,

3.14.s:
madhyaṃ rājagṛhaṃ divyaṃ dvāragopurabhūṣitam /
śālābhirbahubhiryuktaṃ sabhā bhiruṣaśobhitam //
3.14.d:
मध्यं राजगृहं दिव्यं द्वारगोपुरभूषितम् ।
शालाभिर्बहुभिर्युक्तं सभा भिरुषशोभितम् ॥
3.14.m: With a divine royal palace in the center, adorned with gateways and towers, / furnished with many halls, and graced with assembly halls,

3.14.s:
siṃhāsanasabhāṃ caiva navaratnamayīṃ śubhām /
madhye siṃhāsanaṃ divyaṃ cintāmaṇivīnirmitam //
3.14.d:
सिंहासनसभां चैव नवरत्नमयीं शुभाम् ।
मध्ये सिंहासनं दिव्यं चिन्तामणिवीनिर्मितम् ॥
3.14.m: And an auspicious hall of the throne made of nine kinds of gems, / in the midst of which stood a divine throne fashioned of wishing-jewels,

3.14.s:
svayaṃ prakāśamadvandvamudayādityasaṃnibham /
vilokya cintayāmāsa brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ //
3.14.d:
स्वयं प्रकाशमद्वन्द्वमुदयादित्यसंनिभम् ।
विलोक्य चिन्तयामास ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ॥
3.14.m: Self-luminous, without a peer, resembling the rising sun— / beholding it, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, reflected:

3.14.s:
yastvetatsamadhiṣṭhāya vartate bāliśo 'pivā /
purasyāsya prabhāveṇa sarvalokādhiko bhavet //
3.14.d:
यस्त्वेतत्समधिष्ठाय वर्तते बालिशो ऽपिवा ।
पुरस्यास्य प्रभावेण सर्वलोकाधिको भवेत् ॥
3.14.m: “Whoever resides presiding over this [throne], even if a fool, / would surpass all the worlds by the power of this city.

3.14.s:
na kevalā strī rājyārhā puruṣo 'pi tayā vinā /
maṅgalācāryasaṃyuktaṃ mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam /
anukūlāṅganāyuktamabhiṣiñcediti śrutiḥ //
3.14.d:
न केवला स्त्री राज्यार्हा पुरुषो ऽपि तया विना ।
मङ्गलाचार्यसंयुक्तं महापुरुषलक्षणम् ।
अनुकूलाङ्गनायुक्तमभिषिञ्चेदिति श्रुतिः ॥
3.14.m: A woman alone is not fit to rule, nor is a man without her; / ‘One should consecrate [a ruler] possessing auspicious conduct, endowed with the marks of a great man, / accompanied by a compatible woman,’ so says the Veda.

3.14.s:
vibhātīyaṃ varārohā bhūrtā śṛṅgāradevatā /
varo 'syāstriṣu lokeṣu na cānyaḥ śaṅkarādṛte //
3.14.d:
विभातीयं वरारोहा भूर्ता शृङ्गारदेवता ।
वरो ऽस्यास्त्रिषु लोकेषु न चान्यः शङ्करादृते ॥
3.14.m: This fair-hipped lady shines forth as the embodied deity of erotic sentiment; / yet in the three worlds there is no suitable groom for her except Śaṅkara.

3.14.s:
jaḍilo muṇḍadhārī ca virūpākṣaḥ kapālabhṛt /
kalmāṣī bhasmadigdhāṅgaḥ śmaśānāsthivibhūṣaṇaḥ //
3.14.d:
जडिलो मुण्डधारी च विरूपाक्षः कपालभृत् ।
कल्माषी भस्मदिग्धाङ्गः श्मशानास्थिविभूषणः ॥
3.14.m: Yet he has matted hair, carries a severed head, is Virūpākṣa, and bears a skull, / spotted, his body smeared with ashes, adorned with bones from the cremation ground.

3.14.s:
amaṅgalāspadaṃ cainaṃ varayetsā sumaṅgalā /
iti cintayamānasya brahmaṇo 'gre maheśvaraḥ //
3.14.d:
अमङ्गलास्पदं चैनं वरयेत्सा सुमङ्गला ।
इति चिन्तयमानस्य ब्रह्मणो ऽग्रे महेश्वरः ॥
3.14.m: Will she, who is exceedingly auspicious, choose him who is an abode of inauspiciousness?” / As Brahmā was thinking thus, Maheśvara appeared before him,

3.14.s:
koṭikandarpalāvaṇyayukto divya śarīravān /
divyāṃbaradharaḥ sragvī divyagandhānulepanaḥ //
3.14.d:
कोटिकन्दर्पलावण्ययुक्तो दिव्य शरीरवान् ।
दिव्यांबरधरः स्रग्वी दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनः ॥
3.14.m: Endowed with the beauty of ten million gods of love, possessing a heavenly body, / wearing heavenly garments, bearing garlands, smeared with divine fragrant ointments,

3.14.s:
kirīṭahārakeyūrakuṇḍalādyairalaṅkṛtaḥ /
prādurbabhūva purato jaganmohana rupadhṛk //
3.14.d:
किरीटहारकेयूरकुण्डलाद्यैरलङ्कृतः ।
प्रादुर्बभूव पुरतो जगन्मोहन रुपधृक् ॥
3.14.m: Adorned with a diadem, necklaces, armlets, earrings, and the like; / he manifested before him, bearing a form that enchants the world.

3.14.s:
taṃ kumāramathāliṅgya brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ /
cakre kāmeśvaraṃ nāmnā kamanīyavapurdharam //
3.14.d:
तं कुमारमथालिङ्ग्य ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
चक्रे कामेश्वरं नाम्ना कमनीयवपुर्धरम् ॥
3.14.m: Then Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, embraced that youth / and gave him the name Kāmeśvara, bearer of a desirable body.

3.14.s:
tasyāstu paramāśakteranurūpo varastvayam /
iti niścitya tenaiva sahitāstāmathāyayuḥ //
3.14.d:
तस्यास्तु परमाशक्तेरनुरूपो वरस्त्वयम् ।
इति निश्चित्य तेनैव सहितास्तामथाययुः ॥
3.14.m: “This indeed is the suitable groom for that supreme power,” / having determined thus, accompanied by him, they went to her.

3.14.s:
astuvaṃste parāṃ śaktiṃ brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ /
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ kumāro nīlalohitaḥ /
abhavanmanmathāviṣṭo vismṛtya sakalāḥ kriyāḥ //
3.14.d:
अस्तुवंस्ते परां शक्तिं ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ।
तां दृष्ट्वा मृगशावाक्षीं कुमारो नीललोहितः ।
अभवन्मन्मथाविष्टो विस्मृत्य सकलाः क्रियाः ॥
3.14.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara praised the supreme power. / Seeing that fawn-eyed lady, the youth Nīlalohita / was overcome with love, forgetting all his ritual deeds.

3.14.s:
sāpi taṃ vīkṣya tanvaṅgo mūrtiṃmantamiva smaram /
madanāviṣṭasarvāṅgī svātmarūpamamanyata /
anyonyālokanāsaktau tāvṛbhau madanāturau //
3.14.d:
सापि तं वीक्ष्य तन्वङ्गो मूर्तिंमन्तमिव स्मरम् ।
मदनाविष्टसर्वाङ्गी स्वात्मरूपममन्यत ।
अन्योन्यालोकनासक्तौ तावृभौ मदनातुरौ ॥
3.14.m: She too, seeing that slender-limbed [youth] as if he were love incarnate, / her entire body overwhelmed with love, considered him to be her own self's form; / both of them, intent on gazing at one another, were stricken with love.

3.14.s:
sarvabhāvaviśeṣajñau dhṛtimantau manasvinau /
parairajñātacāritrau muhūrtāsvasthacetanau //
3.14.d:
सर्वभावविशेषज्ञौ धृतिमन्तौ मनस्विनौ ।
परैरज्ञातचारित्रौ मुहूर्तास्वस्थचेतनौ ॥
3.14.m: Knowing the particularities of all emotions, firm-minded, intelligent, / their conduct unknown to others, for a moment their minds were unsettled.

3.14.s:
athovāca mahādevīṃ brahmā lokaikanāyikām /
ime devāśca ṛṣayo gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ /
tvāmīśāṃ draṣṭumicchanti sapriyāṃ paramāhave //
3.14.d:
अथोवाच महादेवीं ब्रह्मा लोकैकनायिकाम् ।
इमे देवाश्च ऋषयो गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ।
त्वामीशां द्रष्टुमिच्छन्ति सप्रियां परमाहवे ॥
3.14.m: Then Brahmā spoke to the great goddess, the sole ruler of the world: / “These gods, sages, and hosts of gandharvas and apsarases / wish to see you, the sovereign lady, united with your beloved in the supreme battle.

3.14.s:
ko vānurūpaste devi priyo dhanyatamaḥ pumān /
lokasaṃrakṣaṇārthāya bhajasva puruṣaṃ param //
3.14.d:
को वानुरूपस्ते देवि प्रियो धन्यतमः पुमान् ।
लोकसंरक्षणार्थाय भजस्व पुरुषं परम् ॥
3.14.m: Or who, O goddess, is the most blessed man suitable to be your beloved? / For the sake of protecting the worlds, betake yourself to a supreme consort.

3.14.s:
rājñī bhava purasyāsya sthitā bhava varāsane /
abhiṣiktāṃ mahābhāgairdevārṣe bhirakalmaṣaiḥ //
3.14.d:
राज्ञी भव पुरस्यास्य स्थिता भव वरासने ।
अभिषिक्तां महाभागैर्देवार्षे भिरकल्मषैः ॥
3.14.m: Become the queen of this city! Be seated upon the excellent throne, / consecrated by the highly fortunate, spotless divine sages.

3.14.s:
sāmrājyacihnasaṃyuktāṃ sarvābharaṇasaṃyutām /
sapriyāmāsanagatāṃ draṣṭumicchāmahe vayam //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne madanakāmeśvaraprādurbhāvo nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.14.d:
साम्राज्यचिह्नसंयुक्तां सर्वाभरणसंयुताम् ।
सप्रियामासनगतां द्रष्टुमिच्छामहे वयम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने मदनकामेश्वरप्रादुर्भावो नाम चतुर्दशो ऽध्यायः
3.14.m:
Endowed with the emblems of empire, adorned with all ornaments, / seated upon the throne with your beloved—we wish to see you [thus].”

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, named “The Manifestation of Madana-Kāmeśvara,” in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
